  array leaf, read at `base + lin(lo0 + I·st0, lo1 + J·st1, X0)` with IX 1 and IX 2 in the leaf
  phase; an `idx` with an index vector (kind V) read through the vector's element (an indexed load;
  its `chkb` loop in the leaf phase, so it stays where L5 has it); a mask selection (M or MM) only as
  the operand of F3 or as an operand of a tree all of whose array leaves are selections with the
  same mask local (`Tn[colorIn] - Tc[colorIn]` iterates the mask once). **Concatenation parts**: in
  L9 (c)'s copy pass, a part that is a range or `:` selection or a view of an array is copied from
  its base by its index map instead of being materialized first (its IX 1 and IX 2 at the part's
  place in the part order), which `seafuse` writes as L9 (c) with that part's loop reading the base
  (L-eu). This holds for every row of a stack, and for rows of matrices and scalars and rows of
  scalars and vectors alike (decided by the user 2026-10-30, L-fy): a scalar part is written as one
  element store at its place; a vector part of a row of scalars and vectors is copied as a 1 × n
  block. A part folds when it is a view (`.T`, `.flat` of a matrix, `.col`, `.row` of a vector) of
  an operand that is not a view, or a selection of an array that is not a view whose every index is
  a range or `:`; a selection with a scalar index (`A[1, :]`), a view of a selection (`v[0..4].row`:
  the view folds, the selection is materialized) or a selection of a view (`B.T[1..3, :]`) is not a
  folded part. A vector concatenation folds its `v[:]` and `A.flat` parts too. One folded part
  makes the whole concatenation `seafuse`'s; a concatenation with none stays with `sealoop`'s L9.

* **F5 (elemental applications)**. L19 (in `seafuse`, §2.12.3) rewrites every `emap`; an `emap`
  inside an element-wise tree or an F2 group is a fusible k-result node: its arguments are leaves or
  subtrees of the tree, its checks are L19's (2) at its node, and its element is the per-element
  `call` of L19 (4) (inlined by `sealoop`'s L20), whose kept results are scalar `.l` locals of the
  body; a result nothing reads is discarded (L19 (3)).

**Readings fixed by 7c** (the forms F1–F5 leave open, as built and as T2's goldens write them; lead
decisions L-fz–L-gg, §9). Normative with the rules above:

1. *Positions* (L-fz): every node a rewrite writes takes P, the position of the rewritten
   statement (the ancestor whose parent is a block, so a call written as a statement is the
   statement; for a group S1's), except: a `chk` or `chkb` takes the position of the node whose
   check it is (the tree node, the `idx` of a folded selection, the `asg` of a target's own checks,
   the `lib` of `EMPTY_REDUCE`); an `rcnt` its `rng`'s; F1's RES `anew` the root's; a stored group
   local's `anew` its statement's; F5's per-element `call` the `emap`'s; a concatenation written as
   L9 (c) the `arr`'s; a reduction's final its statement's.
2. *Order of a leaf and check phase* (L-fz): at each node its operands left to right, a leaf as
   `tmp Lk`, an inner node recursively; then every array operand's extents of the node, all loaded
   before its checks; then its L7 (2) checks. `tmp V = ci SEA_SHAPE_VEC` is written once per
   rewrite at its first vector check and `tmp O = ci 1` once at its first use. A folded range or
   mask selection's kept extent (IX 3) is written where its node loads its operands' extents; its
   IX 1 and IX 2 are the leaf's evaluation. Each extent of a folded `.col` is a `tmp` loaded at its
   node (`ext(B, 0)`, `ci 1`; `.row`: `ci 1`, `ext(B, 0)`), its `tmp Lk` being its base.
3. *Which trees* (L-gb): a bare leaf (a whole-array `lv`, a folded selection or view alone) is no
   element-wise tree: F1 and F3 need at least one fusible node (F2 (1) lists a folded selection or
   view separately); `ind2sub` with a scalar `r` is no fusible node (L11's form). With a single
   dynamic array leaf in a matrix space the test Pl and the broadcast copy are kept as F1 (4)
   writes them, though Pl always holds (L-ga). A fixed-size root's static extents are `ci` `tmp`s
   at P; a fixed-size value stored in place takes the extents of its first array leaf (a fixed
   vector its static n) (L-ga).
4. *Stores in place* (L-gc): a whole-array target by F2 (6) (a single statement is the `block P n`
   of its leaf and check phase, the prologue `tmp X = ext(V, d)`, `tmp E = bin eq (lv X) (lv N)` per
   dimension folded by `bin band`, the data loads and the nest; O always bound, `data(O)` loaded in
   leaf order in place of the leaf's own data only where the tree reads V); a fixed-size whole
   target has no prologue and no O and is written in its home. A selection target (kinds S, R, A,
   M, MM): L6 steps 2–5 after the value's leaf and check phase, the value's extent being the
   space's; step 6 loads `data(T)`, then the leaves' data in leaf order, then `bind O = ci 0`, `tmp
   One = ci 1`; step 7's nest computes the element at the value index O; the target's index records
   are copied, a `$` that the target's `idx` claims written as L6 and IX 1 write it (`lv` of the
   base at the `idx`'s position, `ext` at the `$`'s); in a dynamic matrix's broadcast copy O and One
   stand before the test, the plain arm reads at the linear O and the broadcast arm reads each leaf
   at `K·SI + L·SJ`, K the value's row counter (`K += One` per stored element, reset after the inner
   loop) and L its column counter (`bind L = 0`, `L += One` after the inner loop).
5. *Groups* (L-gd): the space test compares S2 … Sn with S1 (`bin eq` of Si's extent and S1's,
   rows then columns for a matrix space, folded by `bin band`); a read of a local bound by an
   earlier group statement is no leaf (its extents are that statement's root extents, its element
   that statement's Ei). The fused nest loads first the data of every stored local and target in
   statement order, then of every array leaf in leaf order; a matrix group's fused arm holds the
   test Pl with the plain and broadcast copies over all the group's array leaves (reads of
   group-bound locals excluded). The split copy runs each statement's own F1 (4) nest, loading its
   own data (its result, then its leaves), a read of a group-bound local being a whole-array leaf of
   the earlier statement's split array and an unstored local stored into a `tmp` of a new array in
   the split copy's block (R11); a masked reduction's split nest runs over its mask's base positions
   with a counter J of the selected elements.
6. *A `tbind` in a group* (L-ge): a k ≥ 2 `emap` is fusible only as the direct value of a `tbind`
   (not under `eval`, `tasg`, `tret` or a `seq`), with every component an array of `bool`, `i64` or
   `f64`; its arguments are leaves of its tree (a subtree argument is fused as its own tree into
   RES and read as a whole-array leaf); a `tbind` outside a group stays with L19. In the fused nest
   the `tbind` of `.l` locals opens a `block` holding the rest of the element body (R8), each kept
   (named) component's element store following it in that block; in the split copy the statement
   is L19's block form, with an array for each kept component; a kept component is stored before
   the group only when read after it. A group's `tbind` components total at most 499; a `tbind`
   past that is not groupable.
7. *Reductions* (L-gf): **masked** (not `sum`): `bind Q = ci 0` and `tmp One = ci 1` after the data
   loads, the nest loop(X; K) over the base with `if` of the mask element, Q replacing K in L13's
   body and `Q += lv One` the last statement of the `if`'s block; the mask's data is loaded again
   for the nest after the base's. **Masked `sum`**: sum8's H, A, M and lane stores, the data loads,
   `bind Qc = ci 0`, `tmp One = ci 1`, `tmp Q = ci 7`, then loop(X; K) { `if` (mask element at K) {
   W = Qc & Q; G; Y; `asg` G; `est`; Qc += One } } in place of sum8's direct `hloop` (the lane is
   the selected count, L-et). **`.flat`**: fused with a single array leaf only, one loop over N = R·C
   at the linear position K, N's `tmp` after the leaf and check phase; in a group its space is a
   vector of R·C. **In a group**: only over a space of the group's rank; its accumulators stand in
   the enclosing block after the stored locals, its steps follow the stores in the nest, its final
   is bound after the group's block (`sum`: `tmp Z`, `bind s = ifx(N > 0, xblk{…}, cf 0)`; `max`:
   `bind s = lv R`); a masked reduction's count and `EMPTY_REDUCE` stand in (a), its mask extent in
   the space test. **`variance`/`std` of `i64`**: their deviations are `f64`, so they use F8; the
   mean is the checked `i64` sum converted. In a same-mask tree (`A[m] - B[m]`) the mask's data is
   loaded once, with its first leaf.
8. *F5 with k = 1* (L-gg): the per-element `call` stands in the element expression in place of the
   `emap` (no `.l` local is bound for its one result).

**Example** (W1's bisection body, `ports/w1_shaft_design.sea` lines 259–265, LANGUAGE.md §2.1; the
lines moved from 251–257 at 9d, when the port's header grew, L-md).
`mid`, the `tbind` of `shaft_safety(mid, MG, TG, pGrid)`, `up`, `lo = where(up, mid, lo)` and `hi =
where(up, hi, mid)` form one group (every node quiet: `shaft_safety`'s body has only `f64`
operations, `if` expressions, `min`, `sqrt` and `pow`, and no loop); the space is that of `mid`;
the leaves are `lo`, `hi`, `MG`, `TG`, `pGrid` (uniform) and the constants; `lo` and `hi` are reused
targets; `mid`, `nfv`, `nyv`, `up` are not read after the group, so they are never stored in the
fused nest. In every iteration of `for it in 0..40` the space test holds (all of the group's roots
have the grid's shape), the reuse tests hold (`lo` and `hi` have that shape from their
definitions), and the fused plain copy runs: no allocation (the `anew`s of the reuse fallback and of
the split copy stand in arms the run never takes; §2.12.10's count shows 0 per iteration).

#### 2.12.5 Passes 3a (`sealower`), 3b and 3c

`sealower` gains no rule: `sea.hirl` keeps its records and refinements; R33 and R34 (§2.12.3) are
validation readings it accepts. It validates as before otherwise. `seaopt` (pass 3b) is unchanged
but for `lirrw`'s vector validation, which it loads and never exercises (Decision 113). `sealopt`
(pass 3c) writes **`sea.lir3`** instead of `sea.lir` (its output file name, one line; no
transformation changes), which pass 3d reads (Decision 98); `--emit lir3` dumps it.

**Observed at 7c** (a follow-up for the later phases, not a decision): fused output can make
`sealopt` much slower although its `sea.lir2` is smaller. In 7c's second review one fuzz program
took 239 s to `--emit lir3` against 101 s before 7c, with byte-identical output; several programs
with long groups passed the review's 120 s timeout for this reason. `sealopt`'s compile time on
fused code is to be looked at when 7e and 7f measure the passes and W4's compile time (§6.3). At
7f W4 compiles in 21.4 s and W1 in 11.0 s, far under the 120 s timeout (§6.3 "Measured at 7f");
the review's slow fuzz program was not measured again.

#### 2.12.6 Pass 3d: `seavec`

`seavec` is a new Baysick program, pass 3d (Decision 98): it reads `sea.lir3`, validates it with
`lirrw` (as `sealopt` validates `sea.lir2`), applies T11, T12, T13 and T10, in that order, to each
function, and writes **`sea.lir`**, the final LIR that pass 4 reads and `--emit lir` dumps. Its
files are `passes/seavec/ve0main.bas` … with `build.list` = `lib io diag tables lirrw`, `data errors
exits consts entries records`; own lines 100 – 59 999; `SUB` prefix `ve_`. It has the room L-bp
leaves a pass that loads `lirrw`: the numeric array letters `S V`, the free columns of `R`, the
scratch `W` between entries, and the unreserved string arrays and scalars (its letter condition at
the gates is waived as `sealopt`'s is, Decision 98). `lirrw` validates the vector classes `x`, `y`,
`m` and the `LF` records in `sea.lir` and `sea.lir3` input positions where they are allowed (only in
`sea.lir`, so `seaopt`, `sealopt` and `seavec` reject them in their inputs) and writes them
(Decision 113). As built (WP-LIB): `seavec` reads `sea.lir3` with `lirrw`'s LIR input kind as
`sealopt` does; `lirrw`'s writer does not validate the vector records `seavec` puts into its tables,
and `seavec` does not read its output back. Every `sea.lir` is validated in the test harness instead
(Decision 116, L-gk): the tool `tools/lirchk.bas` (`tools/lirchk.build.list`: `lib io diag tables
lirrw`, `data errors exits consts entries records`, as `seavec`'s; own lines 100 – 59 999 with the
room L-bp leaves a program that loads `lirrw`; a tool, not gated) reads one `sea.lir` as `seavec`
reads its input, validates it with `lirrw`'s `sea.lir` input kind (the only one that accepts `x y m`
and the `LF` records, with every check of the vector classes: lane counts, `vfeat` only on
`x86_64-linux`, no vector or mask register as a parameter, argument, result or `chk` argument),
writes nothing and ends with status 0 or `lirrw`'s `BAD_RECORD` failure; `tests/run.sh` runs it on the
`sea.lir` of every program and dump test it compiles (for the target it compiles for), and
`tests/stage.sh` on every `seavec` output it produces (`NAME.lir` and `NAME.lirx64`, both targets); a mask register's lane count
is fixed by its first write in record order, a read of a mask with none yet is `BAD_RECORD` (property
2), and `mand mor mnot` and a `mov` of masks take the lane count of their first source (L-gn);
`lirrw` checks only `vfeat` against the target and accepts `y`, `ldm4` and `stm4` in an
`arm64-macos` file, which `seagen_a64` rejects (§2.12.7, L-go); a `lirrw` rejection prints no
detail, so each of its rejection cases in `tests/lib_check.sh` is a one-record mutation of an
accepted file (L-gp). `lirrw`'s string interning (`GOSUB 75000`: the string in `Z$`, its `S$` row in `Q2`, a new
row when absent) is part of its interface for the programs that load it: `seavec`
calls it for the names of the vector entries and the word `avx2` (L-gy; `passes/lib/API.md`
documents it). Its output depends on the `#target` record (Decision 99): on `arm64-macos` T13
writes 2-lane loops; on `x86_64-linux` each vectorized loop is written twice under `vfeat` (4-lane
first, 2-lane in the `else` part, §3.6.5). A function to which none of T11–T13 applies is written
unchanged (T10 is idempotent), so `sea.lir` equals `sea.lir3` for it. Decision 72's capacity rule
holds for every transformation (a transformation whose result would exceed a LIR limit, or a
`seavec` table's region, is not applied to that loop).

*Constants in `seavec`* (Decisions 115, 117). In T11, T12 and T13 a *constant* is a register whose
only definition in the function is an `li`, or a `mov`, `iadd`, `isub` or `imul` whose operands are
constants, its value folded exactly and lying in −2⁵² … 2⁵² (§2.8; in that range the wrapping
instruction gives the exact value). This is L-br's reading of T7 extended: T3 leaves a repeated `li`
as a `mov` of the first (§5.8 T3), T3 does not fold an `isub` of two `li`s (rule 17's `isub L N O`),
and T7 writes its Δ as an `imul` of two such registers. The read and write counts these rules use
("only definition", "nothing reads", "read after") are counted over the whole function (L-gw). A
register is *read after* a loop L when a record after L's last record reads it, or a record before
L inside a loop that encloses L does (reached around that loop's back edge) (L-gu).

**T11. Unrolling of short constant loops** (Decisions 102, 117). T11 visits the loops of the
function as it stands before T11, in record order (its copies are not visited again, L-gt). An
innermost `loop B J S C T` whose S and T are constants and whose *iteration count* n is known, 1 ≤
n ≤ 8, whose body has at most 64 records, no block record, no `exit`/`next`/`ret`, and at least one
load or store whose base is an `sa` of a slot and whose `idx` is J, and whose J is not read after it
(L-gs), is replaced by n copies of its body in order, copy k (k = 1 … n) with J replaced by a new
register written `li Jk v` at its top, v = S + (k − 1)·T folded exactly (L-gq; when a v would leave
−2⁵² … 2⁵², T11 does not apply). n is known when C is a constant c with 0 ≤ c ≤ 7 (n = c + 1), or
when C's only definition is an `rcount C E lo hi st incl site` whose `lo`, `hi` and `st` are
constants (rule 4): then n is the exact number of elements of the range `lo..hi step st` (`incl` 0)
or `lo..=hi step st` (`incl` 1) of LANGUAGE.md §5.1, computed from the folded values with exact
integer arithmetic (§3.6.4 `rcount`: the loop's `last` is n − 1); `st` = 0 (a run-time error) and n
= 0 (an empty range, whose `rcount` writes `last` = 0 and whose guard never enters the loop) make
T11 not apply. A rule-17 loop (`isub L N O` with N and O constants) has C a constant. Registers are
threaded through the copies (L-ev): a register written in the body gets a new name in each copy; a
read in copy k of a register the body writes reads the name copy k gives it when copy k has already
written it, else copy k − 1's name (copy 1: the original register, the value before the loop);
after the last copy, a `mov` from its name to the original register for every register written in
the body and read after the loop or carried around it. The guard's `if` stays, and so does the
`rcount` (it has a site; T10 does not delete it): a loop runs at least once when entered (§3.6.4),
so the n copies run exactly when the loop would, with the same values. After T11 such an access has
a constant `idx` register.

**T12. Scalar replacement** (§5.3; Decisions 102, 117). T12 visits the slots in the order of their
`slot` records, as the function stands before T12 (L-gt). A slot s of at most 256 × 8 bytes whose
every `sa` register (a `p` register every definition of which is an `sa` of s; this rule's own use
list replaces the Terms' private base, whose uses are only without an `idx`, L-gr) is used only by
`ldi ldf sti stf` with `idx` `-` or a constant register (offset off + idx·scale a constant)
and as an operand of a *slot copy* (below), never by `ldb stb ldp stp`, another `mcopy`, a call or an
`rcall`, never a stored value or an operand of `mov`, `padd` or `psel`; and whose accesses touch each
8-byte location with one class only and never partly overlap another location (offsets multiples of
8 from the slot's start; an `ldi` and an `ldf` of the same bytes, or offsets 0 and 4, refuse the
slot, L-ew): each distinct (s, byte offset) becomes a new register of its class; a load of it is a
`mov` from that register, a store a `mov` into it; the first access in record order of each location
must be a store on every path (a forward walk with F6's joins over the function's blocks; a location
read before it is surely written refuses the whole slot; a guard whose condition is known counts as
decided, below; after a `do`'s `enddo` the state is the join of the states at the `exit`s naming that
`do`, not F6's entry state after a loop's closing record, since a path that reaches `enddo` runs the
body again and only its `exit`s leave it, and after a `do` with no `exit` nothing is reachable; an
implementation may bound the nesting it tracks and use the `do`'s entry state beyond it, which is
conservative, L-hb); the `sa` instructions and the slot's `slot`
record are deleted when no use remains (the slots are renumbered densely, `s1`, `s2`, …).

A *slot copy* is an `mcopy Pd Ps N` whose Pd and Ps are `sa` registers of two different slots and
whose N is a constant, a multiple of 8, with 8 ≤ N ≤ the size of each slot. This is how pass 3a
fills a fixed-size array or struct from a literal (its parts stored into the literal's own slot,
then copied) or from another such value (`var r = q`). In the first-access walk a
slot copy reads each location of the source slot at offsets 0, 8, …, N − 8 and then writes the
location at the same offset of the destination; a location's class is propagated through slot
copies (a location copied from or to a location of class `i` or `f` has that class, and two classes
for one location refuse the slot). A location that no slot joined to it by slot copies accesses by
`ldi ldf sti stf` has no class: it takes no part in the walk, gets no register, and the slot copies
write no `mov` for it; its slots are still replaced (L-ha: its bytes are only copied between replaced
slots, which nothing else reaches, so they are never observed). The slots T12 replaces are the greatest set of slots that meet
the conditions above and every slot copy of which has its other slot in the set too (start from
every slot that meets them and remove one whose slot copy has a partner outside the set, until
nothing changes), so a slot copy always joins two replaced slots. Each slot copy then becomes, at
its place, `mov Rd,o Rs,o` for o = 0, 8, …, N − 8 in increasing order (Rs,o and Rd,o the registers of
the source's and destination's locations at offset o): a `mov` copies all 64 bits of its register,
so each location receives exactly the bytes the `mcopy` would copy, and the two regions never
overlap (§3.6.4), so the order of the `mov`s does not matter. An `mcopy` whose other operand is not
an `sa` register of a slot (array data, a `ref` parameter's memory) is not a slot copy and refuses
the slot: the bytes of array data are not known at compile time, and splitting such a copy into
loads or stores of a replaced slot is left out of v1.

*Known guards* (L-gz). In the first-access walk an `if`/`ifz` block whose condition register has a
single definition in the function that folds is *decided*: an `icmp cc c a b` with a and b constants
(rule 17's guard `li Z 0`, `icmp gt E N Z`, `if B E`, with N a constant), folded as the signed
comparison, or an `rcount C c lo hi st incl site` with `lo`, `hi`, `st` constants and `st` ≠ 0
(rule 4's guard `if B E` on its flag), folded as n > 0 with n as T11 computes it. When it holds, the
part that runs (`if`: the first; `ifz`: the `else` part) is on every path through the block and the
other part on none; when it fails, the other way round. The part on no path is dead for the walk
(its accesses are neither required to follow a store nor counted as stores). Rule 17 guards a
fixed-size element-wise result's store loop by `icmp gt N 0` with N constant, so without this a
fused fixed-size result copied into a variable (W3's `q = q + dt * f(q)`) would keep its slots. So
that §3.6.4's property 2 holds for the new registers on every path of the written code, every
decided block that holds an access to, or a slot copy of, a slot T12 replaces is resolved: its
`if`/`ifz`, `else` and `endif` records and its dead part are deleted, the part that runs staying in
place (the condition's definition stays; T10 deletes it when nothing reads it, an `rcount` staying,
as it has a site).

**T13. If-conversion and vectorization** (Decisions 99–101, 108, 115, 117). T13 visits the *candidates*
of the function as it stands before T13, in record order: each `loop` L whose body holds no `loop`
(a `do` in it is allowed here, unlike in the Terms' "innermost" of §5.8, and P1 must dissolve it).
The loops a rewrite writes (vector loops, tails, the `else` loop) are not visited again, as T9's
copies are not (§5.8). On each candidate T13 works in this order: P1 (inlined returns), P2 (unit
accesses), P3 (invariant loads), the if-conversion, the conditions 1–5, the rewrite. P1–P3 and the
if-conversion are L's *preparation*; it is kept only when L is then vectorized. When a step of the
preparation leaves L with a `do`, a block or an access that the conditions reject, when L fails one
of the conditions 1–5, or when the rewrite would exceed a LIR limit or a `seavec` table's region
(Decision 72), L and everything P2 wrote before it are written exactly as they stood before P1 (no
counter update of P2 is written: those exist only with the rewrite), and T13 goes on with the next
candidate. In T13 *before L* means immediately before L's opening record, in the part that holds
it (§5.8 Terms; a `loop` runs its body at least once when it is entered, §3.6.4, so what stands
there runs exactly when L is entered); the rewrite replaces L in place. In the rewrite, the scalar
loop L that runs the tail and the `else` part is L after P1 and P2, without the if-conversion (P3
changes nothing in a scalar loop). So `sea.lir` differs from `sea.lir3` only in the loops T13
vectorizes (and in T11's and T12's changes).

*Constants.* The conditions 1 and 5 and P2 read "constant" in the sense of "Constants in `seavec`"
above. T13 folds a constant's value into the `li`s it writes and reads
no constant's register before or after L except L's own operands S, C and T, which are written
before L (L reads them at its entry, §3.6.4 property 2).

**P1. Inlined returns.** L20's lowering of an inlined call (rule 37: an `iblk` is `do D` … `enddo D`,
each `iret` its `mov`s and `exit D`, §3.5.9) leaves in L a `do` that every path leaves by its `exit`.
P1 dissolves each `do D` in L, innermost first, whose body holds no `loop`, no `do` (after those
nested in it are dissolved), no `ret`, no `next` and no `exit` naming a block other than D. A part
of a block (or D's body) *ends in `exit D`* when its last record is `exit D`, or is the `endif` of an
`if`/`ifz` block both of whose parts end in `exit D` (a missing `else` part is empty and does not).
Repeatedly, until neither applies (the result does not depend on the order):

1. the records after an `exit D`, and after a block both of whose parts end in `exit D`, up to the
   end of the part (or of D's body) that holds it, are deleted: they never run;
2. for an `if`/`ifz` block I exactly one of whose parts ends in `exit D`, the records after I up to
   the end of the part (or body) that holds I move, in order, to the end of I's other part (an
   `else` is created for a block without one).

Then a record is *in tail position* when it is the last record of D's body, or the last record of a
part of a block whose `endif` is in tail position. When D's body ends in `exit D` and every `exit D`
is in tail position, every `exit D`, the `do D` and the `enddo D` are deleted. Otherwise D stays (a
path that reaches `enddo D` runs D's body again, §3.6.4; a guarded `exit D` with records after its
block on both of its paths would need them duplicated), and L is not vectorized. P1 moves and
deletes records but never copies or reorders an operation, so every path runs the same instructions
in the same order and §3.6.4's property 2 still holds (a deleted record never ran).

**P2. Unit accesses.** When L's step T is a constant 1 and S, C and T are invariant in L, with `ind`
J:

* A *counter* of L is an `i` register K ≠ J whose only write in L is one `iadd K K U` (U a constant
  1) at the top block level of L's body, after every read of K in L. In the iteration whose `ind` is
  J it holds K₀ + (J − S), wrapping, K₀ being its value at L's entry.
* A *walked base* is a `p` register Q with exactly two definitions in the function: one before L
  (T7's invariant-stride form, §5.8) and `padd Q Q Δ`, the first record of L's body, with Δ a
  constant whose value δ is the element size of the accesses on Q (8 for `ldf stf`, 1 for `ldb stb`);
  Q is read only by that `padd` and by accesses in L with base Q, `idx` `-` and scale 0 (T7's `Q - 0
  o`), all of one element size. In the iteration whose `ind` is J such an access at offset o addresses
  Q₀ + (J − S + 1)·δ + o, Q₀ being Q's value at L's entry. A reverse walk (δ the negative element
  size, from a slice with step −1) is refused: its elements run downwards, which the vector form's
  ascending lanes do not express; its accesses stay, and L fails (2).

An `ldf stf ldb stb` access in L (at any depth) whose base D is invariant in L, with scale z and
offset o, and whose `idx` X is computed in L from exactly one of J or a counter K, with coefficient
1, constants and invariant registers by wrapping `iadd`, `isub` and `imul` by a constant 1 only (X =
V + c + Σσᵢtᵢ: V that J or K, c a constant, tᵢ invariant registers with signs σᵢ = ±1), becomes `D′
J z 0` with D′ = D + (Σσᵢtᵢ·z + e), e = c·z + o; for a counter, one more term t = E with σ = +1,
E = K₀ − S. An access `Q - 0 o` on a walked base becomes `D′ J δ 0` with D′ = Q + (o + δ − δ·S), and
the `padd Q Q Δ` is deleted. Before L (after whatever stands there) P2 writes, in this order:

1. for each counter whose reads are rewritten, in the order of the counters' `iadd`s in L, `isub E
   K S` (K holding K₀ there): one E per counter, shared by its accesses;
2. for each D′, in the record order of the first access that uses it (accesses with equal D, terms,
   e and scale share one D′): T7's unit-stride instructions (§5.8), one group `li Z σz`, `imul T1 t
   Z` (both omitted when σz = 1, T1 being t), `padd D1 D T1` per term t, the counter's E first, then
   the others in the order of their first reads in X's computation, then, when e ≠ 0, `li G e` and
   `padd D′ D1 G` (each operand the previous result, D′ being the last one written); for a walked
   base, with S a constant, `li G e` and `padd D′ Q G` with e = o + δ − δ·S (D′ being Q when e = 0),
   and with S not a constant, `li Z −δ`, `imul T1 S Z`, `padd D1 Q T1`, then, when e = o + δ ≠ 0,
   `li G e` and `padd D′ D1 G`.

A counter none of whose reads remain loses its `iadd`; after the rewrite's last record (the `endif`
of the vector form's `if`) it gets `iadd K K C` and `iadd K K T` (T, the step, holds 1 and is
defined outside L), the K₀ + C + 1 that L leaves, the counters in the order of their `iadd`s in L.
Then the pure instructions of L whose results nothing reads are deleted (T10's first rule,
restricted to L). Every instruction P2 writes wraps, as the address computations it replaces do, so
each access addresses exactly the bytes it addressed before, element by element, and (4)'s test sees
the true bases; an access whose folded constants would leave −2⁵² … 2⁵², or whose X chain holds
another instruction (a checked one, a second counter, J with another coefficient), an invariant
register that occurs as two terms, or more than 6 invariant terms tᵢ (L-gv), is not changed.

**P3. Invariant loads.** A load `ldf F P - 0 o` in L (at any depth) is *invariant* when: P is
invariant in L and is a parameter never written or a register every definition of which is an `sa`
of one slot s; no register holding that address (P; for a slot, every `sa` register of s) is,
anywhere in the function, a stored value or an operand of `mov`, `padd` or `psel`; its bytes lie
inside the memory P reaches (T8 (c), §5.8); and L holds no store whose base is P (for a slot, any
`sa` register of s), no `mcopy`, no `call` and no `rcall` other than `sea_log sea_exp sea_sin sea_cos
sea_pow sea_hypot`. Outside L, P may be a `call` argument or an `mcopy` operand (so it need not be a
private base, §5.8 Terms). By §3.6.4 properties 3 and 4 (L-af) no instruction of L changes those
bytes, and P is an object pointer (§5.8 T8, L-at), so the load cannot fail and reads one value in
every iteration. An invariant load is a record of the vector set (2) and may stand in a part that
is if-converted (computing it on both paths reads valid memory and changes no value, LANGUAGE.md
§6.10); in the vector loop it is replaced by one load before the vector loop and a splat (the
listing below); in the scalar loops it stays where it is.

**If-conversion** (L-fg). In L, each `if`/`ifz` block (with or without `else`, nested ones
innermost first) whose condition register c is a mask register (2) written earlier in the iteration
and whose parts hold only records of the vector set below (no store, no failing instruction, no
`rcall` with a site, no `call`, no block of another kind) is *if-converted*: both parts are computed
in order, every register a part writes being renamed in that part, and after the block each register
R written in a part and read at any record outside that part (later in the iteration, earlier in L's
body, which a later iteration reaches, or after L) is merged from Ra and Rb, the renamed values of
the two parts (the value of R before the block where a part does not write it): an `f` register by
`fsel R c Ra Rb`, a mask register by `iand R1 c Ra`, `bnot R2 c`, `iand R3 R2 Rb`, `ior R R1 R3`
(R1, R2, R3 new registers); for `ifz` Ra and Rb are swapped. A register read only inside the part
that writes it is not merged. The merges stand in the order of their registers' first writes in the
block, and each reads c's value from before the block: a part that writes c (the `&&`/`||`
lowering, `fcmp gt c …; if B c; fcmp le c …; endif B`) writes a renamed register like any other, and
c's own merge comes last. Since c, Ra and Rb hold 0 or 1, the mask formula is the selection exactly,
and lane by lane `mand`, `mnot`, `mand`, `mor` give the same. This is the speculation LANGUAGE.md
§6.10 allows for arms that cannot fail; it changes no observed value (each lane selects the scalar
arm's result). A unit access in a converted part is in range whichever arm runs: T1 narrows only
on integer comparisons (§5.8 Facts), never on an `fcmp` or a loaded `bool`, and a block whose
condition is not a mask register is not converted, so an access whose `chkb` T1 removed, or whose
extents a fused copy checked before L, addresses an element that exists in every iteration of L.
A block that is not if-converted stays, and L fails (1). Then L is vectorized when:

1. L is `loop B J S C T` with T a constant 1 and S, C, T invariant in L, and after its preparation
   its body is one region (no block record, no `exit`, `next` or `ret`), so L is innermost, and the
   body holds at least one unit access (after P2; Decision 117: a loop with an empty body, or with no
   access, gains nothing from the vector form and is not vectorized);
2. every record of the body is in the *vector set*: a *unit access* `ldf X D J 8 0`, `stf V D J 8
   0`, `ldb M D J 1 0` or `stb M D J 1 0` with D invariant in L (T7's unit-stride form, §5.8: a
   folded or whole-array leaf of a plain copy gives it, its constant and invariant index terms
   folded into D, and P2 gives it to counter-indexed accesses and walked bases); an invariant load
   (P3); `fadd fsub fmul fdiv fsqrt fneg fabs fmin fmax` of `f` registers; `fcmp cc M a b`; `fsel R
   c a b`; `iand ior` of two mask registers and `bnot` of one; `mov` of an `f` or mask register;
   `lf` (a splat); an `rcall` of `sea_log sea_exp sea_sin sea_cos sea_pow sea_hypot` (no site); and
   the sum8 group of (5). The *mask registers* are the greatest set of `i` registers each of which
   is written in the body only by `fcmp`, `ldb`, and `iand`, `ior`, `bnot` or `mov` of mask
   registers, and read only by `fsel`'s condition, `stb`, `iand`, `ior`, `bnot`, `mov` and, before
   the if-conversion, an `if`/`ifz` (found as §5.8 finds the array registers: start from every `i`
   register written in the body and remove one whose writes or reads break this until nothing
   changes); each holds 0 or 1 (`fcmp` and `bnot` write 0 or 1, and every stored byte is 0 or 1,
   §3.6.4);
3. every `f` register the body reads is written earlier in the same iteration (an invariant load's
   destination included), or invariant in L (splatted once before the vector loop), or the sum8
   accumulator; every `i` register it reads is a mask register written earlier in the iteration, J
   as the `idx` of a unit access, or J, Q and W in a sum8 group (5); no register written in the body,
   J included, is read after L, and none is read before its write in the body (no lane value lives
   out, no other carried value), the sum8 home excepted. The registers *written in the body* are
   those L's body writes before the if-conversion, a renamed register standing for its original (a
   counter P2 removed is no longer written in the body). J is never read after a loop by pass 3a's
   lowering or by `seafuse` (a loop variable is scoped to its loop), so refusing such a read costs
   no workload loop and spares the rewrite the value L-ay gives J;
4. *independence at run time*: for every pair of unit accesses of one kind (`f64` or byte) at least
   one of which is a store, with different bases Da and Db (identical bases: the same element,
   always allowed), the distance d = Da − Db (`pdiff`) satisfies d ≤ −w·8 or d ≥ w·8 for `f64` (w·1
   for bytes), w = 8 the elements per vector iteration, or d = 0; the test runs before the loop,
   and the scalar loop runs when it fails (accesses of different kinds never overlap: an array has
   one element kind, L-ex);
5. *the sum8 group* (Decision 101): the records `iand W J Q` (Q the constant 7), `ldf G A W 8 0`,
   `fadd G G Y`, `stf G A W 8 0` with A the `sa` of a 64-byte slot (L13's home, R14) and the loop's
   start S the constant 0: the vector loop keeps the eight accumulators in four 2-lane (or two
   4-lane) registers loaded from the home before the loop (lanes 0–1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7) and stored back
   after it, so lane k adds exactly the elements with index ≡ k (mod 8) in increasing order
   (LANGUAGE.md §10.5's order, independent of the width); no other carried value is vectorized
   (`max min argmax argmin`, `nnz any all`, the `i64` sums, F3's masked sums and user accumulations
   stay scalar: lane-split forms would change ties, signed zeros or overflow points).

**The rewrite.** L is replaced, in place, by the *vector form* below (normative, so that its
goldens follow byte for byte; every listed `li` is written where it is listed, with a register of
its own). Before it stand P2's instructions (they are before L). Let n = C + 1 (up to 2⁶⁴) and nv =
n div 8 the vector iterations.

1. *The split*: `li R7 7`, `isub A C R7`, `li R3 3`, `ishr Cv A R3`, `ishr H C R3`, `icmp le V Cv
   H`. For C ≥ 7 (unsigned) Cv = (C − 7) div 8 = nv − 1 ≤ H; for C < 7, A wraps to at least 2⁶⁴ − 7
   and Cv ≥ 2⁶¹ − 1 > 0 = H; both are below 2⁶¹, so the signed `icmp` is the unsigned comparison and
   V = 1 exactly when nv > 0, the full range C = 2⁶⁴ − 1 included (nv = 2⁶¹, n never formed).
2. *The independence test* of (4): the *entries* are the pairs (base register, kind) of the body's
   unit accesses, in the record order of each entry's first access; a *pair* is two entries i < j
   of one kind with different registers at least one of which has a store in the body (one pair per
   two entries, however many accesses they have), in the order of i, then j. When there is a pair:
   `li Z0 0`; when an `f64` pair exists, `li P8 64`, `li N8 −64`; when a byte pair exists, `li P1 8`,
   `li N1 −8`; then for each pair (Ei, Ej): `pdiff Dd Ei Ej`, `icmp ge G1 Dd Pk`, `icmp le G2 Dd Nk`,
   `icmp eq G3 Dd Z0`, `ior G4 G1 G2`, `ior G5 G4 G3`, `iand Vk Vk−1 G5` (Pk, Nk of the pair's kind;
   V0 = V). The form's condition is the last Vk (V when there is no pair), so nv > 0 enters as the
   first operand of the chain.
3. `if Bi Vlast`; then on `arm64-macos` the 2-lane part and its tail; on `x86_64-linux` `vfeat F
   avx2`, `if Bf F`, the 4-lane part and its tail, `else Bf`, the 2-lane part and its tail, `endif
   Bf`; then `else Bi`, the scalar loop L on the whole range, `endif Bi`; then P2's counter updates.

A *w-lane part* (w = 2 with the class `x` and m = 4 copies, or w = 4 with `y` and m = 2; `Xop` names
`xop` or `yop`, `ldmw`/`stmw` `ldm2`/`stm2` or `ldm4`/`stm4`) is, in order:

* *the splats*, in the record order of the body (within a record, operands left to right): for the
  first read of each invariant `f` register r, `Xsplat Sr r`; for each invariant load `ldf F P - 0
  o`, `ldf F′ P - 0 o` and `Xsplat SF F′`; for each `lf F v` of the body, `lf F′ v` and `Xsplat SF
  F′`; each part writes its own (so on `x86_64-linux` each arm has its splats);
* *the sum8 homes*, for each sum8 group in the order of its `iand`: `Xld Hq A - 0 (q − 1)·8w` for q
  = 1 … m (`ldx` at 0, 16, 32, 48; `ldy` at 0, 32);
* `li E8 8`, `loop Bv Jv S Cv E8`, the vector body, `endloop Bv`;
* the sum8 homes stored back, `Xst Hq A - 0 (q − 1)·8w`, in the same order;
* *the tail*: `li R7′ 7`, `iand Nt A R7′`, `li Z′ 0`, `icmp gt Gt Nt Z′`, `if Bt Gt`, `li R3′ 3`,
  `ishl Pt Cv R3′`, `iadd S1 S Pt`, `li E8′ 8`, `iadd St S1 E8′`, `isub Lt Nt T`, `loop Bl J′ St Lt
  T`, the body of L after P1 and P2, `endloop Bl`, `endif Bt`: the tail count n − 8·nv is Nt = A mod
  8 (A = n − 8, Cv = A div 8) and its start S + 8·nv is St.

*The vector body*: each record of the prepared body in order is replaced by m consecutive copies,
copy q (q = 1 … m) computing lanes (q − 1)·w … q·w − 1, as follows: a unit access `ldf X D J 8 0` /
`stf V D J 8 0` becomes `Xld Xq D Jv 8 (q − 1)·8w` / `Xst Vq D Jv 8 (q − 1)·8w`, and `ldb M D J 1 0`
/ `stb M D J 1 0` becomes `ldmw Mq D Jv 1 (q − 1)·w` / `stmw Mq D Jv 1 (q − 1)·w`; `fadd fsub fmul
fdiv fsqrt fneg fabs fmin fmax fcmp fsel` become `Xadd … Xmax Xcmp Xsel` of the copies (same `cc`);
`iand ior bnot` of masks become `mand mor mnot`; a `mov` becomes a `mov` of the copies; an `rcall` of
`sea_f` becomes `rcall sea_f_x` (or `sea_f_y`) with the same field layout; an `lf F v` or an
invariant load writing F becomes nothing when F has no other write in the body (its reads then read
SF) and `mov Fq SF` otherwise; the sum8 group's `iand` and `ldf` become nothing, its `fadd G G Y`
`Xadd Hq Hq Yq` and its `stf` nothing. In copy q an operand that is an `f` or mask register written
in the body is that register's copy-q register (one per register and copy, the same for all its
writes), an invariant `f` register r is Sr, and J is Jv.

*Registers.* Each copy of L (the tails, the `else` loop) has its own local registers (those written
in L and read only in L, J included); the registers written before L or read after it are the same
in every copy (L-bl). The split, the test, each part's splats, homes, step and vector loop write
registers of their own. T10 then renumbers the function (§3.6.1), which fixes every number, so only
which registers are the same matters. Every lane performs its element's scalar sequence (§3.6.4:
each `x`/`y` instruction is lane by lane the scalar instruction of its name), so the vector and
scalar forms give identical bits (LANGUAGE.md §6.8 4.).

**Alignment**: none is required or assumed: unit accesses are unaligned vector loads and stores
(NEON `ldr q`, SSE2 `movupd`, AVX2 `vmovupd`); no peeling (L-ey).

**What the workloads get** (Decisions 108, 115, 118). W1's bisection nest, the plain copy's linear loop
over the grid (`.main`, lines 259–265 of the port since 9d, 251–257 before it), is vectorized: its accesses are already unit;
`shaft_safety`'s inlined body is a `do` that ends in a single `exit`, which T8 treats as an
innermost loop and T9 leaves whole (T9 unswitches only `loop` blocks, Decision 118), and P1
dissolves it; its `&&` conditions merge as masks; its loads of `pGrid`'s fields (an `sa` slot
also passed to a `call` and an `mcopy` destination outside the loop) are invariant loads (P3); and
its `if` chains, whose arms call only `pow` and compute `f64` values, are if-converted. The broadcast
copy is not (non-unit accesses). The split copy (the `else` arm of the group's space test, each
statement's nest over its own space, L-eq) is: five of its loops in W1's nest, one of them over
`shaft_safety`'s inlined body with the same lane ops as the fused body (Decision 119), and in W4's
group of `Tc`, `tgs`, `Tn` and `dMax` its two element-wise loops (`add mul`; `sub mul add`) at each
of the two call sites, in 2-lane and (on `x86_64-linux`) 4-lane form (found by 7f's independent
review at 7e's tree and after 7f, checked in `--emit lir` on both targets at 7f's close). W4's
`rb_half_sweep` store `T[1..ny-1, :] = where(colorIn, Tn, Tc)` (its inner loop over rows: the reads
of `Tn`, `Tc` and the mask at `seafuse`'s linear counter O, which P2 makes unit accesses, the store to
`T`, and a step that T3 left as a `mov` of an `li 1`, a constant in T13's sense) and `residual`'s
fused nest (its reads through the row counter K, P2) are vectorized; the group nest of `Tc`,
`tgs`, `Tn` and `dMax` is not (its masked `max` carries values under an `if` that holds a store-free
but carried update, which (3) excludes); the scalar SOR loop is not (its `next`, a `chkb` and the
carried `dMax`; §5.2's shape stays), and neither is W5's LCG loop (a failing `imulc`, a carried
value, `itof`). A W1-shaped loop
over a unit-step slice (`tests/programs/vec_ifexpr_w1.sea`) gets a walked base (P2). The shape
lines of §2.12.10 check W1's nest and W4's store. W1's vector body calls `sea_pow_x` (or `_y`) twice
per copy, both computed, where the scalar loop calls `sea_pow` once per element; with T9's split of
the `do` (Decision 115's option (a), as built in 7e) it called it three times per copy (two in one
T9 copy, one in the other), and 7f measured that split to cost W1's compute time (Decision 118).

#### 2.12.7 Pass 4 (both targets)

* **Allocator** (`passes/lib/ralloc.bas`, §4.9.2): the classes `x`, `y`, `m` are allocated like `f`
  from the vector register file of the target (an `m` register of a 2-lane mask holds all-ones or
  all-zeros 64-bit lanes in a vector register; of a 4-lane mask in a `ymm`), with spill slots of 16
  (`x`, 2-lane `m`) and 32 bytes (`y`, 4-lane `m`) at 16-byte alignment, accessed with unaligned
  vector moves (`str q`/`ldr q`; `movupd`; `vmovupd`), so no frame is realigned (the System V stack
  guarantees 16 bytes, L-fh); across a `call` or `rcall` every vector register is caller-saved (on
  arm64 only the low 64 bits of `v8`–`v15` survive a call, so an `x` or `m` value live across one is
  spilled, L-ez). As built (WP-LIB): L-ez's "spilled" is §4.9.2's "Calls" save, a store to the
  interval's save slot (listed by `ra_sv`) before each call it crosses and a load after it, on both
  targets and on the free path of a `release`, not a spill of the whole interval (L-gl); a vector
  interval takes the `f` row "crossing no call" even when it crosses a call, so arm64 does not
  prefer `d8`–`d15` (which would only add prologue saves), and is saved around each call even in a
  callee-saved register, which `ra_used` still reports (L-gm); the classes are 4 `x`, 5 `y`, 6 a
  2-lane and 7 a 4-lane `m`, a mask's lane count coming from its defining instruction (`xcmp`/`ldm2`
  2, `ycmp`/`ldm4` 4, `mand mor mnot mov` their first source's, L-gn).
* **Comparisons, selections, `xmin`/`xmax`** (both targets; L-fi): a mask lane is all-ones where the
  comparison holds; `lt le eq` use the ordered predicates, `gt ge` swap the operands of `lt le`, and
  `ne` uses the unordered not-equal (a NaN lane is set, as `fcmp ne`); AVX uses the `_OQ` predicates
  for `lt le eq` and `NEQ_UQ` for `ne`. `xmin`/`xmax` (and `y`) are, per lane, exactly §3.6.4's
  rule: t = (b < a) ordered (`xmax`: b > a); r = select(t, b, a); u = (a unordered a); r =
  select(u, b, r); never `fmin`/`fminnm`/`minpd`/`maxpd`, whose NaN and ±0 rules differ.
* **Mask loads and stores** (L-fi; every stored byte is 0 or 1, §3.6.4): `ldm2` loads 2 bytes,
  widens them to two 64-bit lanes of 0 or 1 and negates them (0 → 0, 1 → all-ones); `stm2` shifts
  each lane right by 63 (all-ones → 1), narrows to bytes and stores 2 bytes; `ldm4`/`stm4` the same
  with 4. arm64: `ldr h`, `uxtl` (`.8h`, `.4s`, `.2d`), `neg .2d`; store `ushr #63`, `xtn` (`.2s`,
  `.4h`, `.8b`), `str h`. SSE2: `movzwl` and `movd`, `punpcklbw`, `punpcklwd`, `punpckldq` with a
  zero register, then `psubq` from zero; store `psrlq $63`, `pshufd $0x08`, `packssdw`, `packuswb`,
  `movd` and a 2-byte `movw`. AVX2: `vpmovzxbq` (4 bytes to four lanes of 0 or 1), `vpsubq` from
  zero; store `vpsrlq $63`, `vextracti128`, `vpackusdw`, `vpackusdw`, `vpackuswb`, `vmovd` and a
  4-byte store. `ysel` uses `vblendvpd`, whose selector is the lane's sign bit, set in an all-ones
  lane.
* **`seagen_a64`** (NEON, AAPCS64): the 2-lane arithmetic as single `.2d` instructions (`fadd fsub
  fmul fdiv fsqrt fneg fabs`), `fcmgt`/`fcmge`/`fcmeq` (with operand swaps for `lt le`, `ne` as the
  negation of `fcmeq`), `bsl`/`bif` for `xsel`, `dup` for `xsplat`, `mov d, v.d[k]` for `xlane`;
  `pdiff` as `sub`. `y` instructions, `ldm4`, `stm4` and `vfeat` are `BAD_RECORD` on arm64.
* **`seagen_x64`** (System V): the 2-lane instructions in SSE2 (`addpd subpd mulpd divpd sqrtpd`,
  `andpd`/`xorpd` with sign masks for `xabs`/`xneg`, `cmppd`, `andpd`/`andnpd`/`orpd` for `xsel`,
  `unpcklpd` for `xsplat`); the 4-lane instructions in AVX2 with VEX encodings (`vaddpd`, …,
  `vcmppd`, `vblendvpd`, `vbroadcastsd`); `vfeat d avx2` as `cmpq $SEA_VAR_AVX2, sea_variant(%rip)`
  and `sete` (`_sea_variant`, §4.8); `pdiff` as `sub`. **`vzeroupper`** is executed at every exit
  from the code of a 4-lane loop (its tail's start, the `else` of its `if`) and before every `call`
  or `rcall` of a non-`_y` entry from inside it, never between two 4-lane instructions (L-fd;
  performance only). No FMA instruction is ever written (no `vfmadd*`), on either target (§3.6.4
  "Reproducibility").
* Scalar instructions keep their templates of §4.9.2; the shape tests' scalar loops (§5.2) do not
  change (W4's SOR loop and W5's LCG loop are not vectorizable: they carry values and have blocks
  with stores).

#### 2.12.8 Runtime: vector forms of the elementary functions

Twelve entries (Decision 103), ids 39–50, enter `rt.inc`'s `SEA_ENTRY_LIST` and §4.8's Id-first
table with WP-CONTRACT (written NAME-first here, as §4.8's planned tables are, so that the contract
check reads only the Id-first table; WP-CONTRACT moves them there):

| NAME | Id | symbol | Site | Args | Results | Contract |
|------|---:|--------|------|------|---------|----------|
| `LOG_X` | 39 | `sea_log_x` | `-` | `x` | `x` | each lane exactly `sea_log` of that lane; cannot fail |
| `EXP_X` | 40 | `sea_exp_x` | `-` | `x` | `x` | each lane `sea_exp` |
| `SIN_X` | 41 | `sea_sin_x` | `-` | `x` | `x` | each lane `sea_sin` |
| `COS_X` | 42 | `sea_cos_x` | `-` | `x` | `x` | each lane `sea_cos` |
| `POW_X` | 43 | `sea_pow_x` | `-` | `xx` | `x` | each lane `sea_pow` of the lanes of the two operands |
| `HYPOT_X` | 44 | `sea_hypot_x` | `-` | `xx` | `x` | each lane `sea_hypot` |
| `LOG_Y` | 45 | `sea_log_y` | `-` | `y` | `y` | each of 4 lanes `sea_log`; `x86_64-linux` only (AVX2) |
| `EXP_Y` | 46 | `sea_exp_y` | `-` | `y` | `y` | as 40, 4 lanes, `x86_64-linux` only |
| `SIN_Y` | 47 | `sea_sin_y` | `-` | `y` | `y` | as 41, 4 lanes, `x86_64-linux` only |
| `COS_Y` | 48 | `sea_cos_y` | `-` | `y` | `y` | as 42, 4 lanes, `x86_64-linux` only |
| `POW_Y` | 49 | `sea_pow_y` | `-` | `yy` | `y` | as 43, 4 lanes, `x86_64-linux` only |
| `HYPOT_Y` | 50 | `sea_hypot_y` | `-` | `yy` | `y` | as 44, 4 lanes, `x86_64-linux` only |

**ABI** (§4.10.1 gains the rows): arm64: the operands in `v0` (and `v1`), the result in `v0`; may
clobber what the scalar entries may; preserves `x19`–`x29`, `sp`, `d8`–`d15`, FPCR. x86_64: the
`_x` entries take `%xmm0` (and `%xmm1`) and return `%xmm0`; the `_y` entries take `%ymm0` (and
`%ymm1`) and return `%ymm0`; both may clobber every vector register and what the scalar entries may;
a `_y` entry is called only from 4-lane code and returns with the upper halves live (it executes no
`vzeroupper` before returning; before calling a scalar entry for a rare lane it stores its live
`ymm` values in its frame and executes `vzeroupper`). Stack: at most 512 bytes below the incoming
`sp` (the return address on x86_64), inside `SEA_STACK_MARGIN`. The `_y` symbols are defined only by
the x86_64 runtime; `seavec` names them only for `x86_64-linux` (Decision 99), so an arm64 program
never references one.

**Algorithm**: §4.10's text per lane, as §4.10.1 "Vector forms" says: branches become per-lane
selects, table lookups per-lane loads, and the *rare* paths (special inputs, `exp` with |x| ≥ 512,
the Payne–Hanek reduction for |x| ≥ 2²³, subnormal inputs) call the scalar entry for each lane that
needs one: the rare lanes are found by vector compares into one lane mask, which is tested once (the
common case calls nothing scalar). Two sets are found only after the common computation: `pow`'s
lanes whose step-10 |ehi| ≥ 512 (`exp_core`'s rare and huge paths) and `hypot`'s lanes whose
scaling-up branch holds step 6's subnormal rounding (max(|x|, |y|) < 2⁻⁵⁰⁰). The rare sets are per
target where an instruction is missing: the `x86_64` SSE2 forms treat `pow` with finite x < 0 as rare
(no per-lane variable shift), the arm64 forms compute the negative bases of an integer y in vector;
the results are bit-identical either way, since a rare lane's result is the scalar entry's. Every
operation is one of §4.10's (no FMA, no approximate instruction), so each lane's bits are the scalar
entry's.
SSE2 has no `pcmpgtq`, `roundpd`, `pinsrq` or 64-bit packed conversion and NEON no 64 × 64-bit
multiply: where §4.10's step needs one, the vector form uses an exact sequence or the scalar entry
for that lane. Files: `rt_vmath.s` per target (beside `rt_math.s`); it calls only the scalar contract
entries (`rt_math.s`'s helpers are assembler-local labels, so it cannot call them) and emits its own
copy of the tables with `SEA_EMIT_MATH_TABLES` (the `sea_mt_*` labels are file-local, §4.10.3); both
Makefiles take the runtime sources by wildcard, so no object list changes. As built: arm64 751 lines
(the `_x` entries), x86_64 1 084 lines (the `_x` entries in SSE2 and the `_y` entries in AVX2, both
instantiated from shared macros).

**Tests** (§6.2, "Phase-7 tests"): `tests/math/math_check.c` gains the vector entries: (1) every
committed vector of `tests/math/*.vec` in every lane position of a 2-lane (and on x86_64, with AVX2
present, a 4-lane) call, the other lanes filled from the rare and special inputs of the same file;
(2) a seeded random differential test (L-fj): for each function 2²⁴ inputs per lane pattern from a
fixed-seed xorshift generator over all bit patterns and over each function's interesting ranges
(|x| near 2²³ and 512, subnormals, ±0, ±∞, NaN payloads), each vector result lane compared bit for
bit with the scalar entry; built as before (`-O1 -ffp-contract=off`; the 4-lane part in a second
translation unit with `-mavx2`, run only when the CPU reports AVX2, which the Linux host does,
Decision 104). As built: the lane patterns of (2) are *mixed* (every lane drawn from all inputs),
*all-common*, *one-rare* (exactly one rare lane, its position rotating with the call index) and
*all-rare*, 2²⁴ vector calls per function and pattern, each lane of each call checked against the
scalar entry; the rare inputs that fill the other lanes in (1) are the cases of the same file whose
arguments are zero, subnormal, infinite, NaN, |x| ≥ 2²³ or 256 ≤ |x| < 1 024. The tests run on a
thread pool (`-lpthread` on Linux) with their output buffered per task and printed in a fixed order,
so the output is deterministic and the case fits `cross_run.sh`'s 60 s limit (measured: 5 s on the
Mac, 33 s on the Linux host). `tests/rt/<target>/rt_vmath_abi.s` checks each target's own ABI
(registers, FPCR / MXCSR, the 512-byte stack bound) and `tests/rt/x86_64_linux/rt_vmath_abi_y.s` the
`_y` entries (AVX2; it reports a host without AVX2 and fails).

#### 2.12.9 Capacity and limits

Baysick's limits bind the two new programs as every pass (§2.7: 10 000 lines, 255-byte lines,
1 000 `FOR`s, 65 536 string bytes; projected in §2.7 "Projected for phase 7"). The compiled program
grows: a fused group writes its leaf and check phase once and up to three nests (the plain and
broadcast copies, F1 (4), and the split copy, F2 (2)); a vectorized loop is written up to three
times (4-lane, 2-lane, scalar) plus its tail. LIR limits are respected by Decision 72's rule
(T11–T13), HIR limits by L-el. No `limits.inc` value changes.

#### 2.12.10 W4, W1 and the checks

**The W4 port.** `sea/ports/w4_heat_plate.sea` is a new port of `w4_heat_plate.m` (without
figures, without `SEA_PLOT` and `SEA_SAVE_FIGURES`), written statement by statement as W1's is
(operation order kept, LANGUAGE.md §6.8; faithfulness notes in its header comment), with the
scalar SOR solver of `tests/accept/w4_sor.sea` (whose loop shape §5.2 fixes), the red-black solver
with `rb_half_sweep` exactly as LANGUAGE.md §2.4 writes it (a `ref T` parameter, `where` for the
masked store; Decision 107), `residual`, the heat-flow balance, the flux field and the profiles of
the MATLAB script, the export record with every key of `workloads/reference/w4_heat_plate.json`,
and the option loop of W1 (`--export-reference` only). Its token map `sea/ports/w4_heat_plate.tokens`
is written from the MATLAB `fprintf` formats and `compare.py`'s `RULES` (§6.4). `tests/accept.sh`
accepts it as it accepts W1 and W5 (§6.3, "Phase-7 acceptance"), and `make cross` runs it as a
`ports/` case, byte-identical on the host but for the `Compute time` line.

**What runs fused.** By F1–F5 with their conditions: W1's grid bisection loop (lines 259–265 of the
port, the group of §2.12.4's example); W4's `rb_half_sweep` (class (c) of §8.6, inlined at both
call sites, fused in its body before `sealoop` inlines it, Decision 110): `Tp`'s concatenation
copies its three slices from `T` (F4); `Tc`, `tgs`, `Tn` and `dMax` form one group (the masked
reduction fused, F3), which ends before the store `T[1..ny-1, :] = where(colorIn, Tn, Tc)` because
`tgs` reads `T` at rows shifted against the rows the store writes (F2 (3)); `tgs` is not read after
the group and is never stored; `Tc` and `Tn`, read by the store, are; the store is a fused selection
store (F1 (3), (5): kind R and A, reading `Tn` and `Tc`, not `T`'s root path, at the element it
writes), so it allocates nothing.

**The temporaries check** (Decision 105). A *temporary* is an array allocated for a value that has
no name in the source: an operand of an operator, a view, a selection, a part of a concatenation,
an elemental application's result that a tree consumes, or a copy made by a copy on write that the
reference would not make. The check counts allocations at run time: with `SEA_HEAP_CHECK=count`
(a new value of the existing switch, §4.5, L-fk) the runtime prints, in place of the heap line,
`heap: <a> allocations, <l> live objects` + LF, a counting every object the runtime creates (the
`sea_arr_new*` entries, the copy of `sea_arr_unique`, every `str` the runtime returns). Two test
programs, `tests/fusion/w1_bisect.sea` and `tests/fusion/w4_rb.sea`, are the W1 bisection loop over
the port's 90 × 120 grid and W4's red-black iteration over the port's 161 × 241 plate, each taking
its iteration count k from `args()`; `tests/fusion.sh` (the group `test-fusion` of `make test`, and
a cross case kind `fusion` on the host under both variants) runs each with k and k + 1 and requires
the difference of the two counts to be exactly the hand-derived allocations per iteration: **W1:
0** (the fused plain copy, §2.12.4's example); **W4: 6** (per call of `rb_half_sweep`: `Tp`'s result,
the stored group locals `Tc` and `Tn`; two calls per iteration; `T` is unique, so its `cow` copies
nothing). The derivation is T2's from the agreed text, written in the test's header (L-fa). So the
check sees cow copies and the paths the run takes, which a count of allocation sites in the code
cannot.

**The vector check** (Decisions 108 and 119; `tests/shape.sh`, the group `test-shape`).
`tests/shape/NAME.shape` gains the line kind `vector <target> <function> <first line> <last line>
[<op> …]`, each op one of the lane ops `add sub mul div min max sqrt neg abs cmp sel`. A candidate
is an innermost `loop` of the function (identified as the scalar lines identify theirs, L-ar) in
`sea build --target <target> --emit lir` whose body holds a lane-computing instruction (`x` or `y`
followed by a lane op; 2 lanes for `x`, 4 for `y`). It is from the line range when one of its own
records has a site of the program's file in the range, or else the nearest record with a site
before its `loop` record does: a vector body holds no failing instruction and so no site, and the
statement's checks, run before the loop, carry its line (inlined code keeps its callee's lines,
L-fl). It qualifies when its body holds every listed op (Decision 119; none listed, every candidate
qualifies). The line passes when a qualifying 2-lane loop (on `x86_64-linux` also a qualifying
4-lane loop) has, in the `-S` text between its top label and its closing branch with no other top
label inside, an instruction of the target's lane form for each of its lane ops (arm64 `.2d`/`.16b`
NEON forms, SSE2 `…pd` forms on `%xmm`, AVX2 `v…pd` forms on `%ymm`, with `xsel` as
`bsl`/`bif`/`bit`, `andnpd`, `vblendvpd`). Written: W1's bisection, `vector arm64 .main 259 265
sqrt` and the same for `x86_64` (only a loop over `shaft_safety`'s inlined body holds `sqrt`; the
split copy's loop over that body holds the same ops, so the op list does not tell the two apart: a
gap the user accepted, Decision 119, the `fusion` test showing that the fused path is the one that
runs);
W4's selection store, `vector arm64 .main 296 296 sel` and the same for `x86_64` (the store's line
in `rb_half_sweep`, inlined into `.main` at both call sites; only the store loops carry its site).
The two port lines were 251–257 and 261 when 7f wrote the shape files; the longer port headers of
9d moved them to 259–265 and 296 (`rb_half_sweep` is lines 289–298 of W4), and the `.shape` files
and this text follow (L-md). 7f's records keep the lines of their time.
7f also measured whether T9's unswitching of `shaft_safety`'s
inlined-return `do` matters for W1's speed (W1's vector body called `pow` three times per copy
where the loop without that split calls it twice, §2.12.6 "What the workloads get"): W1's compute
time was 35 ms with the split and 27 ms without it, its output byte-identical (median of 15
interleaved runs, arm64; 37 and 29 ms on the final 7f tree), so T9 no longer unswitches a `do`
(Decision 118), and `sea_pow` is called twice per copy in place of three times on both targets.

**Goldens that fusion changes** (Decision 97). Programs' outputs never change. The dump goldens of
the stages after `seaexpand` change where F1–F5, L18/L20's copying or T11–T13 apply: every test with
a `NAME.hirl` whose program has a tree `seafuse` rewrites (Decision 111), a group, a fused reduction,
a folded view or selection, or an elemental application gets a `NAME.hirf` (re-derived by hand from
F1–F5) and re-derived `NAME.hirl`, `NAME.lir1`, `NAME.lir2`, `NAME.lir3` and `NAME.lir`; every other
test with a `NAME.lir2` (29 tests: `lir4_seaopt` has a `NAME.lir2` and no `NAME.lir`) has its
`NAME.lir` renamed `NAME.lir3` and a new `NAME.lir` equal to it unless T11–T13 apply (derived by hand
when they do; the review counted about 7 such loops: `opt5_bce_range`, `opt5_bce_scope`, `opt5_cow`,
`opt5_cow_kept`, `opt5_sor`, `opt5_sr_stride`, `opt5_sr_unit`, of which T13's conditions decide
which vectorize; with Decision 115's preparation the set is larger: every vectorized loop over a fused
selection store, a unit-step slice or an inlined elemental with returns, T2 deriving each by hand).
A test whose subject is the unfused form (the agreed examples of rules 21, 22,
23, 28, L7's and L13's tests, 6c's `elem6_*` dumps of L19) keeps its subject: its statements are
separated so that no group forms and each tree is one `seafuse` leaves to L7 (an intermediate `let`
read by a `printf` of one element between the statements, which ends any group, F2 (1), and its
`.out` gains that line), and its goldens are re-derived; the others are re-derived with fusion
applied. T2 lists every changed golden with the rule that changes it (L-fb). **Per-target goldens**
(L-fc): a `seavec` dump's `x86_64-linux` golden is `NAME.lirx64` (an extension `stage.sh`'s `*.lir`
loop does not match); a hand-written `x86_64-linux`-only pass-4 test is `NAME.lirx64` with its
`.out`, run only through `seagen_x64`; a hand-written `seavec` stage test is a `NAME.lir3` without
`NAME.sea` (its subject stated in `tests/CORPUS.md`, since LIR has no comment record, L-gx), with
`NAME.lir` and `NAME.lirx64` (`stage.sh` runs `seavec` on it per target, and pass 4
on each output when a `NAME.out` exists).

### 2.13 Phase 8: linear algebra (sub-phase 8a)

**Status: agreed 2026-11-01.** This section is the specification of phase 8 of §8 (row 8,
"Linear algebra"), written as sub-phase 8a in the way 7a specified phase 7 (§2.12) and revised after
one independent review (RCOND without interchanges, Decision 125 restated and 129 added, the cross
return path, the private routines of the factorizations, the generated C header, the link-map
script, the Baysick overlap clarification, the `consts` lines in the capacity). Its questions are
**Decisions 121–129** (§2.13.11, mirrored in §9 as "Decisions of phase 8"), each decided by the user
as option (a) (2026-11-01). Its smaller readings are the lead decisions **L-ij – L-jf** (§2.13.12,
mirrored in §9 as "Lead decisions of phase 8"), agreed with the text. No code, test or contract file
changes with 8a: the contract changes are listed in "Contract changes" below and are made by the
work package WP-CONTRACT of sub-phase 8b, each with its document table in the same change (the
contract rule of §2.6). The normative sections listed in §2.13.13 are edited by WP-CONTRACT (the
tables that mirror a contract file, and the LANGUAGE.md text of §2.13.2) or by the integration of
each sub-phase (the rest), as 7b did; until each is edited, this section is the agreed specification
and those sections describe the code as built (sea commit 5e3e8e4, phase 7 complete). The Baysick
work package WP-BSK-OVERLAP (contract change 6, in the Baysick repo) is a precondition for 8c.
Decision 130 (decided by the user in 8c, 2026-11-01) amends RCOND's overflow rule (§2.13.6, L-io),
and 8c's integration corrected two facts of the text (the identity's `rcond` orders and `dlacn2`'s
sign rule, §2.13.6, §2.13.8).

#### 2.13.1 Scope

**What exists today** (read from the passes, the runtime and the contract files at 5e3e8e4):

* *Pass 1* parses the whole grammar: `A @ B` is `bin matmul` (`seaparse.bas` 11510's operator
  table), and the calls of `lu chol solve rcond eig_sym` are ordinary calls.
* *`seaname`* resolves the handle type names to the predefined types 6–9 (`sn6type.bas` 8745–8770;
  §3.5.1: 6 `Figure`, 7 `Axes`, 8 `Lu`, 9 `Chol`), reports an array of a handle type as `arrays
  cannot hold %s` (258, 9135–9150) and then every handle type node as `not supported yet: handle
  types` (9155–9198). The five library names are predeclared (`sn0main.bas` 450–470, `sc0main.bas`
  470–490).
* *`seacheck`*: the operand errors of `@` (240 for a scalar or `bool` operand, 230 for vector @
  vector) and then `not supported yet: @` for every other pair (`sc5expr.bas` `ck_bin` 10560–10625);
  `ck_lib` (`sc6call.bas` 12505–13610) has no row for the five names (its table 12595–12607), so
  each call is `not supported yet: <name>` at 12635.
* *`seafuse`* already treats `bin matmul` as a non-fusible node (`fu4fan.bas` 30260, 30773);
  *`sealoop`* has no `matmul` case (its L7 in `lp4ew.bas` would take a `bin matmul` with an array
  operand as an element-wise operator); *`sealower`* lists `matmul` among the binary operators
  (`sl0main.bas` 1095) and lowers none; no `sea.hirl` record names a library call of §10.8.
* *Contract files*: `passes.txt` has `matmul` in `binop` and `hbinop` and needs no handle record
  (types 8 and 9 are predefined, §3.5.1); `rt.inc` has `SEA_TAG_LU` 5 and `SEA_TAG_CHOL` 6, entries
  1–50 (`SEA_ENT_COUNT` 50) and no linear-algebra entry; the `entries` capacity is 64 in `sealower`,
  `seagen_a64` and `seagen_x64` (L-cs) and 399 in the `lirrw` passes; `errors.inc` has every message
  phase 8 reports (run-time 2, 10–14; compile-time 217, 230, 240, 243, 255, 258); `limits.inc` has
  `SEA_LIM_FIXED_MATMUL_E` 8.
* *Runtime*: `main` calls `_bsk_kern_init`, `_bsk_kern_use` and `_bsk_kern_variants` (§4.4) but
  nothing calls `_bsk_kern_gemm` or `_bsk_kern_gemm_sub`, which Baysick 0.6.0 provides with the IEEE
  propagation of its DESIGN.md §6.6.4 (§7.2: done); `rt_mem.s`'s `sea_free` treats any tag but
  `SEA_TAG_ARRAY` and `SEA_TAG_STR` as a corrupted object; no runtime file holds a kernel of §4.3.
  The link-map test §4.3 mentions does not exist (no script checks which Baysick members a program
  pulls).
* *Prelude*: `std.sea` holds `linspace`, `bincount`, `meshgrid`, `setdiff`; nothing of §10.8.
* *Tests*: `err_ns_matmul` and `err_ns_lib_solve` hold the two phase-8 rows of the phase rule;
  `err_ns_handle` and `res_err_handle` use `Figure` (phase 9) and stay.

**What phase 8 implements**, on both targets (row 8 of §8 and its "done when"):

* **The matrix product `@`** (LANGUAGE.md §6.2, §6.8, §10.8): matrix @ matrix through Baysick's GEMM
  (class R), matrix @ vector through Sea's GEMV kernel and vector @ matrix through Sea's 8-lane
  kernel (both class E, pinned), and `@` of two fixed-size operands evaluated inline in the pinned
  order (Decision 125).
* **The handle types `Lu` and `Chol`** (LANGUAGE.md §4.1): locals, parameters, results, tuple

* **The library functions** `lu`, `chol`, `solve` (both forms), `rcond` and `eig_sym` (both forms)
  of LANGUAGE.md §10.8, as runtime entries 51–61 (§2.13.5): LU with partial pivoting and ‖A‖₁,
  Cholesky, triangular solves with many right-hand sides, `solve(A, B)`'s choice, the `dgecon`-style
  estimator, and symmetric eigenvalues by tridiagonal reduction and implicit QL (Decision 121), the
  generalized form through `chol(M)`; blocked with the trailing updates through `_bsk_kern_gemm_sub`
  (Decision 122).
* **Sea kernel variants** (§4.4): GEMV and the 8-lane kernel in NEON, SSE2 and AVX2 forms,
  bit-identical (class E); the factorizations in one form per target, their variant dependence being
  Baysick's (L-it).
* **W2 and W3 complete** (without figures): `sea/ports/w2_truss_fem.sea` and
  `sea/ports/w3_quarter_car.sea` with their token maps, accepted by `tests/accept.sh` and by `make
  cross` under both x86_64 variants (§2.13.9, Decision 127).
* Every earlier program's output unchanged bit for bit, on both targets and both x86_64 variants.

**What W2 and W3 need** (from `workloads/w2_truss_fem.m`, `workloads/w3_quarter_car.m`):

* W2: `K(freeDof, freeDof) \ F(freeDof, :)` on the reduced 241 × 241 stiffness matrix (exactly
  symmetric: every `ke` is symmetric and `K(idx, idx) + ke` adds equal values to (i, j) and (j, i)

  lines) right-hand sides, in 96 FSD iterations and the design check: `solve(A, B)`'s Cholesky path;

  §2.2 writes it, then the solve (Decision 128); `B * Usweep` (301 × 244 @ 244 × 1 441) and `B *
  Uinf`: GEMM; `K * u0 - F0`: GEMV (class E). Everything else W2 does exists: index-vector and mask

* W3: `sin(argR) @ Ak` and `(cos(argR) * w.row) @ Ak` (16 001 × 60 @ 60): GEMV, class E, so

* **No feature gap**: unlike W7 (§6.3), neither workload needs a construct LANGUAGE.md lacks. The

**Not in phase 8**: `Figure`, `Axes` and plotting (phase 9); transposed or strided operands passed

candidate if a benchmark asks); LDLᵀ for symmetric indefinite matrices (LANGUAGE.md chose LU);
