| 10d | **Version 1.0.0** (after a 10c whose check exits 0; Decisions 79, 166, 169). **WP-VERSION** `driver/sea` (`VERSION='sea 1.0.0'`), `README.md`, `sea/CLAUDE.md`'s status and version line; the lead: §0, §1.2, §2.2, row 10 | `build/sea --version` prints `sea 1.0.0`; `make test` and `make cross` pass; no re-measurement (L-pp); **phase 10 is complete and Sea v1 is done** (§1.2) |

## 9. Decisions (agreed)

Agreed 2026-10-20: the user accepted every recommendation. Each item: the options, the option
decided, and what it affects. Everything else in LANGUAGE.md and this document follows from the
decisions; changing one changes the sections named, and is made in those documents with the
user's agreement.
Ordered by impact. (Column-major layout and the prelude's delivery are decided in the body,
LANGUAGE.md §4.5; §2.5, because no option argued otherwise.)

1. **Exactness versus speed.**
   Options: (a) **exact only**: no FMA contraction, no reassociation outside class R, Sea's own
   FMA-free elementary functions, every class-E result bit-identical on both targets (LANGUAGE.md §6.8);
   (b) exact by default plus an opt-in `--fast` build mode that allows FMA contraction and FMA-
   based elementary functions (results then differ between targets and from the exact mode);
   (c) a target-dependent class: arm64 always contracts `a * b + c` (as its compilers do by
   default), x86_64 SSE2 cannot, so outputs differ by target.
   **Cost of (a), estimated (not measured):** about 0 % on memory-bound fused loops (W1 grid,
   W4 half sweeps, W5 stack-ups); up to 10–20 % on compute-bound scalar chains (W4's SOR update
   has two candidate contractions, an estimated ~15 % on that loop; W3's RK4 several); and
   elementary functions without FMA about 10–30 % slower per call than FMA-based ones. Whether
   MATLAB's own JIT contracts is not known, so (a) does not necessarily reproduce MATLAB
   better; it reproduces *itself* across targets.
   **Decided: (a) for v1**, and revisit (b) with phase-10 measurements: the speed goal
   has an estimated margin on every workload (§5.5), byte-identical outputs on both targets
   make every test simpler and stronger, and (b) can be added later without changing any
   program. Affects LANGUAGE.md §6.8, §10.4; §4.5, §5, §6.6.
2. **Baysick growth policy and the number of passes.**
   Options: (a) the policy of §7.3 (restructure first, grow Baysick only on a measured need,
   prefer Dartmouth precedent, else a labelled extension), with eight compiler programs (§2.1)
   and no Baysick language change now; (b) raise Baysick's line limit and add a `COMMON` block
   now, before the compiler exists, so passes can be fewer and larger; (c) forbid any Baysick
   change: the compiler must fit Baysick 0.6.0 as it is, whatever the number of passes.
   **Decided: (a).** The calibration (§2.7) says Baysick 0.6.0 is sufficient with an
   estimated 26 000–42 000 lines in eight programs, but the estimate is ±50 %; (a) commits to
   nothing unmeasured and pre-agrees how a measured need is handled. (Recalibrated in phase 1
   from the real passes: about 42 000–53 000 lines, with pass 2a reaching the 10 000-line
   limit around phase 6 and pass 3a near it from phase 7, §2.7; the pre-agreed response is to
   split them, §7.3.) Affects §2.1, §2.7, §7.
3. **Index base.**
   Options: (a) 0-based with half-open ranges `a..b`; (b) 1-based with inclusive ranges, like
   MATLAB and Baysick's MAT. **Decided: (a).** It matches the C/Rust family Sea's syntax
   comes from, half-open ranges compose without `±1`, linear and DOF indices are plain products.
   Cost: ports add 1 to exported indices, which the acceptance checks catch structurally
   (§6.3). Affects LANGUAGE.md §5, every example, LANGUAGE.md Appendix D.
4. **Array semantics.**
   Options: (a) values (copy-on-write) with explicit `ref` parameters for in-place updates, and
   runtime handle types for figures and factorizations; (b) references (NumPy-like aliasing);
   (c) ownership and borrowing (Rust-like moves). **Decided: (a).** MATLAB users'
   expectations, no aliasing bugs, O(1) passing, and `ref` makes in-place updates explicit and
   checkable. (c) is the fastest in theory but adds a borrow checker to a compiler written in
   BASIC. Affects LANGUAGE.md §4.1, §4.5, §8.2–§8.3; §4.2.
5. **Kernel sharing and Baysick's GEMM contract.**
   Options: (a) link Baysick's `libbaysickrt.a` for GEMM and grow Baysick's kernel contract by
   the update entry and IEEE propagation of §7.2; Sea owns every other kernel; (b) Sea writes
   and owns its own GEMM (both targets, all variants), no Baysick change; (c) move all matrix
   kernels into a third shared repository used by both. **Decided: (a).** One copy of the
   hardest kernel (the register-blocked GEMM in three variants), a small and testable change to
   Baysick (the micro-kernel loading `C` instead of zero), no new repository. Cost: a
   cross-repository contract (`include/runtime.inc`, §2.6) and a Baysick change before phase 8.
   (b) costs an estimated 2 000–4 000 assembly lines per target. Affects §2.6, §4.3–§4.4,
   §7.2.
6. **Elementary functions: own or host, and which in v1.**
   Options: (a) Sea's own `log exp sin cos pow hypot` (≤ 1 ulp, identical bits on every target,
   scalar and SIMD), only these in v1 (LANGUAGE.md §10.4, LANGUAGE.md §10.13); (b) the host libm (Apple libm, glibc),
   like Baysick; (c) (a) with the full C set (`tan asin … tanh log2 log10`) in v1.
   **Decided: (a).** It makes every output except linear algebra byte-identical across
   targets (W1, W4, W5 entirely), and fused SIMD loops need vector forms, which the host libms do
   not provide on both targets. Six functions are what the workloads use; each further function
   is weeks of careful work and is added when a program needs it. With (b), §6.6 loses the byte identity of W1/W5 and
   LANGUAGE.md §6.8 gains a host-dependent class. Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.4; §4.5, §6.6,
   §8 phase 3.
7. **Changes to `sea/workloads/` and a MATLAB rerun.**
   Options: (a) change `sea/workloads/`: `compare.py --candidate` with the own-extremum rule
   (§6.3); `run_all.m` writes each report to `reference/<name>.txt` with `diary` on the last
   repetition, takes `nRepeat` ≥ 5, and records `maxNumCompThreads` and the machine model; then
   the **user reruns MATLAB once** (with the default thread count, and once more with
   `maxNumCompThreads(1)` for a single-threaded comparison), regenerating the reference files;
   (b) only `compare.py --candidate`, no rerun: reports are compared by hand, timings against the
   current 3-run multithreaded baseline. **Decided: (a).** Without stored MATLAB reports
   §6.4 cannot be automated, and the current baseline's variance (W2: 1.05–1.74 s) makes a
   best-of-3 comparison noisy. Which baseline (default or single-threaded) is the pass
   criterion is part of this decision; decided: the default-threaded one, as users run
   MATLAB, with the single-threaded one reported. Affects §1.2, §5.7, §6.3–§6.5. **Done**
   (2026-10-21, sea commit c1736f7): the user's rerun on an M2 Pro with MATLAB R2026a committed
   `workloads/reference/<name>.txt` for the five workloads, `baseline_timings_matlab.json`
   (default threads) and `baseline_timings_matlab_1thread.json`.
8. **Typing strictness and untyped integer literals.**
   Options: (a) static, signatures annotated, locals inferred, only `i64 → f64` implicit, untyped
   integer constants typed by context and a `var` initialised by one typed by its assignments
   (LANGUAGE.md §4.2); (b) as (a) but untyped integer constants always `i64` unless used directly with an
   `f64` (so `var dMax = 0` followed by `dMax = d` is a type error asking for `0.0`); (c) all
   numbers `f64`, no `i64` (MATLAB's model). **Decided: (a).** It gives MATLAB
   programmers the obvious meaning of `var dMax = 0` and still keeps integer counters `i64`; the
   cost is one flow-insensitive pass over each function's assignments. Affects LANGUAGE.md §4.2, §4.10, §9.1.
9. **Vectors as their own rank.**
   Options: (a) rank-1 `T[]` distinct from rank-2 `T[,]`, orientation written with `.col`/`.row`
   where broadcasting needs it; (b) MATLAB's model, everything 2-D. **Decided: (a).**
   Static loop shapes, no orientation bugs; the price is writing `.col`/`.row` in the rare
   outer-product broadcasts (W3's road grid). Affects LANGUAGE.md §4.5, §5, §6.3, §6.9.
10. **Shape polymorphism.**
    Options: (a) `elemental fn`; (b) generic functions over array shapes; (c) every scalar
    function implicitly elemental. **Decided: (a).** Covers every workload use, keeps
    type checking simple, and is the form fusion needs; (c) hides allocation and loops behind
    ordinary-looking calls. Affects LANGUAGE.md §8.5; §5.1.
11. **Surface syntax.**
    Options, as a package: (a) `*` element-wise, `@` matrix product, `.T` transpose,
    `solve(A, B)`; `^` right-associative binding tighter than unary minus; newline-terminated
    statements with the three rules of LANGUAGE.md §3.7; (b) MATLAB's `.*` / `*` / `'` / `\`, left-associative
    `^`, `;` required. Individual items can be changed. **Decided: (a).** One meaning per
    symbol removes MATLAB's commonest bug (`*` for `.*`); `\` reads as an escape in a C-like
    language; right-associative `^` is the mathematical convention; newline statements read
    cleanly in long engineering scripts, and the one trap (a line starting with a binary
    operator) is a compile error. Affects LANGUAGE.md §3.7, §6.1–§6.2, Appendix A.
12. **Can bounds checks be disabled?**
    Options: (a) no: always on, eliminated by analysis; (b) a `--unchecked` build option;
    (c) a per-block `unchecked { }` construct. **Decided: (a)** for v1. The checks that
    survive elimination are a compare and an untaken branch off the critical path; an option
    would create a second behaviour to test. If phase 10 shows a workload losing more than 5 %
    to checks, revisit with that measurement. Affects LANGUAGE.md §5.4; §5.2.
13. **Plot format and fidelity.**
    Options: (a) SVG with embedded PNG images, geometry specified (LANGUAGE.md §12.5) but v1 tests structural
    plus cross-target byte identity; (b) as (a) with every SVG byte specified and hand-derived
    byte-exact plot tests; (c) PNG files through a rasterizer. **Decided: (a).** It
    tests what matters for v1 (the right figure, deterministic on both targets) without
    freezing layout details before anyone has looked at the figures; (b) can follow without an
    API change. Affects LANGUAGE.md §12; §6.2.
14. **Program arguments for the workloads' flags.**
    Options: (a) `args()` returns the command-line arguments, and the ports take
    `--export-reference` and `--figures` (LANGUAGE.md Appendix D); (b) `getenv`, keeping the workloads'
    environment variables `SEA_EXPORT_REFERENCE`, `SEA_PLOT`, `SEA_SAVE_FIGURES`; (c) both.
    **Decided: (a).** Arguments are explicit at the call site and need one tiny library
    function; environment variables leak into child processes and are invisible in a command
    line. The acceptance and benchmark scripts pass the flags. Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.10, Appendix D; §6.3, §6.5.
15. **File extension and command name.**
    Options: (a) `.sea` and `sea`; (b) `.sea` and `seac`; (c) another name.
    **Decided: (a).** Short and obvious; check for a clash with an existing `sea` command
    on the user's systems before release. Affects §2.2, tests, docs.
16. **`pow` in `const` items** (raised by phase 3's design, §4.10.5). LANGUAGE.md §7.2 lets a constant use `^` with the run time's bits, and pass 2a
    evaluates every constant to one literal, so a `^` that is not a `powk` needs `pow` at compile
    time. Options: (a) `FEPOW` in `f64emu.bas`: the operation sequence of §4.10.4 on the exact
    IEEE emulation, with the tables from a generated `DATA` block `mtab`; bit-identical to the
    runtimes by construction and tested against the same vectors; about 400–600 Baysick lines
    and 110 `DATA` lines in pass 2a (and 2b, unless it is a separate module), bringing pass 2a's
    pre-agreed split (§2.7) forward by about a phase; no language change; (b) such a `^` is
    `not a constant expression` (LANGUAGE.md §7.2 changes; constants keep `powk`, `sqrt` and
    the arithmetic operators), no compiler cost, and a program writes a `let` (not visible inside
    functions) or `sqrt` instead; (c) evaluate such constants at program start (changes "every
    `const` is evaluated at compile time", Decision U2 in §0, and needs a new kind of global).
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21): it keeps the language as agreed, and its cost lands
    where pass 2a's split is already planned. A `const` may use `^` and the call `pow`
    (LANGUAGE.md §7.2 now lists `pow` beside `sqrt`); `log exp sin cos hypot` stay outside
    constant expressions; pass 2b still folds no `pow` (§3.5.7). Affects LANGUAGE.md §7.2;
    §2.6.3, §2.7, §3.5.2, §3.5.5, §4.10.5, §4.10.6.
17. **Shape of the split of pass 2a** (raised by phase 4's plan, §2.7: phase 4 takes the one
    program to 8 900–10 200 lines). Options: (a) **resolve, then type**: a new program `seaname`
    (`sea.ast` → `sea.res`) resolves names and scopes, checks items and signatures and evaluates
    constants and constant exponents, and `seacheck` (`sea.res` → `sea.hir1`) types, checks the
    rest and emits; `seacheck` sheds the exact arithmetic (`limb`, `f64emu`, `FEPOW`, `mtab`), and
    both stay below 9 000 lines after phase 4; it costs a new intermediate format, `--emit res`,
    `.res` goldens and an error hand-over between the programs; (b) **declarations, then bodies**:
    a smaller format, but the body checker keeps the arithmetic modules and reaches the limit
    again around v1; (c) **typing, then the late checks and emission**: moves about 1 000 lines,
    too few. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). Affects §2.1, §2.2, §2.6.2, §2.6.3, §2.7,
    §2.10, §3, §3.4.1, §6.2, §8.
18. **Prelude functions in phase 4** (`linspace`, `bincount`, and `meshgrid`, `setdiff`).
    Options: (a) **inline prelude calls in pass 3a in phase 4**: the inlined-call form (a return
    becomes the exit of a block, parameters bound to the arguments, run-time error sites mapped to
    the program's call, §3.6.4) is brought forward from phase 6 for prelude calls only; phase 6
    reuses it for the inlining rule of LANGUAGE.md §8.6, and the inlining of user functions stays
    in phase 6; (b) move them into the runtime on both targets, changing their (P) marks in
    LANGUAGE.md §10; (c) compile prelude functions as LIR functions with a hidden call-site
    argument, changing the "Sites" rule of §3.6.4. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21).
    Affects §3.6.6 (in 4b), §2.7, §8.
19. **How phase 4's numeric "done when" is checked** (no `write_json` before phase 6). Options:
    (a) **the acceptance programs print a JSON subset with `printf("%.17g")`, and the workload
    repository's `compare.py` gains `--keys k1,k2,…`** (the same rules, restricted to those keys);
    the Linux host is checked by byte identity with the Mac's output; (b) a shell checker in
    `tests/` that re-implements the rules for the listed keys; (c) only hand-derived spec tests in
    phase 4, the workload numbers moved to phase 6. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21).
    Affects §6.3 (in 4b), §8; `sea/workloads/reference_py/compare.py`.
20. **Array literals of `str` or struct elements.** LANGUAGE.md §6.9 makes a row of scalars a
    fixed-size array, and `str` and structs are not scalars. Options: (a) **such literals are
    dynamic** (`str[]`, `S[]`); fixed-size `str` and struct arrays exist by annotation; (b) they
    are fixed-size like numbers; (c) fixed up to 256 elements of any kind, dynamic beyond.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). LANGUAGE.md §4.5 and §6.9 gain one sentence in 4b.
21. **Named options of library functions in phase 4.** Options: (a) **the library options
    (`desc:`, `dim:`) in phase 4**; named and default arguments of user functions stay in phase 6
    (the phase-rule row becomes "a named argument of a user function"); (b) all named arguments in
    phase 6, so phase 4 has ascending sorts only and no `dim:` reductions; (c) all named and
    default arguments in phase 4. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). Affects §2.6.2 (in
    4b), §8.
22. **Which whole-array operations are runtime calls.** Options: (a) **inline LIR for element-wise
    loops, reductions, indexing, gathers and scatters, mask compaction, `find*`, concatenation
    and projections; the runtime only for memory, copy on write and freeing, strings,
    `sort`/`argsort`, `args` and `error`**: the inline loops are what phase 7 fuses and
    vectorizes, and the pinned orders are exact in LIR by construction; (b) a generic runtime
    layer of strided descriptors and per-operation entries; (c) (a) with the variable-length
    results (`find`, `x[m]`, concatenation) in the runtime. **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-21). Affects §3.6.6, §4.8 (in 4b).
23. **Scope edges of phase 4.** Options: (a) **include the exact math functions `abs sign sqrt
    floor ceil trunc round min max where isnan`, `ind2sub`/`sub2ind`, `lower`, `str(x)`,
    `meshgrid` and `setdiff`; leave `%` with an `f64` operand (the exact `fmod`) to phase 6** as
    a phase-rule row; (b) only what the "done when" needs (the math functions), the rest in phase
    6; (c) everything, `f64 %` included. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). Affects §2.6.2
    (in 4b), §8.
24. **A heap-leak check for tests.** Options: (a) **`SEA_HEAP_CHECK=1` in the environment makes
    the runtime write the number of live dynamic objects to standard error at a normal exit**, a
    test aid, not a language feature; tests set it through a `.meta` line; (b) no leak check.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). Affects §4.5, §4.8, §6.2 (in 4b).
25. **Constants that read a constant without a value** (raised by the review of 4a's
    specification). The single program evaluated a constant whose check found no error even when
    it named a constant whose check or evaluation had failed, and reported an `integer overflow`
    of that evaluation if the overflow came, in evaluation order, before the read of the failed
    constant (`const B = 9223372036854775807 + 1 + A` with `const A: i64 = 1 + x` reported
    `1:11: integer overflow`, not `A`'s `undeclared name 'x'`). Splitting pass 2a would have to
    reproduce that order in two programs. Options: (a) **a constant that names a constant without
    a value, or whose type is an error type, is not evaluated and gives no further error**: the
    error reported is the one that caused the missing value, and `seaname` needs to replicate no
    check (§3.4.1); (b) keep the evaluation order and replicate the checks of constants in
    `seaname`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-21). It is made in the single `seacheck`
    first, as its own change (sub-phase 4a-0, §8), with its tests (§6.2). Affects LANGUAGE.md
    §7.2; §3.4.1, §3.5.2, §6.2, §8.
    **Refined (2026-10-21, found by the 4a implementation; the user to be told):** "whose type is
    an error type" covers any part of the expression whose type is in error, and a call of a
    function item named `pow` or `sqrt` (an error already, `redefinition of predeclared name`)
    also leaves the constant unevaluated (LANGUAGE.md §7.2; §3.4.1 rule 2, §3.5.2). Without it
    `seaname`, which evaluates only what it can type, would have to type every node a faulty
    declaration poisons. It differs from the single program (and from 4a-0) only in programs
    that already have an error in an item or a signature, and there only where a constant
    without an error of its own holds such a part yet got a value or an evaluation error: by
    `&&`/`||` not reaching the part (`const B: bool = false && f() == 1.0`, f faulty: no value
    now, `false` before), or by an `i64` overflow or division by zero evaluated before it. The
    first error then changes when that value or evaluation error made an error earlier in source
    order: with `const D = B || 9223372036854775807 + 1 > 0` before `B`, the single program
    reports `D`'s overflow (1:16), the rule reports `f`'s error. Applied by 4a's `seacheck` (§8);
    tests in §6.2.
26. **The seam of the split of pass 3a** (raised by the size gate after 4d, §2.7: projected 9 665
    lines). Options: (a) **`sealoop` is HIR→HIR**: it rewrites the array constructs into explicit
    scalar loops with a small set of primitive HIR records (§3.5.9: `xblk tmp hloop ext adat eld est
    anew wbin`, from 4e `chkb chk rcnt cow mcpy cdat`), and `sealower` keeps all LIR emission,
    lowering each primitive to exactly the LIR §3.6.6 already gives; (b) `sealoop` emits the array
    code as LIR fragments inside the HIR stream (symbolic registers, blocks and labels that
    `sealower` renumbers and splices); (c) another split: ownership as its own pass, or a LIR macro
    expander after `sealower`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22). It is the seam §2.7 planned,
    it leaves `sea.lir1` unchanged (checked by hand on the examples of rules 17, 20, 22 and 30), it
    keeps one LIR emitter, and it puts the array rules, rule 37 and phase 6–7 inlining and fusion
    where they are tree operations. (b) gives similar sizes with a much harder third format; (c)
    leaves the array growth in `sealower`. Affects §2.1, §2.2, §2.6.3, §2.7, §2.10, §3, §3.5.9,
    §3.6.6, §3.9, §6.2, §8; `passes.txt`; the driver.
27. **Where ownership and evaluation order live after the split.** Options: (a) **in `sealower`**:
    rules 12 (the copies before a `ref` call), 15, 16 and 31 (deferred `ref` arguments) as before;
    `sealoop`'s temporaries take part through the rules T1–T3 of §3.5.9 (a `tmp` of a plain local
    is another name for it; an `xblk`'s owned temporaries are released right after its value, the
    value's own moved out); (b) `sealoop` writes the reference counts explicitly (`retain` and
    `release` statements, the releases on every exit) and the rule-12 copies and rule-31 deferrals
    as HIR, so `sealower` knows nothing of counts; (c) the rule-12 copies in `sealoop`, ownership in
    `sealower`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22). Owned or borrowed depends on how `sealower`
    lowers a node, the 4d dumps and the heap check pin every `retain` and `release`, and `sealoop`
    needs no count knowledge. Affects §3.5.9, §3.6.6 rules 12, 15 (k), 16.
28. **What 4d code moves in 4e-0.** Options: (a) **rule 17's constructors and fill loops (`zeros
    ones filled`), `len rows cols numel` and rule 30 (`for` over a vector)**, so that the primitives
    are proven byte-exact on the existing dumps before 4e builds on them; (b) nothing: `sealoop`
    starts as a validating copy; (c) also the scalar indexing (rules 18, 19, `$`) and the `ref`
    element paths (rule 31). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22). Affects §3.5.9 (L1–L4), §3.6.6
    rules 17 and 30, §6.2, §8.
29. **How much the 4e-0 specification fixes.** Options: (a) **the primitive records for 4e and 4f
    now** (codes 72–87) and the rewrites of what 4e-0 moves; the rewrites of rules 20–25, 26
    (numeric literals) and 28 at the start of 4e and 4f, those of 26 (`str` and struct literals), 29
    and 30 (`str` and struct elements) and the other records of 4g, and those of 4h, at theirs, the LIR of
    §3.6.6 staying as agreed (so the user is asked again only if an agreed LIR example must
    change); (b) everything for 4e–4h now; (c) only the records 4e-0 uses (72–81). **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-22). Affects §3.5.9, §8 (the first step of 4e, 4f, 4g and 4h).
30. **Name of the new intermediate file.** Options: (a) **`sea.hirl`, `--emit hirl`** (HIR with
    the loops explicit); (b) `sea.hir2`, `--emit hir2`; (c) `sea.loop`, `--emit loop`. **Decided:
    (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22): a HIR variant (the same records plus set `HL`), and the suffix `1`
    keeps meaning the first version of a format (`hir1`, `lir1`). Affects §2.2, §3, §6.2, `CLAUDE.md`.
31. **How the agreed LIR is expressed with the fixed `sea.hirl` records** (raised by the 4e
    specification: the set `HL` cannot write a fixed-size home slot, a `bool` used as 0 or 1,
    rcount's E as a condition, stores at `- 0 off`, or the mutable counters of rules 20, 21, 25
    and 26). Options: (a) **refinements of the existing records and their validation, R1–R10 of
    §3.5.9** (R11, an owned `tmp` directly in a block `sealoop` writes released at its end, was added
    on review of the specification as a refinement of the same kind): `anew` of a fixed-size type with r = 0 is a home slot, `adat` of a fixed-size array
    is no instruction, a `ci` index of `eld`/`est` gives `- 0 off`, the children of `cdat` are
    data, `est` stores any numeric element, rcnt's `e` is a `bool`, `wbin` takes `bool` operands,
    scalar `.l` locals bound by `bind` and assigned by `asg`, array `.l` locals bound in the
    blocks `sealoop` writes, T3 not for fixed-size values, `sealower` rejecting every array
    expression; no new record or field, `passes.txt` unchanged; (b) new records 88 and later
    (`home`, a bool-to-integer node, a constant-offset store), a format change with the same LIR;
    (c) fixed-size construction left in `sealower`, duplicating loop code there. **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-22): every agreed example comes out exactly, the contract text changes but
    no format does. Affects §3.5.9, §3.6.6 ("Lowering of the `sea.hirl` records").
32. **Rule 27 (fixed-size arrays in memory) in 4e or 4g** (the phase-rule step 4e makes every
    fixed-size array construct legal, while §8 listed rule 27 under 4g). Options: (a) **4e
    implements rule 27 for fixed-size `f64`, `i64` and `bool` arrays completely — homes, copies,
    assignment, arguments, `ref` arguments, results through hidden addresses, several results,
    `ifx`, `dyn`, `fix` — and 4g adds structs and reference elements on the same machinery**; (b)
    fixed-size results and tuple components unsupported until 4g (a phase-rule row for them); (c)
    fixed-size arrays only as locals and literals in 4e. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22):
    it is what the phase-rule table already says, W2's and W3's element functions need fixed-size
    results, and the hidden-result code is written once. Affects §3.6.6 rule 27, §6.2, §8 (4e,
    4g), §2.7.
33. **`ind2sub` with array arguments** (two results; rule 22 has one; W4 needs `[hj, hi] =
    ind2sub(size(T), holeIdx)`). Options: (a) **two element-wise loops (`k % r`, then `idiv(k, r)`)
    over held arguments** (§3.5.9 L11), observably identical to one loop, fused in phase 7; (b) one
    loop writing both arrays; (c) deferred to phase 6 with the multiple-result elemental functions.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22). **Refined** (lead decision, 2026-10-22, on review): the
    two loops are exact only for a scalar `r` (the same errors at the same element); with an array
    `r` (`ind2sub` is elemental) they would change the order of errors and of the shape check, so
    `ind2sub` with an array first argument stays the phase-rule word `ind2sub` (at the `call`) until
    phase 6 brings the multiple-result elemental functions (§2.6.2). Affects §3.5.9, §3.6.6 rule 22,
    §2.6.2, §6.2.
34. **Index vectors that share the target's buffer in a selection store** (`v[v] = 0`, `v[v] += 1`
    on an `i64[]`: rule 21 as first written read the indices from the buffer its stores were
    changing). Options: (a) **a borrowed index vector of a store whose target is an `i64` array is
    retained like the value and released after the store, so that the target's copy on write
    copies a shared buffer**; (b) every index vector of a store copied; (c) unchanged. **Decided:
    (a)** (lead decision, 2026-10-22, required by LANGUAGE.md §5.5: the indices are evaluated before
    any element is stored; rule 21's agreed example, a `bool` mask of an `f64` target, is
    unchanged). For a fixed-size target, which has no copy on write, the same rule copies an index
    vector that is the target variable itself into a new home (lead decision of the same date).
    Affects §3.6.6 rule 21, §3.5.9 L6, §6.2.
35. **The size gate after 4f, after the split of pass 3a** (§2.7's ×1.5 gate after 4f belonged to
    the branch without the split, and `sealower` is above its 5 000-line trigger). Options: (a)
    **a per-program gate after 4f** for `sealoop`, `sealower` and `seacheck`: built lines ≤ 7 000,
    projected v1 size ≤ 9 000, at least 2 free array letters; a failure schedules that program's
    split before 4g; (b) the old formula and thresholds; (c) no gate before 4h. **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-22). Affects §2.7, §8 (4f).
36. **Where an untyped `[]` gets its type, and where 252 is reported** (raised by the second
    review of the 4e specification: LANGUAGE.md §6.9 required a type from context without listing
    the contexts, and error 252's position kind `binding` had no place for `len([])` or `[] + v`).
    Options: (a) **the contexts listed in LANGUAGE.md §6.9 (a binding's declared type, an
    assignment target, a user function's parameter, a `return`'s result type, the other arm of an
    `if` expression with an array type, a struct field's type), anywhere else 252 at the `[]`; the
    position kind of 252 becomes `expr`**, so an unannotated `let x = []` reports at the `[` too;
    (b) the kind stays `binding`, other positions a new code; (c) left open. **Decided: (a)** (lead
    decision, 2026-10-22, to be reported to the user). No pass reads the position kind of an error
    record (it is documentation that `check-contracts` compares), and no test has a 252 golden, so
    the change of `include/errors.inc` needs no code or test change with it. Affects
    `include/errors.inc`, §2.6.2, §3.5.5, §6.2, §8 (4e), LANGUAGE.md §6.9.
37. **Conversions and selection or `.flat` targets in a tuple assignment** (raised by the review
    of the 4e build: LANGUAGE.md §4.2 (b), (c) and §4.5 promise the conversions of assignment in
    every assignment, but the `tasg` record carried only a scalar `i64` → `f64` flag, and the build
    rejected or crashed on the other cases). Options: (a) **each target is stored exactly as `ti =
    ri` would store result i, after the call, in target order: the `cv` field of `tasg` (format
    unchanged, `u`) widens to the sum of 1 (`i64` → `f64`, scalar or element by element), 2 (`dyn`)
    and 4 (`fix`); `seacheck` checks each component with `asg set`'s rules (217 and 201 at the
    target; a selection target takes an array of its rank or a scalar, either of its element type
    or `i64` for `f64`); `sealoop`'s new rewrite L12 binds every result to a `.l` local by one `tbind` and stores
    each target by an `asg set` of it, converted, which the other rewrites then lower**; (b) route
    only the converting or selection targets through locals (stores out of order); (c) reject such
    tuple assignments. **Decided: (a)** (lead decision, 2026-10-22, to be reported to the user).
    Affects LANGUAGE.md §7.3, §3.5.5 (`tasg`, implicit `dyn` and `fix`), §3.5.9 (L12, R8, R10, the
    validation), §3.6.6 rules 12 and 15 (j), §6.2.
38. **How rules 23 and 24 are written with the fixed `sea.hirl` records** (raised by the 4f
    specification: the set `HL` has no `iand` for rule 23's lane, no type for its 64-byte
    accumulator home, and rule 2 writes a `mov` where rule 23's example writes the destination

    accumulator `.l` local; `wbin and`; the appended type `f64[8]`; `asg set` of a counter with a

    kind; `passes.txt` gains one enumeration word (`wop … and`)**; (b) the same with `bin band` on
    `i64` operands instead of `wbin and`, `passes.txt` unchanged (`band` then meaning two things); (c)
    new `HL` records 88 and later (`slot`, `rcall`, an accumulator form), a format change with the
    same LIR. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22): every agreed example (rules 23, 24) comes out

39. **Result types of library calls on fixed-size arguments** (LANGUAGE.md said nothing). Options:
    (a) **`dim:` reductions of a fixed-size matrix give a fixed-size vector (a home, no heap);
    `sort` and `argsort` of a fixed-size vector give the dynamic `T[]`/`i64[]` (the runtime sorts heap
    vectors: pass 2a writes a `dyn`); `find` is always dynamic**; (b) all of them dynamic; (c) all
    fixed in, fixed out (`sort` and `argsort` copying to the heap and back). **Decided: (a)** (the

40. **Sorting `str` vectors in 4f** (§6.2's 4f list asked for it, while `str[]` is the phase-rule
    word `strings` until 4g). Options: (a) **`rt_sort.s` implements `f64`, `i64` and `str` in 4f (the
    whole contract of §4.8), the `str` path tested in `tests/rt` on both targets, the `sort_str`

    §6.2, §8 (4f, 4g).
41. **A positional argument after a named one** (`sort(desc: true, v)`: LANGUAGE.md §8.1 put
    positional arguments first but named no error, and Appendix A accepted the order). Options: (a)
    **a new compile error `positional argument after a named argument`, reported by pass 1 at the
    argument** (`errors.inc` one entry, LANGUAGE.md §8.1 and an Appendix A note, about 15 lines of
    `seaparse`); (b) a syntax error: Appendix A's `call_args` puts named arguments last and pass 1
    reports `unexpected token '…'`; (c) allowed, positional arguments binding in order wherever
    they stand. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-22): the clearest message, covering user

    `C1`, at `token`): pass 1's codes are 100–199 (§2.6.2, checked by `tests/include_asserts.inc`), so
    the number 264 named while deciding could not be used. Affects LANGUAGE.md §8.1, Appendix A;
    §2.6.2, `errors.inc`, §6.2.
42. **The order of an `i64` `sum`** (raised by the review of the 4f specification: LANGUAGE.md
    §10.5 said "exact with an overflow check (order irrelevant)", while rule 23's agreed sequence
    `iaddc R R x` checks every partial sum in index order, so `[2⁶², 2⁶², −2⁶²]` overflows although
    its total fits). Options: (a) **LANGUAGE.md follows the agreed rule: the elements are added in
    index order from 0, and an overflow of any partial sum is `integer overflow`; `mean`, `variance`
    and `std` of an `i64` vector use that sum**; (b) an exact sum (a 128-bit or wider accumulator)
    with one check of the total, changing rule 23. **Decided: (a)** (lead decision, 2026-10-22, to be
    reported to the user): the agreed LIR stays, and the result is the same on both targets.
    Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.5; §6.2.
43. **Options of library functions are named only** (raised by the same review: LANGUAGE.md §8.1
    allowed a positional argument for any parameter). Options: (a) **the options of a library function
    (`dim:`, `desc:`, `style:`) are given only by name; a positional argument in their place is `no
    overload` (243, §2.6.2)**; (b) options also by position. **Decided: (a)** (lead decision,

    "Readings fixed by 4f" already checks. Affects LANGUAGE.md §8.1, §10.
44. **How 4g's operations are written with the fixed `sea.hirl` records** (raised by the 4g
    specification: the set `HL` cannot write a replacing store of a reference element, the address
    of a struct element, a struct copied into an element or written in place there, the retains
    after a copy of reference elements, struct homes, a field loaded through an element's address,
    an owned `match` scrutinee released on `break`, `continue` and `return`, the copy on write of
    an array field, or rule 15 (j)'s moves through L12's locals). Options: (a) **refinements in the
    style of Decisions 31 and 38, R17–R25 of §3.5.9, with no new record kind and `passes.txt`
    unchanged, and three new `sealoop` rewrites: L15 projection, L16 `match`, L17 every store of a

    records 88 and later (a `retain`, an address record, a struct copy): explicit, a format change,
    the same LIR. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): the agreed examples of rules 26, 29, 30
    and 33 come out exactly through `sealoop`, and `sealower` stays as small as possible. Affects
    §3.5.9 (R17–R25, L15–L17, the extensions of L2–L14, the validation), §3.6.6 (rules 15 (k), 19, 26–30,
    33, 38 and "Lowering of the `sea.hirl` records"), §8.
45. **Element-wise operators on `str` arrays** (LANGUAGE.md §6.4 made the comparisons element-wise
    on arrays, §6.2 made `+` element-wise "on arrays", but §6.3's result-type rule did not mention
    `str`; no workload uses either). Options: (a) **comparisons and `+` element-wise on `str` arrays,
    with broadcasting (`names == "x"`, `names + "!"`), through L7; §6.3's result type gains `str`
    for `+`**; (b) comparisons only, `+` with a `str` array operand 240; (c) neither in v1, 240 for

    pinned the comparisons, and `+` costs nothing more in L7. Affects LANGUAGE.md §6.2–§6.4; §2.6.2
    ("Readings fixed by 4g"), §3.5.9 (L7), §6.2.
46. **The domains of `str(x)` and `lower(s)`** (LANGUAGE.md §10.9 listed `str` of `i64`, `f64` and
    `bool` and `lower` of a `str`, but said neither whether `str` of a `str` is allowed, as `f64(f64)`
    is, nor whether either is elemental like `f64()` and `i64()`). Options: (a) **scalars only: `str`
    of an `i64`, `f64`, `bool` or `str` (a `str` returned unchanged), `lower` of a `str`; an array
    argument is 243**; (b) as (a) but `str` of a `str` is 243; (c) both elemental too (`str(v)` a
    `str[]`, `lower` of a `str[]` a `str[]`). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): it matches
    phase-1 decision 2 (the identity conversions) and keeps the library at what the workloads use.
    Pass 2a writes `str(s)` of a `str` as s itself (§3.5.5). Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.9; §2.6.2,
    §3.5.5, §3.6.6 (rule 32), §6.2.
47. **4g in one step or two, and its size gate** (`sealower` had 913 lines left under 7 000 built
    lines and its 4g increment was estimated at 800–1 360, §2.7). Options: (a) **one specification
    step (this one), then two build sub-steps: 4g-1 (strings, `match`, `error`, `args`, `str`,
    `lower`, `str` elements, `sort_str`) and 4g-2 (structs, records, projection, fixed-size `str`
    and struct arrays, `manualD_part1`), with a size gate after 4g-1 that re-projects `sealower`
    from its measured increment; if 4g-2 would take it past 7 000 built lines, a relief (more
    `sealoop` rewrites, a compaction with no change of behaviour, or a split) is specified and
    agreed before 4g-2**; (b) one 4g with the gate after it (`sealower` may end above 7 000, the
    relief then coming before 4h); (c) `sealower`'s cap raised to 8 000 built lines (its projected
    v1 ≤ 9 000 unchanged), one 4g. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): `sealower`'s estimate
    after 4g (6 887–7 447) straddles 7 000, and 4g-1 measures the shared ownership machinery before
    the struct half commits to its design. Affects §2.6.2 (the phase-rule rows 4g-1 and 4g-2), §2.7
    (the projection and the gate after 4g-1), §6.2, §8 (rows 4g-1 and 4g-2).
48. **The scope of anonymous records** (LANGUAGE.md §4.6: a record "can be bound with `let`/`var`,
    read with `.f`, and passed to `write_json`", either a closed list or examples). Options: (a)
    **records are anonymous struct types wherever no type name is written: bound, read, fields
    assigned when `var`, nested, array literal elements and `filled`, `if` arms, the projection of
    a record array, element loops**; (b) only the uses §4.6 listed (bind, `.f` read, nesting,
    `write_json`): a field assignment 239, an array of records 258 `arrays cannot hold {…}`.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): no new errors, and records reuse the struct machinery
    at no cost. Affects LANGUAGE.md §4.6; §2.6.2, §3.5.9 (R21, records with structs throughout),
    §3.6.6 (rule 38), §6.2.

**Lead decisions of 4g** (2026-10-23, within Decisions 44–48, each taken because one answer is
clearly right, to be reported to the user; each is written into its normative section):
L-a, `match is not exhaustive` (207) at the `match` exactly when its last arm is not `_` (a `match`
without arms included), and `unreachable pattern` (208) at every arm after a `_` arm and at every
arm with a pattern equal to an earlier one, both by `seacheck`, in plain source order (LANGUAGE.md
§7.6; §2.6.2 "Readings fixed by 4g"); L-b, in a record literal a repeated name is 205 and `T`,
`flat`, `col`, `row` 222, by `seacheck` at the `init`, 204 and 206 impossible (LANGUAGE.md §4.6;
§2.6.2); L-c, `.f` of a matrix of structs or records is 249 with the matrix's type (LANGUAGE.md
§4.7; §2.6.2); L-d, a wrong number of arguments of `lower` or `args` is 243, as `now(1)` is (`str()` and
`str(1, 2)` are syntax errors by the grammar's `conv_type "(" expr ")"`)
(§2.6.2); L-e, views and selections under a projection are materialized first, no fusion before
phase 7 (§3.5.9 L15); L-f, a `str` value of more than 4 096 bytes computed while evaluating a
constant is `program too large: strings` (400) at the constant's item, `SEA_LIM_LINE_BYTES` reused
and no limit added (LANGUAGE.md §7.2; §2.6.2 `here`, §3.4.2); L-g, comparisons of `str` constant
expressions are `bool` constant expressions, written `rcnb` (LANGUAGE.md §7.2; §3.4.2); L-h, empty
structs are legal (size 0, an 8-byte home slot, element size 0 in arrays), with one runtime test
per target (LANGUAGE.md §4.6; §2.6.3, §3.5.9 R21, §6.2); L-i, the Decision-25 tests keep their
intent with an undeclared struct type (229) in place of `str`, the tests of the removed phase-rule
rows are retired in the sub-step that removes their row, and the affected `.res` goldens are
re-derived (§6.2); L-j, `anew` of an array of `str`, struct or record elements always uses a
clearing entry (§3.5.9 R21); L-k, struct layouts come from one shared module `passes/lib/layout.bas`
used by `sealoop` and `sealower` from 4g-2 (§2.6.3); L-l, every node of L15–L17 takes the rewritten node's
position, L16 keeping its patterns' and arm blocks' own (§3.5.9); L-m, `slay` records exist for
record element types too (§3.6.6 rule 38); L-n, in 4g-1 an L17 `str` element store into a `ref`
parameter root reads P afresh after the cow (the same values), and R23's reuse of that cow's
register takes effect with 4g-2, together with a stage golden for it (§3.5.9 R23, L17 steps 5–6). *For the user's information:* `error` does not end a
path (LANGUAGE.md §8.1), so `fn f() -> i64 { error("x") }` is `missing return`; a 4g-1 test pins
it (§6.2).

49. **Which relief for `sealower` before 4h** (`sealower` was 6 994 built lines after 4g-2, 6 under
    its 7 000-line cap, with 4h's 150–300 and phases 5–10's 1 100 still to come, §2.7). Options:
    (a) **compaction now: a sub-step 4h-0 that compacts `sealower` with no change of behaviour by
    C1–C6, the register-text function of C4 included, about 600–770 lines, its first step a scratch
    prototype of the multi-line string `DEF` (WP-0); reserves in this order: (V) the semantic
    validation of `sea.hirl` moved into `tools/seaval.bas` (300–400), rule 36's composites with
    `ind2sub` and `sub2ind` moved into `sealoop` (150–170), a middle HIR→HIR pass (440–520)**; (b)
    the mechanical compaction only (C1–C3, C5, C6: 415–540, no `DEF`-based emission); (c) a split
    now, the middle HIR→HIR pass taking rules 18, 19, 36 and the field reads (440–520, a new program
    with the same `sea.hirl` format); (d) rules 18, 19, 36 and the field reads moved into `sealoop`
    (440–520; `sealoop` to 8 820–8 990 at v1). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): it lasts to
    v1 with margin (7 794 at the recorded upper ends, 8 344 under stress), lowers the cost of every
    later emitted instruction, is proved neutral by byte-identical `sea.lir1` and spends none of
    `sealoop`'s margin. Affects §0, §2.7 (the relief, the reserves, "Measured after 4h-0"), §8 (row
    4h-0).
50. **`sealower`'s cap and gates after the relief.** Options: (a) **the 7 000-line cap kept
    through 4h; gates after 4h-0 (4h starts only if built + 300 ≤ 7 000), after 4h, after phase 6
    and after phase 8; a gate fails when the built size plus the remaining upper ends, or the
    stress projection (the phase-level part × 1.5), exceeds 9 000, and a failure applies the next
    reserve before the next phase's code**; (b) 7 000 as a hard cap until v1, any phase that would
    cross it needing a relief first; (c) the cap raised to 8 000 now (Decision 47 (c)'s figure) and
    no relief now. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23). Affects §2.7 (the gates), §8 (rows 4h-0
    and 4h).
51. **Where `sealower`'s semantic validation of `sea.hirl` lives.** Options: (a) **it stays in
    `sealower`; its move to `tools/seaval.bas` is the first reserve relief**; (b) moved now:
    `seaval` (format `hirl`) gets the checks of §3.5.9, `tests/run.sh` runs `seaval hirl` on every
    program's `sea.hirl`, `sealower` keeps the `passes.txt`, tree and safety checks (frees 300–400;
    a production compile then no longer checks `sealoop`'s output); (c) a validating pass between
    `sealoop` and `sealower`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23). Affects §2.7 (the reserves),
    §3.5.9 ("What the passes validate", only if the reserve is applied).
52. **How the library calls of phases 6, 8 and 9 are lowered in `sealower`.** Options: (a)
    **table-driven: one generic path builds the `rcall` from `rt.inc`'s entry records (arguments,
    results, site), with rule 15's ownership (owned results, temporaries among the arguments
    released after the call); a new library function is then an entry row plus front-end and
    `sealoop` work; specified with phase 6**; (b) per-function lowering, as rules 14, 24 and 35 are
    written now. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-23): it brings phase 8's estimate from 200–300
    to 100–150 and phase 9's from 150–250 to 80–120. Affects §2.7 (the increments and the gates
    after phases 6 and 8), §3.6.6 (a rule for library calls, specified with phase 6), §8 (rows 6, 8
    and 9 when they are specified).

**Lead decisions of 4h-0** (2026-10-23, within Decisions 49–52, each taken because one answer is
clearly right, to be reported to the user; each is written into its normative section): L-o,
`sealower`'s v1 projection counts 4h's own increment: the recorded 8 094 omitted it because 4g
alone spent the "4g and 4h" allowance (907 against 550–800), corrected to 6 994 + 300 + 1 100 =
8 394 before the relief (§2.7); L-p, the neutrality of any `sealower` compaction is proved by
byte-identical `sea.lir1` of every `tests/programs` program, every run-phase `tests/errors`
program and the W4 acceptance program (`tests/accept/w4_sor.sea`), before against after, plus
every stage pair, `make test` and `make cross` (§2.7, §8 row 4h-0); L-q, the compaction keeps every
part file's line range and the insert-between numbering (§2.6.3), each new `DEF FN` gets a header
comment in `sl0main`'s table of helpers, and no array letter is used (`C S X` stay free; §8 row
4h-0); L-r, 4h-0 touches only `passes/sealower/*` and the text of the docs, with no contract file,
intermediate format, `sealoop`, driver or test script changing (§8 row 4h-0).

53. **How rule 37 is written in `sea.hirl`** (no record was a block with a value that can be left
    early: `ret` returns from the caller, an `xblk` has no exit, a `block` no value). Options: (a)
    **two new records, `iblk` (code 88: the callee's body block, lowered `do`/`enddo`, its value R1
    … Rk, with its type and result count) and `iret` (89: the values owned, the releases down to the
    `iblk`, the `mov`s, `exit`), the `iblk` always the value of an `xblk` whose statements are the
    parameter `tmp`s; `sealoop`'s new rewrite L18 does all the tree work, `sealower` gains only
    their lowering; `passes.txt` gains the two records**; (b) the same records with the `iblk`
    holding the parameter `tmp`s itself (pops n + 1), with its own release rule for owned arguments
    (one record fewer per call, a second copy of the `xblk`'s release logic in `sealower`); (c) no
    record: `sealoop` writes return-free bodies with a result local and flags (no `do`/`exit`, a
    change to rule 37's agreed LIR, reopening Decision 29). **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24): the argument temporaries reuse T1 and T2 unchanged, rule 37's example comes out
    exactly, and `sealower`'s part is the smallest, as the 4h-0 guidance agreed. Affects
    `passes.txt`, §3.5.4, §3.5.9 (the table, L18, R26–R30, the validation), §3.6.6 (rule 37, the
    lowering of the records), §3.9.
54. **The signatures of the prelude functions** (LANGUAGE.md left `meshgrid`'s element type and the
    argument types of `setdiff` and `bincount` implicit). Options: (a) **one signature each, with
    LANGUAGE.md's parameter names: `linspace(d1: f64, d2: f64, n: i64) -> f64[]`, `meshgrid(x:
    f64[], y: f64[]) -> (f64[,], f64[,])` (an `i64[]` argument converted element by element,
    LANGUAGE.md §4.2), `setdiff(a: i64[], b: i64[]) -> i64[]`, `bincount(idx: i64[], n: i64) ->
    i64[]`**; (b) `meshgrid` also on `i64` vectors giving `i64[,]`, which one prelude `fn` cannot
    be (Sea has no overloading), so a compiler intrinsic (a `seacheck` overload and a `sealoop`
    rewrite, about 100 lines in two tight passes). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24): all four
    stay in the prelude as §2.5 agreed, at no compiler cost; W4's integer grid is written by
    broadcasting. Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.3, §10.6, §10.7; §2.5.
55. **Recursive prelude inlining in 4h** (the committed prelude has no call from one prelude
    function to another). Options: (a) **built now, as rule 37 says, and tested with stage-only
    hand-written two-file `sea.hir` goldens (`inl_nested`)**; (b) deferred to phase 6, a prelude
    call inside the prelude rejected as `BAD_RECORD` until then. **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24): about 20–40 `sealoop` lines, no part of the agreed rule left unbuilt, and phase 6
    reuses it. Affects §2.5, §3.5.9 (L18), §6.2.
56. **`sealoop`'s size gate** (its v1 margin 450–467 at the recorded upper ends, over 9 000 under a
    × 1.5 stress of phases 6 and 7). Options: (a) **`sealoop` joins the gate after 4h (built ≤ 7 000,
    built + 2 600 ≤ 9 000, at least 2 free letters), its stress line recorded and decided at the
    gate after phase 6 together with the fusion seam**; (b) phase 7's fusion decided now as a pass
    of its own in front of `sealoop`; (c) a behaviour-neutral compaction of `sealoop` before 4h's
    code (4h-0's patterns, about 300–450 lines). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24): 4h's own
    increment was already counted in `sealoop`'s recorded margin, and the phase-6 gate measures the
    phase that brings the risk. Affects §2.7, §8 (row 4h).
57. **How rule 37's dumps are tested against the real prelude** (`NAME.prelude` allowed only
    `.lir1`, and every intermediate file holds the prelude's `#file` record with its install
    path). Options: (a) **`NAME.prelude` allowed beside `.hir`, `.hirl`, `.lir1` and `.out`, the
    runners comparing the file-0 `#file` record of such a dump as `#file std.sea` (the goldens
    written so), the driver unchanged**; (b) `.lir1` only, with the same normalization, `sealoop`'s
    rewrite stage-checked only by the hand-written goldens; (c) the driver writes the prelude's
    `#file` record as `std.sea`, a change to §2.2's agreed stream. **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24): both programs of pass 3a are stage-checked on the real prelude, and only test
    scripts change. Affects §6.2, `tests/run.sh`, `tests/cross_pack.sh`.

**Lead decisions of 4h** (2026-10-24, within Decisions 53–57, each taken because one answer is
clearly right, to be reported to the user; each is written into its normative section): L-s, the
prelude's items (file 0 of a stream with more than one `#file` record) are exempt from 212, as
LANGUAGE.md §3.3 says, and the four prelude names resolve only as entered items, so that with
`--no-prelude` they are `undeclared name` as §2.2 says, while a program item with such a name
stays 212 and a local 213 (§2.6.2 "Readings fixed by 4h", §3.4.1); L-t, prelude calls are checked
as ordinary calls (226, 242, 201, 255; named arguments by the phase rule until phase 6), and
`std.sea` uses LANGUAGE.md §10's parameter names, which those messages expose (§2.5, §2.6.2); L-u,
the callee's locals become `.i` locals of the caller, ordinary in every respect and numbered after
the `.l` locals, `.l`'s restrictions staying intact for `sealoop`'s own temporaries (§3.5.4,
§3.5.9 R28); L-v, `sealoop` drops the prelude functions and renumbers the rest densely, because
`sealower` requires dense `fid`s and no prelude function is a LIR function (§3.5.9 L18); L-w, the
order and ownership details of R26, R27, R29 and R30 (owned arguments released in the order R27 gives, after the `mov`s of a `tbind` and before the stores of a `tasg`,
an `iblk` without a destination yielding R1 … Rk, rule 2 (d)'s path for `tbind` and `tasg`, no
end-of-block releases after an `iret`), each the reading that makes an inline call behave as the
call it replaces (§3.5.9); L-x, a prelude function's result types are void, scalars, `str`,
dynamic arrays or tuples of those, rule 37's `mov` covering only register values, and `sealoop`
rejects others, which phase 6 specifies with LANGUAGE.md §8.6 (§2.5, §3.5.9); L-y, every prelude
error has its message: `bincount` with n < 0 or above 2³¹ − 1 and `linspace` with n above 2³¹ − 1
are `invalid array size n`, a too large `meshgrid` result is `out of memory`, all at the program's call line
(LANGUAGE.md §10.3, §10.7; §2.6.2); L-z, the close-out adds one test per after-phase-4 row that has
none (`@`, `format`, `solve`, `figure`), and no test names the four removed words, so none is
retired (§2.6.2, §6.2); L-aa, `w5_stats.sea` is Appendix D's text for what its four keys need,
followed by the `printf` JSON of §6.3 and nothing else on standard output (§6.2); L-ab, neither
`sealower` nor `sealoop` takes more than its spare array letters (`sealower` none, the `iblk` stack
living in its existing block tables; `sealoop` at most one, leaving at least 2) (§2.7, §8).
*For the user's information:* by LANGUAGE.md §10.3 rule 2, `linspace(0.0, 0.0, 4)` is `[0, -0, 0,
0]`; the reference `common.mlinspace` agrees, and a test pins it.

58. **Where the optimizations live.** Options: (a) **every LIR-to-LIR transformation in `seaopt`
    (T1–T10 of §5.8), target-independent; register allocation and instruction selection in pass 4**;
    (b) the loop transformations (T5–T9) in a new pass between `seaopt` and pass 4 (a new program,
    driver step and dump kind, the size of 4e-0's split); (c) check elimination in `sealower`, which
    knows shapes from the HIR (it has 527 lines left under its cap and phases 6–9 still to come).
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) keeps one program per concern and `seaopt`, the
    pass §2.7 sized for this work (2 444 lines), at 4 404–5 684; (b) only pays if `seaopt` cannot
    hold phase 7 too, which the gate after phase 5 measures (Decision 71); (c) spends `sealower`'s
    scarce margin. Affects §2.7, §3.6.5, §5.8, §8. *Revisited by Decision 74* (2026-10-24): after
    5c-1 `seaopt` measured 5 316 lines, so (b)'s condition is met and T5–T9 move to pass 3c.
59. **The allocator.** Options: (a) **one linear-scan allocator in a shared module
    `passes/lib/ralloc.bas`, built into both code generators with per-target register tables**; (b)
    the allocator in `seaopt`, its assignment carried to pass 4 in new `sea.lir` records (set `LF`),
    the code generators only mapping numbers to names; (c) a separate allocator written in each code
    generator; (d) a new pass `seareg` between `seaopt` and pass 4. **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24); (a) is written once, needs no contract change, and costs its 450–750 lines in each
    code generator (both stay ≤ 5 650); (b) also writes it once, but changes `passes.txt`, `seaval`
    and every LIR dump, and adds 600–900 lines to `seaopt`, which then cannot take phase 7 under the
    7 000-line cap; (c) doubles the work and the bugs; (d) adds a program and a dump kind for no
    gain over (a). Affects §2.7, §4.9.2, §8.
60. **Allocator policy.** Options: (a) **fixed scratch registers (arm64 `x15 x16 x17`, `d29 d30
    d31`; x86_64 `%rax %rcx %rdx %r11`, `%xmm14 %xmm15`), so 25/29 and 10/14 allocatable; values
    that cross a call kept in their registers and saved and reloaded around the call (callee-saved
    registers first on arm64); the spill victim chosen by the loop depth of its deepest use, then
    the farthest end; no interval splitting**; (b) the same, but x86_64's fixed operands handled by
    pre-coloured intervals instead of reserved registers (13 allocatable, about 150 more lines in
    the module and more cases to test); (c) values that cross a call only in callee-saved registers,
    otherwise spilled whole (simpler, but x86_64 has no callee-saved `xmm` register: W4's `omega`
    and `dMax`, which cross the slow copy's `sea_arr_unique` call, would live in memory in the hot
    loop). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) meets both §5.2 targets with registers to
    spare (W4's interior loop needs 9 general registers on x86_64), and saves cost only on the paths
    that call. Affects §4.9.2, §5.2.
61. **Bounds-check elimination, and the checks it cannot prove.** Options: (a) **a check is deleted
    only when §5.8's facts prove it (loop ranges from `rcount` and rule 17, creation extents of
    shape-stable arrays, the extents of unchanged parameters, dominating comparisons, checks already
    passed); every other check stays exactly where it is, as a compare and a branch to a cold block,
    never moved or merged; LANGUAGE.md §5.4's "hoists the others out of loops" becomes "keeps the
    others as a compare and a never-taken branch"**; (b) (a), plus loop versioning on a range test
    in front of a loop whose unproven checks are affine in its index (a check-free copy when the
    whole range fits, the original otherwise; exact, but up to twice the code and 200–300 more
    lines); (c) (a), plus hoisting an invariant check when it would run first in the first iteration
    (exact only under conditions that W4's boundary checks do not meet). **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24); (a) proves every check of W4 and W5 and keeps LANGUAGE.md's error order trivially;
    (b) helps loops over arrays whose extents are unrelated to the range, which no workload has in a
    hot loop; (c) adds subtle conditions for little. Affects §5.8, LANGUAGE.md §5.4 (one sentence,
    not a rule).
62. **Copy on write in loops.** Options: (a) **versioning (T6): a test of the counts in front of the
    outermost qualifying loop chooses a copy of the loop without the cows (counts 1) or the
    original; register and `ref`-parameter (memory) forms; one level, at most twice the loop's
    code**; (b) the cow hoisted in front of the loop (`sea_arr_unique` called before the loop even
    when no store would run: exact in values, but an `out of memory` can then come earlier, or where
    the program would not have copied, which LANGUAGE.md §9.2 would have to allow); (c) the cow kept
    in the loop (3 instructions per store, and the data address of the array cannot be hoisted, so
    W4's column pointers are reloaded each point: the W4 target is missed). **Decided: (a)** (the
    user, 2026-10-24); (a) is exact and makes the hot copy a plain store; it costs 200–320 lines and
    code size. Affects §4.2 (its copy-on-write paragraphs name the versioning), §5.8.
63. **What is hoisted, how memory is disambiguated, and unswitching.** Options: (a) **hoisting of
    pure instructions, of checked arithmetic once T1 has made it unchecked, of header loads (also
    from inside `if` arms, for array registers), of loads from private locations (unaliased `ref`
    parameters and private slots, L-af) and of anticipated loads; never of a failing instruction, an
    effect, or a load with an index (L-aj); memory disambiguated by the location classes of §5.8
    (header fields, private locations, then by access kind); promotion of private `i64`/`f64`
    locations to registers in loops (W5's `ref s`); value numbering within regions; if-conversion of
    one-`mov` arms; unswitching of innermost loops on at most two invariant conditions (T9)**; (b)
    (a) without unswitching (W4's two boundary tests stay as two well-predicted branches per point;
    arm64 26 instructions instead of 24, and on x86_64 the boundary arms' registers no longer fit
    the 10 allocatable ones, so the loop body gets spill loads); (c) (a) without promotion (W5's `s`
    is loaded and stored through memory each step: two memory operations and a store-to-load
    forwarding delay on the dependency chain). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); unswitching
    costs 100–180 lines and up to four copies of an innermost loop. Affects §5.2, §5.8.
64. **Strength reduction.** Options: (a) **both forms: unit stride (the index register with a
    hoisted base, constant offsets folded into the base) and invariant stride (a pointer advanced at
    the top of the body, so `next` stays right)**; (b) unit stride only now, invariant stride with
    phase 7's vectorization (W4 and W5 need only unit stride; W2's row access and any `A[i, j]` with
    `j` inner then keep a multiply per access until phase 7); (c) none: scaled addressing only, the
    linear index computed per access. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) meets §5.2's
    wording ("pointer increments of 8 and 8·ld") for 150–250 lines; (b) saves about 80 of them.
    Affects §5.2, §5.8.
65. **Division by constants.** Options: (a) **`%` and `idiv` on `i64` by a constant c ≥ 1: c = 1,
    powers of two (`iand`, `isar`), every other c by the signed multiply-high sequence of §5.8 with
    the floored correction (Hacker's Delight's magic numbers, computed by `seaopt` itself, L-am); a
    zero or negative constant unchanged; `f64` `/` by a normal power of two as a multiplication
    (L-al)**; (b) also negative constant divisors (by negation, the −2⁶³ and −1 cases kept checked;
    no workload divides by a negative constant); (c) powers of two only (W5's `% 2147483647` keeps
    its `sdiv`/`idivq`, hardware division on the dependency chain of every step). **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) covers every workload use (`mod(16807*s, 2147483647)`, `mod(I + J,
    2)`, `mod(nPanel, 2)`); the sequence was checked against floored `%` and `idiv` on the edge
    dividends and 2 000 random ones for each of about 300 divisors (a scratch check while writing
    this; the `opt_*` tests of §6.2 make it permanent). Affects §5.8, LANGUAGE.md (none: §6.6 and
    §6.8 already allow it).
66. **How "meets the §5.2 shapes" is tested.** Options: (a) **two layers: hand-derived `opt5_*`
    `.lir` goldens of pass 3b (the W5 function and a small W4 loop among them), and `tests/shape.sh`
    on `-S` of the acceptance programs for both targets (instruction count bound, exact mnemonic
    counts, no frame access, no call, the number of cold branches), run on the Mac by `make test`**;
    (b) golden `-S` fragments for each target (brittle: any allocator or template change rewrites
    them, and they pin details §4.9.2 does not fix); (c) dynamic counts from performance counters or
    a simulator (not reproducible across machines, no simulator in the toolchain). **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) tests the LIR exactly (it is specified exactly) and the machine code
    by its properties. Affects §6.2, §8.
67. **The corrected §5.2 targets.** Options: (a) **W5: 20 arm64 and 23 x86_64 instructions per step;
    W4: 24 arm64 and 27 x86_64 per interior point (§5.2 "Targets for phase 5"), derived from §5.8
    and §4.9.2; six `f64` loads per W4 point**; (b) keep "≈ 10" for W5 and add peepholes (arm64
    `msub`, shifted-operand `sub`, a Mersenne-specific remainder for 2³¹ − 1): about 16–18, still
    not 10, for more templates; (c) forward `T[j − 1, i]` from the previous iteration's store to
    reach five loads (needs a value carried across iterations through the `continue` path; not in
    phase 5's scope). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) states what the design produces;
    §5.5's time estimates do not change (they were made from latency, not counts). Affects §5.2,
    §6.2's shape files.
68. **The micro-benchmarks.** Options: (a) **`bench/micro/` with `lcg.sea` and `sor.sea` (the
    acceptance programs' loops verbatim, validated by `lcg_final` and `it_sor`), C references built
    `-O2 -ffp-contract=off`, `bench/micro.sh` on the Mac and the host, BENCH.md's methodology, each
    measured with the phase-4 and the phase-5 compiler; TSV committed under `bench/results/`, the
    table in §5.9**; (b) whole-program timings of `tests/accept/w4_sor.sea` and `w5_stats.sea` only
    (mixes in start-up, allocation and the other phases of W5); (c) numbers written into §5.9 only,
    no harness kept. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) isolates the two loops phase 5 is
    judged by and leaves a harness phase 10's `bench/` reuses. Affects §5.9, §8.
69. **Is `seaopt`'s output canonical?** Options: (a) **yes: §5.8 fixes the order, the conditions and
    the placement of every transformation, so `sea.lir` is derivable by hand and its dumps are
    golden tests, as for every other pass**; (b) only properties are specified (behaviour, and
    pattern checks on `.lir`), no goldens. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) follows the
    house rule that expected outputs come from the spec and catches a missed or misplaced
    transformation directly; it makes §5.8 longer and every golden slower to derive. Affects §5.8,
    §6.2.
70. **Sub-phases and gates.** Options: (a) **5a the specification; 5b pass 4's allocator and
    selection on both targets (no `seaopt` change, so the whole corpus checks it); 5c-1 `seaopt`'s
    analysis and local transformations, in parallel with 5b; 5c-2 the loop transformations; 5d the
    shape tests, the benchmarks and the size gate**; (b) one step after the specification; (c)
    `seaopt` first, the allocator last. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) proves the
    allocator against unchanged LIR before the LIR starts changing, and lets two teams work on
    disjoint files; (c) would leave the shapes unmeasurable until the end. Affects §8.
71. **`seaopt`'s size and phase 7.** Options: (a) **a gate after phase 5 records `seaopt`,
    `seagen_a64` and `seagen_x64` (§2.7); when `seaopt` + 2 000 exceeds 7 000, phase 7's
    vectorization is decided as a pass of its own at the gate after phase 6, with Decision 56's
    fusion seam**; (b) decide now that phase 7's vectorization is its own pass; (c) no gate until
    phase 7. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) decides with the measured size (the
    projection spans 4 404–5 684); (b) may create a pass that turns out unnecessary. Affects §2.7,
    §8. *Settled by Decision 74* (2026-10-24): phase 7's scalar replacement and vectorization go
    into pass 3c, `sealopt`, and the gate after phase 5 is revised (L-be, §2.7). *Revised by
    Decision 78* (2026-10-25): phase 7's scalar replacement and vectorization get a pass of their own
    after `sealopt`.
72. **Optimization against the capacity limits.** Options: (a) **a transformation whose result would
    exceed a LIR limit of the function is skipped, so optimization never causes `program too
    large`**; (b) the limit is reported as for any other pass. **Decided: (a)** (the user,
    2026-10-24); (a) keeps the compile errors a property of the program, not of the optimizer
    (versioning and unswitching can multiply a loop's size by up to eight). Affects §3.6.5, §5.8.
73. **A switch to turn the optimizations off.** Options: (a) **none: `seaopt` and the allocator
    always run; the corpus, whose expected outputs come from the spec, is the exactness test**; (b)
    a driver option (`-O0`) under which `seaopt` copies its input and pass 4 keeps the allocator,
    used by a differential test over the corpus and by the benchmarks (a change of §2.2's usage line
    and of `driver_check.sh`). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (b) adds a mode that must
    itself be tested; §5.9 gets its "before" numbers from the phase-4 compiler instead. Affects §2.2
    (only under (b)), §5.9, §6.2.
74. **Where the loop transformations live, after 5c-1** (taken at the gate arithmetic of §2.7,
    "Measured after 5b and 5c-1": `seaopt` 5 316 built lines, and T5–T9 at 770–1 270 would fail
    built + 3 000 ≤ 9 000). Options: (a) **a new pass 3c, `sealopt` (`sea.lir2` → `sea.lir`, LIR in
    and LIR out, after `seaopt` and before pass 4), holding T5, T6, T8, T7, T8, T9 and T10, with
    `seaopt`'s reader, validator, writer and T10 moved into a shared part `lirrw` that both passes
    load; `--emit lir` stays the final LIR and `--emit lir2` is new; phase 7's scalar replacement and
    vectorization go into `sealopt`**; (b) compact `seaopt` first, in a sub-phase like 4h-0 aiming
    at 700–1 000 lines, then add T5–T9 to it; (c) relax the gate for `seaopt`. This revisits
    Decision 58's option (b), which "only pays if `seaopt` cannot hold phase 7": that condition is
    now met. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); (a) gives the loop transformations and the
    vectorizer a pass sized for them (4 069–5 059 built after phase 5, 6 069–7 059 with phase 7, at
    the stress view 4 667–6 043 and 6 667–8 043, §2.7) and
    leaves `seaopt` with no further phase work; (b) costs a sub-phase and still leaves `seaopt` too
    full for phase 7; (c) gives up the stress margin the gates exist for. Affects §0, §2 (the pass
    table), §2.2, §2.6.3, §2.7, §2.10, §3.6.5, §5.8, §6.2, §8; lead decisions L-bc–L-be, L-bi–L-bk, L-bl, L-bm, L-bp.
    *Revised by Decision 78* (2026-10-25, at the gate after phase 5): phase 7's scalar replacement
    and vectorization get a pass of their own after `sealopt` instead of going into `sealopt`.
75. **Which intervals the allocator extends over a loop.** Options: (a) **only a register that may
    be live at the loop's top: read inside the loop, or after it, without a covering write earlier
    in the same iteration, or after the loop (§4.9.2, "Positions and intervals"), computed in `ralloc`'s
    reference walk with one new call, `ra_else`; landing with 5c-2, before 5d's shape targets**; (b)
    keep the first rule (every register first written inside an `if` part is extended over the
    loop) and measure again after 5c-2. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-24); under the first rule
    a temporary of an `if` part holds a register for the whole loop, which floods x86_64's 10
    general registers (W4's `j` loop about 60 % frame traffic after 5c-1, §5.2), while (a) extends
    the loop-carried values and the values defined before the loop and read in it, conservatively
    at nested loops, and costs about 90–170 lines per code generator; (b) would leave every loop with an `if` exposed to the same
    spills, which unswitching removes only for invariant conditions. Affects §0, §4.9.2, §5.2, §8;
    lead decisions L-bf, L-bg, L-bh, L-bl, L-bm, L-bo.
76. **Whether a loop's step that is a `mov` of an `li` register is a constant for pass 4** (found in
    5d by the shape tests: W4's interior `j` loop on x86_64 kept its step, `mov i342 i340` of `li
    i340 1`, in an 11th general register, spilled it and loaded it at every step, 29 instructions
    against §5.2's 27). Options: (a) **for §4.9.2's loop closing a step is a constant also when its
    only definition is a `mov` from a register whose only definition is an `li` (L-br's one level of
    `mov`), on both targets: the closing `add` takes the immediate and the step is no reference of
    the loop (`ra_open` gets no step register)**; (b) the same on x86_64 only; (c) a `sealopt` rule
    that rewrites the step operand of a `loop` record to the `li` register, which changes the `.lir`
    goldens. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-25); (a) is the reading T7 already uses (L-br), keeps
    §4.9.2 the same on both targets and frees a register in every lowered loop (arm64's text changes
    from a register step to `#1` with the same counts); (b) splits a both-target rule for no gain; (c)
    moves a code-generation question into the optimizer and changes goldens. Affects §0, §4.9.2,
    §5.2, §5.8 (T7's note), `passes/lib/API.md` (`ra_open`); L-br.
77. **Which register an x86_64 non-commuting two-address destination takes when its hint is not
    free** (found in 5d with Decision 76: W4's `fsub` of the update's change took the register of
    its dying second operand `T[j, i]`, so "x86_64 forms" computed it in `%xmm14` and moved it, one
    `movapd` more than §5.2's target). Options: (a) **on x86_64 the destination of `d = a op b` of a
    non-commuting operation, b a register operand other than a, takes, when its hint is not free,
    the first free register of its row other than b's, and b's only when no other is free; arm64
    unchanged; told to the allocator by a new call `ra_avoid`**; (b) a code-selection rule that
    computes such an instruction in place in b's register (impossible for `fsub`/`fdiv`/`isub`
    without changing the operation: a − b is not −(b − a) for equal operands, +0 against −0). **Decided:
    (a)** (the user, 2026-10-25); (a) costs nothing when another register is free and never spills
    more, since b's register is still taken when it is the only one; (b) would break LANGUAGE.md
    §6.8's exactness. Affects §0, §4.9.2 ("The scan"), §5.2, `passes/lib/API.md` (`ra_avoid`),
    `passes/lib/ralloc.bas`, `passes/seagen_x64/*`.
78. **Where phase 7's vectorizer lives, after the gate after phase 5** (taken at §2.7, "Measured
    after 5d": `sealopt` at 5 411 built lines passes the gate's three line conditions but has 0 free
    numeric array letters where the gate requires at least 2, its scratch tables having taken `S`
    and `V`, the 2 letters L-bp left it; and `sealopt` + phase 7's 2 000 is 7 411, above 7 000).
    Options: (a) **phase 7's vectorizer gets a pass of its own, a new pass 3d after `sealopt`,
    reading and writing the `sea.lir` format and sharing `seaopt`'s and `sealopt`'s reader,
    validator, writer and T10 through the shared main-program part `passes/lib/lirrw.bas` (L-bi),
    as `sealopt` does; `sealopt` stays as built**; (b) a compaction of `sealopt`'s tables with no
    change of behaviour, freeing 2 letters; (c) waive `sealopt`'s letter condition. **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-25); (a) takes the vectorizer's tables and lines out of `sealopt`, which
    addresses both the letter shortfall and the 7 411 > 7 000 projection, and leaves `sealopt` as
    built and tested; (b) costs a sub-phase and leaves `sealopt` + 2 000 = 7 411 > 7 000 for phase
    7; (c) the same, and gives up the headroom the letter condition keeps. Settled by phase 7's
    specification, not here: the pass's name, its input and output file names (and so which file
    is the final LIR that pass 4 reads and `--emit lir` dumps), its place in the driver's sequence
    and its `--emit` kind, its `SUB` prefix and line range, its budget at the gates (whether phase 7's scalar replacement,
    which Decision 74 put into `sealopt` together with the vectorization, stays there or joins the
    new pass was first left to it too, and is decided further below: it joins the new pass). No contract file changes with this decision
    (`include/*.inc`, `include/passes.txt`), and no code. Phase 7's specification starts from the
    room L-bp leaves a pass that loads `lirrw`: exactly 2 free numeric array letters (`S V`), the
    free columns of `R`, the scratch `W` between entries, and the unreserved string arrays and
    scalars. Affects §2 (the pass table), §2.7 (the gate after phase 5 re-applied, "Measured after
    5d"), §3.6 (the file table), §8 (rows 5d and 7), and the forward notes on Decisions 71 and 74
    and L-bp. *Decided further* (the user, 2026-10-25, after the gate was re-applied with (a): the
    gate as written still asked `sealopt` for 2 free letters, which it sets even for a pass with
    fixes only, and phase 7's scalar replacement had no home yet): options (a) **waive the letter
    condition for `sealopt`, and move phase 7's scalar replacement to the new pass 3d too, so
    `sealopt` receives fixes only**; (b) waive the condition, scalar replacement stays in
    `sealopt`; (c) keep the condition and compact `sealopt` to free 2 letters. **Decided: (a)**;
    `sealopt` then takes no new tables, so its letters guard nothing, and phase 7's LIR work
    (scalar replacement and vectorization) is specified and sized together in one pass; (b) would
    put new tables into a pass with 0 free letters; (c) costs a sub-phase for letters that only
    fixes would use. With it the gate after phase 5 passes all four programs (§2.7, "The gate after
    phase 5 with Decision 78's relief"), and phase 5 is complete (§8).
79. **What is an alpha, and what is GA.** Options: (a) an alpha release after phase 6 (W1 and W5
    end to end) plus release work (license, README, release notes, a version suffix, tags); (b)

    is GA, given when v1 is done (§1.2: all six workloads, phase 10); no git tag or release

    and (b) add a release step and a version suffix to maintain. Affects §1.2 (one sentence); no
    row of §8, no contract file, no code.

80. **What phase 6's ports contain, given that figures are phase 9**
    (§2.11.8; W1 and W5 as MATLAB scripts and Appendix D draw figures, which need phase 9's plotting

    figures" says, keeps the ports ordinary Sea programs that the compiler builds as written, and the
    figures are additive in phase 9 (a new arm of the option loop and a block of plotting calls); (b)
    puts a preprocessor that Sea does not have into the test harness, and the stripped text is not
    the file that is compiled; (c) gives up the workload test that is phase 6's purpose. Affects
