81. **Where the checks of elemental functions and the §8.6 inlining
    class are made, and how the class reaches pass 3a** (§2.11.2, §2.11.3). Options: (a) **`seaname`
    makes one whole-program call pre-pass after resolving the bodies: effects (fixpoint), call-graph
    cycles, 228 and 232 through `rerr`, and the §8.6 class of every `fn` item on the source, written
    as `rfn`'s `el` 2 and carried by `seacheck` as the HIR `fn` kind `inl` (`enum fkind` gains `inl`;
    no record format changes)**; (b) all of it in `seacheck`, which holds the types; (c) `seacheck`
    reports 228/232, and `sealoop` recomputes the inlining class on `sea.hir`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26);
    the class is defined on the source as written (call sites, statements, loops) and on names, which
    are `seaname`'s; the pre-pass is the first check at a `call` node, so moving 228 and 232 keeps the
    rule "Order across the two programs" (§2.6.2); `seaname` has the room (projection 5 611–5 921,
    §2.7) and `seacheck` does not (Decision 82); (b) adds 250–400 lines to the pass that is already
    over its cap at the upper end of its projection; (c) counts on rewritten HIR (defaults copied, pass
    2b's instances), where the counts of §8.6 differ from the source's, and puts a whole-program
    analysis into the pass with the most erratic estimates. Affects §2.11.2, §2.11.3, §3.4.1 and §3.5.4
    (contract change 2 of §2.11.1).
82. **Room in `seacheck` for phase 6** (§2.7, "Projected for phase 6":
    6 426 + 455–870 = 6 881–7 296, above 7 000 built lines at the upper end; its earlier increments
    landed inside their estimates; revised after the review found that `sealower`'s 4h-0 patterns
    do not carry over). The compaction available is smaller than first written: `seacheck` is in the
    `SUB`/`CALL` style (124 `SUB`s, 709 `CALL`s, 9 `GOSUB`s, no `DEF`), so C1, C4 and C6 (`GOSUB`
    fall-through and tail calls, multi-line `DEF` text helpers, one shared `GOSUB` child loop) have
    nothing to act on; C2 (merging consecutive `REM` lines, measured on its own code) saves at most
    219, C3 and C5 0–80: 150–300 in all, which leaves the projection after phase 6 at 6 581–7 146,
    so its upper end still above 7 000. Options: (a)
    **gate `seacheck` as Decision 50 gates `sealower`: its 7 000 condition is replaced by built +
    850 ≤ 9 000 and built + 1 275 ≤ 9 000 (passed at every end: 8 146 and 8 571), with at least 2
    free letters; no sub-step before 6b; the compaction (C2, C3, C5; 150–300) is the reserve that
    the measurement after 6c calls for if built + 120 + 1 275 > 9 000 there**; (b) the compaction
    first, as sub-step 6b-0 (150–300), and keep the 7 000 condition, accepting that the upper end
    still fails it and would need (a) or (c) at the gate; (c) split `seacheck` now: the library-call
    checks (overload tables and typing of §10's functions) into a new pass between 2a and 2b, a new
    intermediate format and driver step; (d) move the named-argument matching (224, 225, 226 of
    user and prelude functions) into `seaname`, which knows the signatures, saving 100–150 lines of
    `seacheck` but leaving `seacheck` to repeat the mapping to write `sea.hir1`. **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-26); `seacheck`'s remaining work after phase 6 is the smallest of the front end (850), so the
    7 000 condition, which exists to keep room for later phases, protects little here, while the
    9 000 conditions, which do, pass at every end; Decision 50 set the precedent for `sealower`
    after it had compacted; it costs no sub-phase and keeps the compaction in reserve; (b) spends a
    sub-phase for a saving that does not reach the condition it is for; (c) is the right shape only
    if phases 8–9 grow `seacheck` well past their 850, which the gate after phase 8 can still decide;
    (d) duplicates the matching across two programs. Affects §2.7, §8 (rows 6b-0, 6b), the gate
    after phase 6.
83. **What §8.6 inlining of the program's own functions covers in
    pass 3a** (L18 inlines the prelude, whose functions have scalar or array parameters and results
    and no `ref` parameter). Options: (a) **all of it: `ref` parameters (R31: the argument's address
    bound to a ref local, lowered exactly as a call's), aggregate results (R32: a caller-provided
    home, as a call's hidden result address), and `return` of a multiple-result call (`tret` → `tbind`
    of `.i` locals and `iret`), so every function §8.6 names is inlined**; (b) amend LANGUAGE.md §8.6
    so that a function with a `ref` parameter is not inlined; (c) exempt all three cases from §8.6.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); §8.6 is normative, and W1's `make_params` (three call sites, but no loop,
    not recursive and about 15 statements, so class (c)) returns a struct, and W1's `shaft_safety`
    (elemental) returns a tuple; R31 and R32 reuse the lowering of calls and homes that phase 4
    tests, so the semantics of an inlined call are those of the call by construction; (b) and (c)
    change the language to fit the implementation and leave `make_params`'s struct result to a call,
    which the workload could live with but the rule does not allow. Affects §2.11.4 (L20), §2.11.5
    (R31, R32), §3.6.6.
84. **How an elemental call with array arguments is lowered** (§3.5.7
    step 3 writes `inst` and `emap`). Options: (a) **`sealoop` rewrite L19: arguments once, rule 22's
    broadcast extents, checks and loop nest, one `anew` per kept result (a result bound to `_` or
    `skip`, or under `eval`, is not allocated), an inlined per-element call, `est` of each kept
    result, L11's statement forms for k ≥ 2**; (b) as (a), but every result allocated; (c) pass 2b
    writes the loops in HIR as it does for `write_json`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); rule 22 already owns
    broadcasting, its checks and its order, so an elemental application has the shapes, sites and
    error order of an elemental library call; skipping discarded results saves W1's grids work and
    memory and changes no output (an error in the body is still raised at the first failing
    element); (b) is simpler by about 40 lines but allocates arrays nobody reads, which the heap
    check would still pass; (c) duplicates rule 22's broadcasting in pass 2b, a second
    implementation of the shape rules that must agree with the first. Affects §2.11.4.
85. **The runtime interface of phase 6's output** (§2.11.6). Options:
    (a) **sixteen entries, ids 23–38: `FORMAT`, `PRINT`, `MAKE_DIR`, `FMOD`, and twelve JSON entries
    (open, close, object, array, end, key, four scalars, vector, matrix), all lowered by rule 39's
    table**; (b) one `sea_json` entry with an operation code as its first argument; (c) the emitter
    written as LIR by `sealower` around a small byte-writing entry. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); each entry
    has one fixed signature, so the entry table types its calls and rule 39 stays a table lookup
    (Decision 52); (b) needs a variadic argument class the entry table cannot describe; (c) moves the
    `%.17g` formatting and escaping into generated code on both targets and grows `sealower`, which
    has the least room. Affects §2.11.6, `rt.inc` (WP-CONTRACT), §4.8.
86. **How the ports are accepted** (§6.3). Options: (a) **a new
    `tests/accept.sh` for `sea/ports/`, beside `tests/accept4.sh`, which stays: `compare.py
    --candidate` and `compare_report.py` with the token maps on the Mac; on the Linux host byte
    identity of the report (minus the `Compute time` line) and of the JSON against the Mac's**; (b)
    merge both into one script with two modes; (c) run `compare.py` and `compare_report.py` on the
    host too. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); the phase-4 programs keep their own keys and the shape tests use
    them, and a separate script keeps phase 4's tests untouched; byte identity on the host is a
    stronger check than the comparators and needs no Python or NumPy there; (b) mixes two contracts
    in one file for no gain; (c) adds a NumPy dependency to the host for a check byte identity already
    implies. Affects §6.3, §8 (row 6e).
87. **How phase 6 is built** (§8). Options: (a) **the sub-phases 6a
    (specification), 6b (calls and output with WP-CONTRACT first, then WP-NAME, WP-CHECK, WP-LOOP,
    WP-LOWER and T2's re-derived goldens integrated together), 6c (elemental, then the measurement after 6c), 6d
    (`write_json`), 6e (ports, acceptance, gate), each with work packages that own disjoint files;
    6b-0 (the `seacheck` compaction) only as Decision 82 (a)'s reserve requires (the measurement
    after 6c)**; (b) one build
    after 6a with every package in parallel; (c) one sub-phase per pass. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); each
    sub-phase ends with a passing `make test` and `make cross` and removes its own phase-rule rows;
    6b's entries and fkind change come first so that 6c and 6d only use them; 6c is followed by the
    measurement of `sealoop` and `seacheck` before 6d adds to them; (b) puts five packages into the
    same passes at once, which the file-ownership rule forbids; (c) splits each feature across
    sub-phases, so no sub-phase tests a feature end to end. Affects §8.
88. **The gate after phase 6 and where phase 7's fusion goes**
    (§2.7: `sealoop` 6 319–6 839 after phase 6, and 7 819–8 339 with phase 7's fusion estimate of
    1 500, up to 9 089 under stress; its increments have missed their upper ends by up to 52 %).
    Options: (a) **write the gate's conditions now in Decision 71's form (each program ≤ 7 000 built
    lines after phase 6 except `sealower` and `seacheck`, Decisions 50 and 82, ≤ 9 000 with its
    remaining phases' estimates and with them × 1.5, 2 free numeric array letters except where
    waived); if `sealoop` fails the stress condition, the letter condition or both, and nothing
    else, phase 7's fusion gets a pass of its own ahead of `sealoop`, and that pass also takes L19:
    it reads `sea.hir`, where an elemental application is still an `emap`, and LANGUAGE.md §8.5
    requires elemental applications to fuse with the element-wise expression around them, so the
    pass treats an `emap` as a k-result element-wise operator, writes the fused broadcast nest with
    the per-element call, and leaves only that call to `sealoop`'s L20 (`sealoop` loses L19's
    180–350 lines in phase 7 and is gated with 1 000 of fixes); the measurement after 6c may bring
    this decision forward when `sealoop`'s measured 6b + 6c increment exceeds 1.5 times its estimate
    (a projection after 6d above 7 000 is relieved by a compaction instead, since the seam takes L19
    out of `sealoop` only in phase 7; wording clarified after the final review)**; (b) decide now that fusion is a new pass (with L19);
    (c) leave the question to phase 7's specification. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); `sealoop`'s
    projections have been the least reliable of all passes (4f 271 against 600–900, 4g-2 774
    against 315–510), so the decision is better taken on a measurement, and writing the condition
    and its consequence for L19 now means neither the gate nor the measurement needs a new question;
    (b) adds a pass and moves L19 before the numbers say it is needed; (c) leaves phase 6 closing
    without a rule for its largest risk, and phase 7 would then find L19 on the wrong side of the
    seam. Affects §2.7, §8 (rows 6c, 6e).
89. **What `make_dir` does when the directory or its parents exist or
    are missing** (LANGUAGE.md §10.10 said only that it creates a directory). Options: (a) **one
    level, as POSIX `mkdir(path, 0777)` under the umask; on any failure the errno is saved and the
    path is tested for a directory by `open(path, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY)` (closed at once): a
    directory is not an error (so `/` and `.` succeed alike on macOS, where `mkdir("/")` gives
    `EISDIR`, and Linux, `EEXIST`); otherwise `cannot create directory '<path>': <saved errno
    text>` (an existing file `File exists`, a missing parent `No such file or directory`); no parent
    is created**; (b) create missing parents, as `mkdir -p`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); the workloads
    create one output directory next to the program; the errors are the existing `CANNOT_MKDIR`
    message with the errno; testing with `open` rather than `stat` avoids the targets' different
    `struct stat` layouts and glibc's versioned `stat` symbols, and testing after any failure rather
    than only after `EEXIST` makes both targets agree; (b) needs a loop over path components with
    its own error rules (which component failed, races between them) that no workload needs.
    Affects LANGUAGE.md §10.10 (one sentence), §2.11.6 (`MAKE_DIR`).
90. **The existing dump tests that §8.6 inlining changes** (§6.2; the
    review found 21 lowering dump tests whose function §8.6 (b) or (c) covers, and about 70 `.res`
    and 51 `.hir1` goldens that `el` 2 and the kind `inl` may change). Options: (a) **re-derive every
    affected golden by hand from the rules; in the 12 tests whose subject is a call boundary (a
    §3.6.6 rule's verbatim example written inside a function, a `ref` parameter root, a
    multiple-result call bound by L12, calls inside a selection) make the function non-inlinable
    with a second call site at the end of `.main` and a `while false` loop with an empty body as its
    first statement, so the test keeps its subject; in the other 9 let the function be inlined and
    re-derive with L20's form; integrate T2's goldens with WP-NAME, WP-CHECK, WP-LOOP and WP-LOWER in
    one step (wording corrected after the final review)**; (b) a
    test-only driver option `--no-inline` (with `el` 0 and kind `fn` written) that the existing dump
    tests use through a `.meta` line, so their goldens stay as they are; (c) re-derive all of them
    with inlining, including the call-boundary tests. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); the tests keep testing
    what their `tests/CORPUS.md` row says, on the configuration users run; the work is mechanical
    (the class is decided on the source by §2.11.3's rules); (b) is the least work but adds a CLI
    option, a pass flag and a harness attribute to maintain, and tests a configuration no program
    is built with; (c) loses the coverage of call lowering that those 12 tests give (the verbatim
    examples of rules 15, 18, 23, 24, 29, 32 and 33 would no longer match their rule's text).
    Affects §3.6.6, §6.2, §8 (row 6b), L-ct.
91. **Where a parameter default's value is checked** (§2.11.2; the
    review found that the first text, which put every default check into `seaname`, needs what
    only `seacheck` has: the types of the default's expression (201 against the parameter's type)
    and the reporting of constant outcomes; `seaname` evaluates the `const` items into `rcn…`
    records, but `sea.res` carries no outcome for a default, and the errors of constants are
    `seacheck`'s, Decision 25; wording corrected after the final review, the decision unchanged). Options: (a) **`seaname` keeps
    the structural checks of the signature step (236, 227 at a `ref` parameter's default, the names
    resolved like a `const` value's); `seacheck` checks each default's value where it checks the
    `const` items (237, 201, 260, 261, a constant's outcome used as Decision 25 says), each error
    competing in source order as every other (§2.6.2)**; (b) all in `seaname`, which would then
    need the expression types and its own reporting of 201, 237, 260 and 261 (duplicating
    `seacheck`'s typing); (c) all in
    `seaname`, with defaults restricted to literals and constant names checked only for their
    type. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); the value check is the `const` check whose
    typing and reporting live in `seacheck` (which evaluates a default's `i64` operations itself,
    as for a `dim:` value), and
    the source-order rule already orders a default's error against a constant's (a default's error
    on line 50 loses to a constant's on line 1); it moves 40–80 lines from `seaname` to `seacheck`
    (counted in §2.7, and within Decision 82 (a)'s conditions); (b) duplicates the typing; (c)
    narrows LANGUAGE.md §8.1's "a constant default". Affects §2.11.2, §2.7, L-bx.
92. **An elemental function without results** (LANGUAGE.md §8.5
    required results "one result or a tuple" without saying whether none is allowed; L19 was
    written for k ≥ 1). Options: (a) **allowed: called with scalars it is an ordinary call
    statement; called with arrays it is applied at every element position for its errors only (it
    has no effects), with L19's k = 0 form (no result allocated, the inlined call as a statement)**;
    (b) forbidden: 253 at the `fn` item (the text `elemental function result must be f64, i64 or
    bool` then also covers "no result"). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); it is the regular case of the rule
    (k results, k = 0), costs a few lines in L19, and makes an elemental validation routine
    (`check_ranges(x)` that calls `error` on a bad element) possible; (b) is simpler by those few
    lines but forbids a well-defined program for no semantic reason. Affects LANGUAGE.md §8.5 (one
    sentence), §2.11.2, §2.11.4 (L19).
93. **A named argument for a `ref` parameter** (Appendix A's `arg`
    does not let `name: ref x` parse, so a `ref` parameter cannot be given by name at all; the
    first text gave 254, `argument for ref parameter '%s' must be marked ref`, whose advice cannot
    be followed). Options: (a) **keep the grammar: a `ref` parameter is given positionally only,
    LANGUAGE.md §8.1 says so, and `name: x` for a `ref` parameter is 254 at x (the message names the
    parameter; the sentence in §8.1 explains it)**; (b) extend Appendix A so that `name: ref x`
    parses (pass 1, about 20–40 lines, and 115's start set), making named `ref` arguments legal;
    (c) report a named `ref` argument as 224 `unknown parameter`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-26); no workload
    passes a `ref` argument by name, the grammar has been fixed since phase 1 (`seaparse` has no
    other phase-6 change), and 254 at least names the parameter; (b) is a clean extension that can
    come later without breaking a program; (c) is wrong (the parameter exists). Affects LANGUAGE.md
    §8.1 (one sentence), §2.11.2, L-bw.

**Decisions of phase 7** (written 2026-10-29 with the text of §2.12, revised after two reviews,
and decided by the user on 2026-10-29, each as option (a)). Each lists its options with the
recommendation as (a), its reasons, the decision, and what it affects.

94. **Where fusion lives** (§2.7, "Projected for phase 7": fusion re-estimated at 1 650–2 980
    lines in its own program, about 1 570–2 880 inside `sealoop`, against the 1 500 carried since the
    pass-3a split). Options: (a) **a new program of pass 3a, `seafuse` (`sea.hir` → `sea.hirf`, ahead
    of `sealoop`), holding F1–F5 and L19 with `ind2sub`'s array form, rewritten there to emit the
    per-element `call` that `sealoop`'s L20 inlines (§2.12.3); `sealoop` keeps L1–L18 and L20 and
    is gated with 1 000 of fixes: Decision 88's consequence, applied to the realistic estimate**;
    (b) a behaviour-neutral compaction of `sealoop` first (a sub-phase 7b-0 as 4h-0, C1, C2, C4, C6
    on its `GOSUB` style, an estimated 400–700 lines), then fusion in `sealoop`; (c) fusion in
    `sealoop` as it is, its 7 000 condition replaced by Decision 50's two 9 000 conditions.
    Recommended: (a), as the only option whose projection can pass, not one with room to spare:
    `seafuse` is 4 870–7 150 after phase 7 (150 over 7 000 at the upper end, under both 9 000
    conditions with 850 and 350 to spare), `sealoop` 6 292–6 892 (108 under 7 000 at the upper end);
    a 52 % overrun of `seafuse`'s 7c increment, as `sealoop`'s worst, would break it, hence the
    measurement after 7c and Decision 112. (b) leaves `sealoop` 7 382–8 992, over 7 000 at both ends
    and over 9 000 with its fixes at the upper end; (c) gives 8 082–9 392, over both 9 000 conditions
    at both ends (9 082–10 392 and 9 582–10 892), so §7.3's split would fire mid-phase. (a)'s costs:
    a new intermediate file (`sea.hirf`, the records of `sea.hir` and set `HL`: no new record), a
    driver step, an `--emit` kind, L19 written a second time in `seafuse` with its own helpers
    (300–600 lines that duplicate `sealoop`'s, which L7, L12 and L20 keep using), the `.l`
    renumbering of Decision 109 and the `HL` copying of Decision 110. Under (b) or (c), §2.12.3 is
    dropped, F1–F5 become `sealoop`'s rewrites L21–L25 (run before L18 and L20 inline, so Decision
    110 still applies), and `sealoop` reads `sea.hir` as now. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §0, §2.1, §2.2, §2.6.3, §2.7,
    §2.10, §2.12, §3.4's file table, §3.5.9, §3.9, §6.2, §8 (rows 7b, 7c).
95. **The semantic contract of fusion** (§2.12.2; LANGUAGE.md fixes the order of an element-wise
    tree only through "operands left to right" and the reference's operator-by-operator loops, so a
    tree with a failing operation that is followed by another loop or check, or that runs over a
    different space than the fused nest, reports different errors when fused). Options: (a)
    **fusion keeps the reference's observable order exactly: leaves and checks in post-order
    before one nest, no check added; quiet nodes (by element type: §2.12.2) fuse anywhere; a failing
    node fuses only as the root of a standalone statement or of its group's last statement, and only
    when nothing that can fail follows its loop (a selection store's checks count, so such a root
    with a selection target is computed into RES first); a failing reduction likewise; everything
    else stays a barrier**; (b) LANGUAGE.md §6.2 is amended to define a whole tree's order as the
    fused one (leaves, all checks, then the elements in increasing linear order, each computing the
    tree in post-order), so every tree fuses and the reference changes with it (some `errors/`
    goldens and L7's form re-derived); (c) fuse only quiet nodes (no failing node ever fused).
    Recommended: (a); no error test changes, the workloads' trees (all `f64`, quiet `shaft_safety`)
    fuse fully, and the condition is checkable on the tree: a failing root runs over exactly its own
    reference space, so it can neither be skipped by an empty broadcast nor overtake a later check;
    (b) changes the language for an optimization; (c) is simpler by the qualifying walk (about 40–80
    lines) and loses only failing roots (an `i64` index computation over a whole array that ends a
    statement). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.2, §2.12.4 (F1 (2), F2 (4), F3), §6.2 (`r_fuse_*`), §5.1.
96. **Adjacent-statement fusion: iteration space and targets** (§2.12.4 F2). Options: (a) **each
    group statement keeps exactly its own reference checks; the group adds one quiet run-time test
    that every statement's root extents equal the first's: if it holds, the fused nest; if not, a
    split copy that runs each statement's own nest over its own space and stores every local; a
    whole-array target written in place when a run-time test finds it has the space's extents (made
    unique by `cow`), else given a new array before the nest (`anew`, the old value read through a
    held `O`), at most one write of each target per group; a matrix nest in a plain copy
    (unit-stride, no broadcast) and a broadcast copy chosen at run time**; (b) static shape facts
    only: a group or an in-place target only where `seafuse` proves the extents equal (same variable,
    fixed-size shapes, results of element-wise operations of one variable, a loop-invariant shape
    carried around a loop), no run-time test, no split copy and one nest; (c) statement fusion only
    in phase 7 (no F2). Recommended: (a); it adds no check (the first draft's "each statement checked
    against the first's space" would have added `shape mismatch` errors the reference never reports,
    for `let a = x * 2.0; let b = y * 3.0` with different lengths), covers W1's loop (whose `lo` and
    `hi` shapes are carried around a loop) and W4's slices with no shape analysis, at the price of a
    run-time test and up to three nests per group (code size only); (b) needs a loop-carried shape
    analysis in a HIR pass (an estimated 300–500 lines more) and still misses shapes that depend on
    run-time values; (c) leaves W1's bisection allocating `mid`, `nfv`, `nyv`, `up` in every
    iteration, so row 7's "done when" fails. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.4, §5.4, §6.2.
97. **The dump goldens that fusion and pass 3d change** (§2.12.10). Options: (a) **re-derive every
    changed golden by hand from §2.12; a test whose subject is the unfused form (an agreed rule
    example, L7's, L13's and L19's tests) is rewritten to keep its subject (its statements separated
    by a `printf` of one element, which ends any group; each tree one that `seafuse` leaves to L7)
    and re-derived; the 29 `NAME.lir` goldens with a `NAME.lir2` renamed `NAME.lir3` with a new
    `NAME.lir`; T2 lists each change with its rule**; (b) a test-only driver option `--no-fuse` (and
    `--no-vec`) that the existing dump tests use through a `.meta` line, their goldens unchanged; (c)
    re-derive all with fusion, including the subject tests. Recommended: (a), Decision 90's
    precedent: the tests keep testing what their `tests/CORPUS.md` row says on the configuration
    users run; the churn is small (the review counted fusion changing `elem6_inst`, `elem6_k5`,
    `elem6_vec`, `ew_colrow` among the dump tests, about 7 of the 29 `.lir` goldens having loops T13
    may vectorize, about 60 mechanical renames and 15–25 hand derivations; about 48 of 310 programs
    contain a tree `seafuse` rewrites, their outputs unchanged); (b) adds options, pass flags and
    harness keys for a configuration no program is built with; (c) loses the coverage of L7's and
    L13's own forms. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.10, §6.2, §8 (rows 7b, 7c, 7e).
98. **Pass 3d's open items** (Decision 78 left them to this specification). Options: (a) **name
    `seavec`; `sealopt` writes `sea.lir3`, `seavec` reads it and writes `sea.lir`, which stays the
    final LIR that pass 4 reads and `--emit lir` dumps; `--emit lir3` new; files
    `passes/seavec/ve*.bas`, `SUB` prefix `ve_`, own lines 100 – 59 999, build list `lib io diag
    tables lirrw`, `data errors exits consts entries records`; at the gates 1 000 of fixes after
    phase 7 and no letter condition (its tables take the `S V` that L-bp leaves, as `sealopt`'s did,
    Decision 78)**; (b) `seavec` writes a new final file (`sea.lirv`) that pass 4 reads, `sea.lir`
    staying `sealopt`'s output and `--emit lir` unchanged; (c) the same file names as (a) but no
    `--emit lir3`. Recommended: (a); `passes.txt`'s set `LF` ("`sea.lir` only") keeps its meaning,
    pass 4's input name does not change, and the renaming touches 29 goldens (those with both a
    `NAME.lir2` and a `NAME.lir`; `lir4_seaopt` has no `NAME.lir`); (b) changes the meaning of `LF`
    and pass 4's file name; (c) leaves `sealopt`'s output undumpable, which the stage tests need.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.1, §2.2, §2.6.3, §2.7, §2.10, §2.12.6, §3's introduction, §3.4's file table, §3.6.5,
    §3.9, §6.2, §8.
99. **Does pass 3d's output depend on the target, and how are its goldens named?** (§3.6.5 says a
    vectorized loop is multiversioned on `x86_64-linux`; every LIR pass so far was
    target-independent.) Options: (a) **yes: on `arm64-macos` T13 writes the 2-lane loop only; on
    `x86_64-linux` the 4-lane loop and the 2-lane loop under `vfeat`; the `_y` entries exist on
    `x86_64-linux` only; a dump or pass-4 test of target-specific LIR has its `x86_64-linux` file as
    `NAME.lirx64` (an extension `stage.sh`'s `*.lir` loop does not match), and `stage.sh` and
    `run.sh` gain the rules of §2.12.10 (L-fc)**; (b) no: `seavec` always writes both versions under
    `vfeat`, and `seagen_a64` treats `vfeat` as 0 and writes nothing for its first part (one golden);
    (c) no AVX2 in phase 7: one 2-lane version on both targets (SSE2 on x86_64), `vfeat` unused
    until a later phase. Recommended: (a); each target gets only code it can run and the arm64 code
    generator needs no 4-lane knowledge; the first draft's `NAME.x64.lir` would have been run by
    `stage.sh` as an arm64 pass-4 test; (b) makes pass 4 drop blocks, which no pass-4 rule does yet,
    and gives arm64 a dead test per loop; (c) is smaller (no AVX2 code in `seagen_x64`, no `_y`
    entries, no variant testing: about 400–700 lines less in all) but leaves row 7's "SSE2 + AVX2
    multiversioning" undone. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.6–§2.12.8, §2.12.10, §3.6.5, §4.4, §6.2, `tests/stage.sh`,
    `tests/run.sh`.
100. **What T13 vectorizes** (§2.12.6). Options: (a) **innermost unit-stride loops whose body is one
     region of the vector set after if-conversion of quiet blocks (Decision 108): `f64` arithmetic,
     `sqrt`, `min`/`max`, comparisons, selections, mask logic, unit `f64` and `bool` accesses, the six
     elementary functions; 8 elements per vector iteration (four 2-lane or two 4-lane copies) with a
     scalar tail, independence tested at run time by address distances (the new LIR record
     `pdiff`); no rounding instructions, no `itof`, no `i64` lanes, no strided or gathered access**;
     (b) (a) plus the rounding instructions and `itof` (SSE2 has neither `roundpd` nor a 64-bit
     packed conversion: per-lane sequences in pass 4, about 150–250 lines in `seagen_x64`); (c) one
     vector per iteration (2 or 4 elements), no unrolling. Recommended: (a); it covers the
     workloads' fused plain loops, every instruction maps to one exact vector instruction or a fixed
     exact sequence (§2.12.7), and the run-time distance test needs no alias analysis (`pdiff` is the
     one contract addition); (b) adds code no workload needs yet; (c) cannot keep `sum`'s eight
     lanes and halves the work per loop test. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.1, §2.12.6, §2.12.7, `passes.txt`
     (`pdiff`), §3.6.4.
101. **Which reductions are vectorized** (LANGUAGE.md §10.5 pins every reduction's order).
     Options: (a) **only `sum`'s 8-lane accumulation (L13's sum8 group, in `sum`, `mean`,
     `variance`, `std` and F3's unmasked fused forms), whose lanes are exactly the pinned lanes, so
     the vector and scalar forms give the same bits for every width; every other carried value,
     F3's masked sums included (their lane is the counter Q, not the index), stays scalar**; (b)
     none; (c) also `max`/`min` by lane maxima and a sequential fix-up of ties and NaN (first index,
     NaN skipped, ±0 order). Recommended: (a); it is bit-identical by construction and costs about
     100–150 lines of T13; (b) leaves W5's means and variances (1 M elements) scalar; (c) needs a
     second pass or per-lane index tracking to restore LANGUAGE.md's first-maximum and ±0 rules,
     for little gain. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.6 (5), §6.2.
102. **Scalar replacement in phase 7** (row 7 names it; §5.3; no done-when of phase 7 needs it, W3
     and W2 of phase 8 do). Options: (a) **in phase 7 as T11 (full unrolling of innermost constant
     loops of at most 8 iterations over slots, with carried registers threaded through the copies)
     and T12 (slots accessed only at constant offsets, one class per location and no partial
     overlap, become registers), in `seavec`**; (b) deferred to phase 8, specified with W3 and W2
     that need it; (c) T12 only, without unrolling (only accesses with constant indices before
     unrolling). Recommended: (a), narrowly: row 7 and Decision 78 placed it in pass 3d, and its
     tests (`sr7_*`, W3's `f64[4]` shape in miniature) need no phase-8 feature; but (b) is a sound
     choice the review called acceptable, and it removes 350–650 lines and their risk from phase 7
     (`seavec` 4 230–5 290) at no cost to phase 7's done-when, which the user may prefer if
     Decision 112's relief is needed; (c) catches nothing in L7's fixed-size loops, which index
     with the loop variable. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.6, §5.3, §8 (rows 7e, 8).
103. **The vector forms of the elementary functions** (§4.10.1 "Vector forms"). Options: (a) **SIMD
     forms per lane of §4.10's text (branches as selects, per-lane table loads, rare lanes through the
     scalar entry), 2-lane on both targets and 4-lane on `x86_64-linux`, tested bit for bit against
     the scalar entries on the committed vectors and a seeded random differential test; (b) is the
     agreed fallback, per function, if (a) threatens the phase**; (b) wrappers that call the scalar
     entry once per lane (bit-identical by construction, about 60 lines per target), the SIMD forms
     left to phase 10's benchmarks; (c) no vector forms: a loop with an elementary function is not
     vectorized. Recommended: (a) with (b) as fallback; row 7 and goal 1 ask for it and W5's 3 M
     `log` and `cos` are where it pays; it is the largest runtime work of the phase (an estimated
     1 200–2 000 lines on arm64 and 2 000–3 500 on x86_64) and its largest risk (SSE2 has no
     `pcmpgtq`, `roundpd`, `pinsrq` or 64-bit packed conversion and NEON no 64 × 64-bit multiply,
     so some steps need exact multi-instruction sequences or per-lane scalar calls); the entries and
     tests are the same under (b), so a function can fall back without a contract change. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects
     §2.12.8, §4.10, §6.2.
104. **How both x86_64 variants are tested.** Options: (a) **`make cross` runs every program,
     error, passes and ports case under the default variant (`avx2` on the host) and again under
     `SEA_KERNELS=sse2`, against the same expected files; the host must offer AVX2 (setup error
     otherwise); `math_check` runs its 4-lane part**; (b) only the `vec_*`, `gen7_*` and port cases
     under `sse2`; (c) one variant per run, with a separate `make cross-sse2`. Recommended: (a); a
     second run of the run half costs about a minute on the host (the compilation, which dominates,
     is shared), and every program then proves the class-E identity of §6.6 for both variants as
     §6.6's first bullet requires (the runtime selects its variant from `SEA_KERNELS` at start-up,
     so the `sse2` run also switches the matrix kernels; their class-R tests use exact data, so
     their expected files stay valid); (b) misses vectorized loops in programs not named `vec_*`; (c) lets a variant go
     untested. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §6.6.1, §8.
105. **How "no temporaries" is checked** (row 7's done-when says "no temporaries in `-S` output").
     Options: (a) **a run-time count: `SEA_HEAP_CHECK=count` makes the runtime print `heap: <a>
     allocations, <l> live objects`, a counting every object created, copies made by
     `sea_arr_unique` included; two programs with W1's bisection loop and W4's red-black iteration
     at the ports' sizes run with k and k + 1 iterations, and the difference must equal the
     hand-derived allocations per iteration (W1 0, W4 6); row 7's wording is read as "no temporary
     allocated by the compiled code", which this checks on the paths the run takes**; (b) a static
     check: `alloc` lines in `tests/shape/NAME.shape` counting the allocation `rcall`s whose site
     lies in a line range of the program in `--emit lir`, compared with a hand-derived n, and the
     `-S` text's call count of the allocation entries; (c) committed `sea.lir` goldens of the ports.
     Recommended: (a); a static count of allocation sites counts the fallback `anew`s of the reuse
     prologue and the split copy that the run never takes, cannot see a copy on write, and must
     attribute inlined code by the callee's lines in the caller; the run-time difference is exact,
     needs no whole-port total, and its numbers follow from T2 and the agreed rules; it changes the
     runtime (§4.5: a new value of the existing switch; `1` and every other value unchanged, so
     `heap_env_other`, which uses `2`, still expects nothing), owned by a 7f package; (b) checks the
     words of row 7 literally but with the blind spots above; (c) commits thousands of lines that
     every pass change re-derives. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.10, §4.5, §6.2, §8 (row 7's "done when" text is
     amended to "no temporary allocated, by the count of §2.12.10").
106. **How phase 7 is built** (§8). Options: (a) **the sub-phases 7a (specification), 7b (contract
     and the two new programs, behaviour-neutral: L19 rewritten in `seafuse`, `.l` renumbering,
     `seavec` copying, the renamed goldens), 7c (fusion, L18/L20's copying in `sealoop`, then the
     measurement after 7c), 7d (the vector forms of the runtime, in parallel with 7c), 7e (`lirrw`
     first, then `seavec`'s T11–T13, pass 4's vector code and the harness), 7f (the heap count, the
     W4 port, the temporaries and vector checks, acceptance, the gate after phase 7), each with work
     packages owning disjoint files (§8 rows 7b–7f)**; (b) one build after 7a with every package in
     parallel; (c) vectorization before fusion. Recommended: (a); 7b proves the new pipeline neutral
     before any rewrite changes output; 7d touches only the runtimes and the math test, so it can
     run beside 7c; 7e needs 7c's fused nests to have something to vectorize in the ports; (b) puts
     several packages into the same passes at once; (c) would vectorize only L7's single-operation
     loops first and re-derive the vector goldens after fusion. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §8.
107. **The form of W4's red-black half sweep** (LANGUAGE.md §2.4 writes it with `ref T` and `where`;
     the MATLAB script returns `[T, dMax]`). Options: (a) **as LANGUAGE.md §2.4 writes it: `fn
     rb_half_sweep(ref T: f64[,], src: f64[,], colorIn: bool[,], omega: f64) -> f64`, the store
     `T[1..ny-1, :] = where(colorIn, Tn, Tc)`**; (b) MATLAB's copy-in/copy-out, `fn
     rb_half_sweep(T: f64[,], …) -> (f64[,], f64)` with `Tc[colorIn] = Tn[colorIn]` and `T[1..ny-1,
     :] = Tc`, called as `(T, d1) = rb_half_sweep(T, …)`; (c) both, (b) as a `fuse_*` test.
     Recommended: (a); it is the documented Sea idiom (LANGUAGE.md §8.3), computes the same values
     in the same order, and needs no copy of `T` per call; (b) is closer to the MATLAB text but its
     masked store is not element-wise over the space (a selection store of a selection), so F2's group
     would end before it. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.10, the port.
108. **Must the workloads' fused loops vectorize, and how?** (§2.12.6; T13 as first drafted
     accepted no block in a loop body, but W1's fused nest holds `shaft_safety`'s inlined `if`
     chains, so as drafted W1 would fuse and never vectorize.) Options: (a) **yes, for W1's
     bisection nest and W4's selection store and `residual`: T13 first if-converts, in an innermost
     step-1 loop, every `if`/`ifz` block whose parts hold only vector-set instructions (no store, no
     failing instruction, no call with a site) into both parts computed and `fsel` merges, which
     LANGUAGE.md §6.10 allows for arms that cannot fail; folded and whole-array leaves of a plain
     copy give T7's unit form `ldf D J 8 0` (§5.8), which T13 requires; W4's group nest (a masked
     `max` carried under an `if`) stays scalar; `vector` lines in `tests/shape/` check W1's nest and
     W4's store on both targets**; (b) no if-conversion: only loops without blocks vectorize, so W1's
     nest stays scalar (fused, no temporaries) and W4's store and `residual` vectorize; the shape
     lines check W4 only; (c) where-conversion in `seafuse`: an `if` expression of quiet arms inside
     a fused tree is written as `where` over both arms' elements (HIR), so the LIR has no block to
     convert. Recommended: (a); row 7's "done when" names fusion, and goal 1 wants W1's grid computed
     in vector registers; if-conversion of quiet store-free blocks is a small T13 step (150–300
     lines, in §2.7's `seavec` estimate) and exact by construction (each lane takes the scalar arm's
     value); (b) is smaller but leaves the workload with the most element-wise work scalar; (c) puts
     a LIR concern into the HIR and needs `seafuse` to see through inlined bodies, which it does not
     (L20 inlines after it). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.6, §2.12.10, §2.7, §6.2. Amended by Decision 115
     (T13's preparation, 2026-10-31).
109. **`.l` local numbering across `seafuse` and `sealoop`, and what "neutral" means for 7b.**
     (§3.5.9 "Locals" numbers `.l` locals in file order; in `elem6_vec.hirl` L19's and L20's locals
     interleave, so any scheme in which the two programs number separately permutes the names and
     changes `sea.hirl`, `sea.lir1` and every later file even where nothing is fused.) Options: (a)
     **`sealoop` renumbers every `.l` local of its output in file order (the order of first
     appearance in the written file), whichever program created it, so `sea.hirl` keeps §3.5.9's
     canonical numbering; 7b is neutral when `sea.hirl`, `sea.lir1`, `sea.lir2`, `sea.lir3`, `sea.lir`
     and every diagnostic are byte-identical over the corpus before and after**; (b) `sealoop`
     continues `seafuse`'s numbering (the first draft's L-ej), §3.5.9 "Locals" amended, and 7b's
     neutrality defined as byte-identical `sea.lir*` and diagnostics with `sea.hirl` identical up to a
     renaming of `.l` locals (checked by a renaming-aware comparison in the test harness), the
     affected `.hirl`, `.lir1`, `.lir2`, `.lir3`, `.lir` goldens re-derived; (c) `seafuse` creates no
     `.l` locals (it writes its locals as source-free `.t` locals, numbered by `seaexpand`'s rule).
     Recommended: (a); one renumbering pass on output (40–80 lines in `sealoop`, in §2.7's estimate)
     keeps every file canonical, makes 7b checkable byte for byte with L-p's method, and frees later
     passes from the order in which the two programs ran; (b) needs a renaming-aware comparison and
     re-derives goldens for no change of behaviour; (c) misuses `.t` locals, whose meaning
     `seaexpand` fixes (§3.5.8). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.3, §3.5.9 "Locals", §6.2, §8 (row 7b).
     **Built at 7b (2026-10-29):** "file order" is the order of the declaring records of the `.l`
     locals (L-fn); two exceptions agreed by the user, 2026-10-29: a `tret` of an `emap` inside an
     `inl`/`elem` function, and the positions of capacity diagnostics (§2.12.3).
110. **Inlining of fused bodies** (`seafuse` runs before `sealoop`'s L18 (prelude) and L20 (§8.6);
     W4's `rb_half_sweep` is class (c) of §8.6 and inlined at both call sites, and `lpainl.bas`'s
     copier knows only the local fields of `lv bind forr fore tmp tbind`). Options: (a) **`seafuse`
     fuses every function, those of kind `inl` and `elem` and the prelude's included; L18 and L20
     copy the `HL` records of `sea.hirf` like any record, renaming every local field (`tmp`,
     `hloop`, `rcnt`'s two local ids, the `lv`s reading them), a callee's `.l` local becoming a new
     `.i` local of the caller; a `sealoop` work package joins 7c for it (80–200 lines)**; (b)
     `seafuse` skips the bodies of functions `sealoop` will inline (kind `inl`, `elem`, the prelude):
     no copying change, but W4's half sweep (and any inlined helper) is not fused, so W4's
     temporaries check fails; (c) inlining moves into `seafuse` (L18 and L20 run there, before
     fusion), so fusion sees inlined code and `sealoop` copies nothing: L18 and L20 (about 900 lines
     with their helpers) move out of `sealoop`, and `seafuse` grows by the same, over 7 000 at both
     ends. Recommended: (a); it is the smallest change that fuses W4 and keeps both programs within
     their projections; (b) fails row 7's done-when for W4; (c) does not fit `seafuse`. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects
     §2.12.3, §3.5.9 (L18, L20, "Locals"), §2.7, §8 (row 7c). **Amended 2026-10-29 (agreed by the
     user, at 7b):** the copying is built in 7b, not 7c, because 7b's `seafuse` already writes L19's
     `HL` records into `inl` and `elem` bodies; and a copied callee `.l` local becomes a new caller
     **`.l`** local (one per inlined call, renumbered in declaring-record order with the caller's own;
     `loc` position P under L18, the callee local's own position under L20), not a `.i` local,
     which keeps `sea.hirl` neutral. The 7c work package for it is therefore void.
111. **Which trees `seafuse` rewrites; single-node matrix trees** (§2.12.4; the first draft left
     every one-node tree to L7, but L7 writes a matrix tree as one `mloop` with broadcast strides,
     which T7 cannot make unit-stride, and it leaves the value of an `asg set` to a temporary, so
     W4's store `T[1..ny-1, :] = where(colorIn, Tn, Tc)` would allocate). Options: (a) **`seafuse`
     rewrites every tree with two or more fusible nodes, a folded leaf, a matrix space, or that is
     the value of an `asg set` to a whole array or a selection or of a group statement; only a
     vector tree of one fusible node with no folded leaf that is not such a value is left to L7,
     whose form is then exactly F1's (L-em)**; (b) `seafuse` rewrites every tree, one-node ones
     included, and L7 is reached only by trees F1 does not qualify; (c) the first draft's rule (every
     one-node tree to L7), with L7 extended to write the plain and broadcast copies and the in-place
     selection store. Recommended: (a); it changes no golden whose tree L7 already writes in F1's
     form (the vector ones) and gives every matrix tree and every store the plain copy and the
     in-place store; (b) re-derives many more L7 goldens for identical output; (c) grows `sealoop`
     (108 lines under 7 000 at its upper end) and duplicates F1. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.12.4, §2.12.10, §6.2.
112. **`seafuse`'s room: the relief if it does not fit** (§2.7: 4 870–7 150 built after phase 7,
     150 over 7 000 at the upper end; free letters 3–6 after 7b and 0–5 after 7c). Options: (a)
     **decided now so that 7b and 7c need no new agreement to proceed: (1) letters: F1–F5's tables
     are written as columns of two-dimensional arrays from the start; if `seafuse` has fewer than 2
     free letters after 7b, its reader's per-node arrays are packed into columns of one array before

     concatenation parts and V-kind gathers are removed from phase 7 first (an estimated 150–250

     Decision 50's form (no 7 000 condition, the two 9 000 conditions kept), each with the user's
     agreement recorded before 7e's code**; (b) Decision 50's form for `seafuse` now, and the letter
     condition waived for it (as for `sealopt`); (c) cut scope now: F4's concatenation parts,
     V-kind gathers and F5 inside trees left to a later phase (about 250–400 lines less; W1's
     elemental call stays fused through L20's inlined body, so W1 is unaffected). Recommended: (a);
     it keeps the 7 000 condition as long as the measurement allows, cuts only what no workload's
     done-when needs, and fixes the order of reliefs before the code so an overrun does not stall
     the phase; (b) gives up the margin that the gate's 7 000 condition exists to keep, before any
     measurement; (c) gives up features that may well fit. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-29). Affects §2.7 ("The measurement after
     7c", "The gate after phase 7"), §2.12.4 (F4), §8 (rows 7b, 7c).
113. **`lirrw` and the vector classes** (`seavec` validates `sea.lir3` and writes `sea.lir` through
     `lirrw`, which knows only the classes `i f p`; `lirrw` is part of `seaopt`, `sealopt` and

     (row 7e), `passes/lib/API.md`. Amended by Decision 116 (2026-10-31: the vector output is validated in

115. **How T13 reaches the loops Decision 108 promises** (2026-10-31; §2.12.6). An analysis of
    `sea.lir3` at 7c's commit found that T13 as agreed vectorizes none of them: W1's nest holds the
    `do` blocks of `shaft_safety`'s inlined returns (L20) and `&&` conditions that write their own
    condition register, and reads `pGrid`'s fields through a slot that is no private base; W4's
    selection store reads its plain arm at `seafuse`'s linear counter O and `residual` through a row
    counter K, neither a unit access; their steps, and T7's walked bases over unit-step slices, are
    `mov`s of `li`s that the Terms' "constant" does not cover. Options: (a) **amendments in `seavec`
    only (WP-VEC): T13's constants as L-br's reading extended; P1 dissolving inlined-return `do`
    blocks; P2 normalizing counters and walked bases to unit accesses; P3 invariant loads of never
    written parameters and slot `sa` bases; mask merges `iand bnot iand ior` in the if-conversion,
    a part that writes the condition register writing a renamed one; the preparation kept only on a
    loop that is then vectorized, the tail and `else` loop being L after P1 and P2 without the
    if-conversion**; (b) fixes at the origin: `seafuse` reading the plain arm at the loops'
    inductions, T3 propagating copies across regions or L-br extended to T7's k and c, T9
    restricted to `loop`s (re-derives the `hirf`, `hirl` and `lir1`–`lir3` goldens of every fused
    selection store and of every loop T3 or T9 touches, and reopens 7c's passes); (c) narrow
    Decision 108 to what T13 as agreed vectorizes (W1's nest, W4's store and `residual` stay
    scalar, and the `vector` shape lines lose their subjects). Recommended: (a); it changes only
    `seavec`'s output, and only for loops it vectorizes (no `lir1`, `lir2` or `lir3` golden
    changes), each rule moves or renames instructions without changing any operation or address
    (bit-identity, LANGUAGE.md §6.8 4.), and no failing instruction is speculated. **Decided: (a)**
    (the user, 2026-10-31), written with the lead's readings that make the rules exact, and with the
    fixes of an independent review of that text (2026-10-31): P1 only on a `do` whose body ends in
    its `exit` with every `exit` in tail position, nothing duplicated; P2 only with step 1 and S, C,
    T invariant, one `isub E K S` per counter, a walked base with exactly two definitions, scale 0
    and Δ the element size (a reverse walk refused), the counter's value after L restored as K₀ + C +
    1 only with the rewrite; P3 excluding stores through any `sa` register of the slot; the
    if-conversion merging every register read outside the part that writes it, in first-write order,
    the condition's merge last, the condition a mask register, condition 3 counting the writes before
    the conversion; the mask registers a greatest fixpoint, also written by `mov`; J not read after L;
    candidates taken from the function before T13, its own copies never revisited; condition 1
    without the guard pattern (§5.8's "before L"); a normative listing of the vector form (the split
    without forming n, the independence test's order, splats, sum8 homes, the tails, the `vfeat`
    layout, the copies' registers per L-bl). Second, T9 unswitches the inlined-return `do` (a `do`
    is a loop in §5.8's Terms), so W1's vector body calls `pow` three times per copy where the body
    without that split would call it twice (the scalar loop calls it once per element). Options: (a)
    **leave T9 as it is and measure W1's speed in 7f**; (b) restrict T9 to `loop`s now (`lir3`
    goldens change where T9 split a `do`). **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-31): T9 changes only
    by a later agreed decision (measured in 7f and decided as Decision 118: T9 restricted to
    `loop`s). Affects §2.7 (`seavec`'s estimate, +2 200–3 900, about 5 260–6 960 built, and its
    measurement after T13's legality code), §2.12.6 (T13), §2.12.10, §6.2 (`vec7_*`), §8 (rows 7e
    and 7f), L-fg; no contract file.

116. **How `seavec`'s vector output is validated** (2026-10-31; amends Decision 113 (a); §2.12.6).
    As built by WP-LIB, `lirrw`'s writer trusts the vector records `seavec` puts into its tables, and
    no pass reads `sea.lir` through `lirrw`'s `sea.lir` input kind, so Decision 113's "validates
    them in `sea.lir` output" held only for `tests/lib_check.sh`'s cases; pass 4 reads `sea.lir` with
    its own reader. Options: (a) **validation in the test harness: a small tool `tools/lirchk.bas`
    built with `lirrw` (no new validator) reads a `sea.lir` with the `sea.lir` input kind, and
    `tests/run.sh` and `tests/stage.sh` run it on every `sea.lir` they produce (WP-HARNESS); `seavec`
    does not re-validate at compile time**; (b) `seavec` reads its own `sea.lir` back through
    `lirrw` before it exits (20–40 lines, and its input read twice in every compilation); (c) only
    pass 4's own reader checks `sea.lir` (Decision 113's option (c)). Recommended: (a); it checks
    every vector record of the corpus with the one validator Decision 113 set up and costs no
    compile time; `seaval`'s format `lir` extended to `x y m` was not chosen, since `seaval` checks
    fields and register classes only and would be a second, weaker validator of the vector classes
    (no lane counts, no `vfeat` target, no parameter and argument rules); (b) doubles `seavec`'s
    read time; (c) leaves `seavec`'s output checked only by a second implementation. **Decided:
    (a)** (the user, 2026-10-31). Affects §2.6.3 (the tool's build list), §2.12.6, §8 (row 7e:
    WP-HARNESS and the done-when), L-gk; no contract file.

117. **T11 and T12 on compiled code; empty loops** (2026-10-31, after T2's and WP-VEC's builds;
    §2.12.6). T2 found, and the builds confirmed, that T11 and T12 as agreed never fire on code Sea
    compiles: a lowered loop's C is an `rcount` result (rule 4) or an `isub` of two `li`s (rule 17),
    never the Terms' constant, and every fixed-size array or struct is filled by an `mcopy` from its
    literal's slot (or from another such value), which T12 refused; so W3's `f64[4]` state, which
    §6.2 promises, was never scalar-replaced. First, options: (a) **extend T11 and T12 now: T11
    takes S and T as constants in the sense of "Constants in `seavec`" and a known iteration count n
    (1 ≤ n ≤ 8) from a constant C or an `rcount` of constant operands, folded exactly by LANGUAGE.md
    §5.1's element count (`st` = 0 and the empty range not unrolled), the guard and the `rcount`
    kept; T12 accepts *slot copies*, `mcopy`s between two replaced slots of a constant multiple of 8
    bytes, written as per-location `mov`s, the replaced slots the greatest set closed under slot
    copies, an `mcopy` to or from any other memory still refusing the slot**; (b) leave T11 and T12
    as agreed for v1 (they fire only on hand-written LIR). Recommended: (a); the rules stay small
    (+115–220 lines, §2.7), and both are exact: the copies run exactly when the loop would, and a
    `mov` copies the 64 bits the `mcopy` would. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-31). Second, a
    loop with an empty body (or with no unit access) met conditions 1–5 vacuously and got the whole
    vector form (`opt5_ovf_const`). Options: (a) **condition 1 also requires at least one unit
    access after P2**; (b) leave it. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-10-31): such a loop gains nothing
    from the form, and its goldens revert to `NAME.lir3`. Affects §2.7 (`seavec`, measured 5 498 built,
    about 5 613–5 718 with this decision), §2.12.6 ("Constants in `seavec`", T11, T12, T13 (1)),
    §6.2 (`vec7_*`, `sr7_*`); lead decisions L-gq–L-gy (and the lead's L-gz, L-ha within it); no contract file.

118. **T9 restricted to `loop` blocks** (2026-10-31, the measurement Decision 115 asked for in 7f;
    §5.8 T9, §2.12.6, §2.12.10). As built in 7e (Decision 115's option (a)), T9 unswitches
    `shaft_safety`'s inlined-return `do` in W1's bisection nest on `dmm > 51`, and the vector body
    then calls `sea_pow_x` (or `_y`) three times per element pair instead of twice. Measured in 7f
    with every `do` unswitch disabled: W1's compute time 35 ms with T9's split and 27 ms without
    it, the output byte-identical (median of 15 interleaved runs, arm64); the `do` records in W1's
    `sea.lir3` went from 47 to 37, and P1 then dissolves a single `do` where it dissolved both
    copies. Options: (a) leave T9 as it is (Decision 115's option (a)); (b) **restrict T9 to
    `loop`s: a `do` block (an inlined return, a `while` loop) is never unswitched**, Decision 115's
    option (b) "T9 restricted to `loop`s" alone, without its other fixes at the origin.
    (b) is one test in `sealopt` (`passes/sealopt/lo6t9.bas`), and the only goldens it changes
    are the `lir3`, `lir` and `lirx64` of `vec7_p1_guard` and `vec7_p1_kept` (§6.2), whose `do`
    T9 had split. **Decided: (b)** (the user, 2026-10-31). As built in 7f: on the final tree W1's
    compute time is 37 ms with the split and 29 ms without it, and its vector body calls `sea_pow`
    twice per copy in place of three times on both targets; `vec7_p1_guard`, which under (b) no
    longer reached P1 rule 2, was rewritten with goldens derived anew (`tests/CORPUS.md`, L-ib).
    Affects §2.12.6 ("What the
    workloads get"), §2.12.10 (the measurement), §5.8 (T9); no contract file.
119. **What a `vector` shape line requires of its loop** (2026-11-01, an independent review of
    7f's WP-SHAPE; §2.12.10, L-fl). As first written, a `vector` line passed on any innermost
    vectorized loop from its line range. The review confirmed that this admits loops that never
    run in the workload: a fused group's split copy (the `else` arm of its space test, the loops
    after `rcall sea_arr_new_u` at the group's line) is vectorized too and lies in the same range.
    For W4 over `rb_half_sweep`'s range, the winning candidates (L1_385 and L1_388 on `x86_64`,
    site 1:257, `add` and `mul`) belonged to the split copy, so the line passed without the store
    loops (site 1:261, `sel`); for W1 over 251–257, five split-copy loops qualified besides the
    fused body. The review also found that the specified site rule ("a site or neighbouring `ldx`")
    cannot hold, since `ldx` and the vector instructions have no site field and a vector body holds
    no failing instruction. Options: (a) **a `vector` line may list the lane ops its loop must hold
    (`add sub mul div min max sqrt neg abs cmp sel`); a candidate qualifies only when its LIR body
    holds every listed op, and each listed op must also appear in its lane form in the `-S`
    range**; (b) narrow line ranges only, with no op list; (c) keep the line as specified.
    **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-11-01). Written with the site rule as built (the loop's own
    site, else the nearest record with a site before its `loop` record): W4's line becomes `261 261
    sel` (only the store loops carry that site) and W1's keeps 251–257 with `sqrt`. Second, (a)
    cannot isolate W1's fused loop: the split copy's loop over `shaft_safety`'s inlined body holds
    the same lane ops as the fused body, only the counts differ, so W1's line also passes on that
    loop. Options: (a) **accept the gap and document it** (the `fusion` test, §2.12.10, shows that
    W1's grid bisection allocates nothing per iteration, so the fused path is the one that runs);
    (b) a further rule that tells the two loops apart. **Decided: (a)** (the user, 2026-11-01:
    accepted, documented). Affects §2.12.10 ("The vector check"), L-fl; no contract file.

120. **How 7g meets W7's feature gaps** (2026-11-01; §6.3 "Feature gaps W7 meets", §8 row 7g).
    Options: (a) **port-only, with no language, compiler, runtime or library change**: the port
    writes its own `interp1` with the pinned formula; it preallocates to the 326,700 candidates and
    keeps a count; it uses loops for `diff`; it uses `linspace` for the floating-point ranges; and
    it keeps one matrix per rolling-resistance case; (b) add a library `interp1(x, y, xq)` (class
