  numbered by §3.5.1 at its first reference; the moved path and value subtrees keep their own
  positions, every node step 4 creates is at P; `sealoop` rewrites the `fore` over `lv J2` by L4
  (its `.j` loop local kept, bound by a `tmp` of the element) and a `dyn` of a fixed field by L10;
  `bind J1`/`bind J2` retain as any `bind` and are released at the block's end in reverse order (a
  struct J2 copied into its own slot, rule 27); each `fld` of a struct-matrix element is lowered by
  rule 18 in full (both extents, both `chkb`, one load per field) (§3.5.7 step 4, §2.11.4, §2.11.5).
* **L-ed** (6e, agreed 2026-10-29) The W5 port leaves out, besides the figures section and the
  `--figures` arm of its option loop, Appendix D's header line documenting `--figures` and the
  `var figures` it would no longer use (§2.11.8).
* **L-ee** (6e, agreed 2026-10-29) The W1 port holds `caseMat` 0-based (MATLAB's `[2 2 3 1 4]` is
  `[1, 1, 2, 0, 3]`), with a header note; the bearing index keeps MATLAB's 1-based number internally
  (`brgIdx`, 0 for none), which is not exported, so §2.11.8's "1-based indices in its JSON" has
  nothing to apply to; MATLAB's `w1:*` error identifiers are dropped and their messages kept; the
  export record is named `out` (`ref` is a keyword) (§2.11.8).
* **L-ef** (6e, agreed 2026-10-29) The ports are cross cases of a new case kind `ports` (bundle
  `cases/ports/NAME.{s,out,args,meta}` and `NAME.expect/NAME.json`): `cross_pack.sh` checks each
  with `accept.sh --save-out`, packs its standard output without the `Compute time` line and
  generates `NAME.args` (`--export-reference`) and `NAME.meta` (`filter=compute-time`); a port that
  fails on the Mac is `NAME.packfail`. Amends §6.6.1 (the case list, the `.meta` keys, the bundle
  kinds, where the `accept` kind is now listed too) and §6.3.
* **L-eg** (6e, agreed 2026-10-29) A token-map regex writes a blank as `[[:space:]]`, never `[ ]`,
  because `compare_report.py` splits the map's fields on whitespace; where a JSON tolerance is below
  one printed unit, the map converts it to the report's units and adds no rounding slack (the
  `Rejects:` precedent). Amends §6.4 in place.

**Lead decisions of phase 7** (written 2026-10-29 with the text of §2.12, revised after two
reviews, and agreed by the user together with Decisions 94–113 on 2026-10-29); each is a reading where LANGUAGE.md or the earlier rules leave a choice, written into
§2.12:

* **L-eh** `seafuse`'s files are `passes/seafuse/fu0main.bas` … in name order, own lines 100 –
  59 999, `SUB` prefix `fu_`, build list `lib io diag tables layout`, `data errors exits consts
  records` (§2.12.3).
* **L-ei** Whether an elemental application is quiet is decided on its instance's callee body
  after §8.6's inlining of the calls in it would apply: a body is quiet when every node in it is
  quiet by §2.12.2's list (by element type: no `i64` arithmetic that can overflow, no `abs` of
  `i64`, no conversion to `i64`), it has no `error`, no index, no loop (a `while` may not terminate:
  never speculated, never moved) and calls only quiet functions; computed once per instance by
  `seafuse` (§2.12.2).
* **L-ej** (replaced by Decision 109 (a)) `sealoop` renumbers every `.l` local of `sea.hirl` in file
  order on output; the `fn` record's nl counts them all (§2.12.3).
* **L-ek** `seafuse` writes a function holding none of the constructs F1–F4 rewrite and no `emap`,
  and a file holding none, byte for byte as read; the stage pair then compares with `NAME.hir`
  (§2.12.3).
* **L-el** A fusion that would exceed a HIR capacity limit is not applied (Decision 72 for HIR);
  L19's own limits are reported as before (§2.12.3); amended 2026-10-29: the position of a
  capacity diagnostic may move with `seafuse` as a separate pass (§2.12.3 "Capacity").
* **L-em** A vector tree with one fusible node and no folded leaf, which is not the value of an
  `asg set` to a whole array or selection nor of a group statement, is not rewritten by `seafuse`:
  `sealoop`'s L7 gives it exactly F1's form (one `loop`, the same checks, `anew`, nest); every
  matrix tree and every such value is rewritten (Decision 111, §2.12.4).
* **L-en** F1 (2)'s "nothing that can fail follows N's loop": N is the root; the statement's store
  makes no check (a `bind`, `ret`, `tret`, an argument, or an `asg set` to a whole array, whose
  reuse prologue's test is quiet); a selection store, whose index, bounds and shape checks the
  reference makes after N's loop, does not qualify and gets RES (§2.12.4).
* **L-eo** A matrix space iterates linearly over R·C in its plain copy when no leaf is folded (the
  whole arrays are contiguous); with a folded selection leaf it keeps `mloop`, whose inner loop runs
  down a column, unit-stride for T13 (§2.12.4).
* **L-ep** The plain copy's test is the conjunction of `bin eq` of every array leaf's extents with
  the space's, written once after the leaf and check phase; the broadcast copy is L7's indexing for
  every leaf (§2.12.4).
* **L-eq** A group keeps each statement's own reference checks and adds none; its one quiet space
  test compares every statement's root extents (and each masked reduction's mask extents) with the
  first's; when it fails the split copy runs each statement's nest over its own space, storing every
  local in an array of its own (§2.12.4 F2 (2)).
* **L-er** A group grows greedily from its first groupable statement and ends before the first
  statement that is not groupable or would break F2 (3) or (4); that statement may start the next
  group (§2.12.4).
* **L-es** A group-bound local not read after the group keeps its `loc` record; its `bind` is
  dropped and nothing is stored or released for it in the fused nest (R34); the split copy stores it
  (§2.12.4).
* **L-et** A masked F3 counts selected elements in Q, and every use L13 makes of the position is Q:
  `sum`'s sum8 lane `Q & 7` and the index `argmax`/`argmin` return, so the lanes and the index are
  LANGUAGE.md §10.5's over the selection; such a loop holds an `if` with a carried value and is not
  vectorized (§2.12.4 F3).
* **L-eu** A concatenation part that is a range or `:` selection or a view is copied from its base
  in L9 (c)'s copy pass, its IX 1 and IX 2 at the part's place in the part order (§2.12.4 F4).
* **L-ev** T11's copies thread the registers the body writes: copy k reads the newest definition
  among copies 1 … k − 1 (copy 1 the original register), each written register gets a new name per
  copy, and a `mov` after the last copy restores the original name of every register read after the
  loop or carried around it (§2.12.6).
* **L-ew** T12 replaces a slot only when, on every path, each location's first access is a store (a
  forward walk with §5.8's F6 joins), every location is accessed with one class only and no two
  accesses partly overlap; otherwise none of the slot's locations is replaced (§2.12.6).
* **L-ex** T13's independence test pairs only accesses of one kind (`f64` with `f64`, byte with
  byte): an array has one element kind and the element sizes differ, so accesses of different kinds
  never overlap (§2.12.6 (4)).
* **L-ey** Vector accesses are unaligned (`ldr q`, `movupd`, `vmovupd`); no loop is peeled for
  alignment (§2.12.6).
* **L-ez** On arm64 an `x` or `m` value live across a call or `rcall` is spilled (AAPCS64 keeps only
  the low 64 bits of `v8`–`v15`); on x86_64 every vector value live across one is spilled (§2.12.7).
* **L-fa** The allocation counts per iteration of §2.12.10 (W1 0, W4 6) are derived by T2 from the
  agreed text of F1–F5 for the final ports and written in the header comment of each
  `tests/fusion/` program with the derivation; a change of the rules re-derives them (§2.12.10).
* **L-fb** T2 lists every golden that phase 7 changes with the rule that changes it, in its report
  and in `tests/CORPUS.md` (by the T1 of the same sub-phase) (§2.12.10, Decision 97).
* **L-fc** Target-specific LIR tests: a `seavec` dump test has `NAME.lir` (`arm64-macos`) and
  `NAME.lirx64` (`x86_64-linux`); a hand-written `seavec` stage test is a `NAME.lir3` without
  `NAME.sea`; a hand-written pass-4 test for `x86_64-linux` only is a `NAME.lirx64` with `NAME.out`;
  `stage.sh` and `run.sh` run each `NAME.lirx64` only through `x86_64-linux` and never take it for a
  `*.lir` test (§2.12.10, Decision 99).
* **L-fd** `seagen_x64` executes `vzeroupper` at every exit from a 4-lane loop's code and before a
  call of a non-`_y` entry inside it, never elsewhere (§2.12.7).
* **L-fe** Aliasing and dependences are decided on root paths (root variable and field chain); a
  read of the path through a call, or through a field reached from another path, is a conflict
  (F1 (5), F2 (3)).
* **L-ff** A group writes each target root path at most once (F2 (3)), so F2 (6)'s held old value O
  never meets a second `cow` (§2.12.4).
* **L-fg** T13 if-converts only blocks in an innermost step-1 loop whose parts hold vector-set
  instructions and no store, failing instruction, `call` or sited `rcall`, innermost first; a block
  it does not convert keeps the loop scalar (§2.12.6, Decision 108); amended by Decision 115:
  candidates may hold `do` blocks that P1 dissolves, P1–P3 run first, mask registers merge by
  `iand bnot iand ior`, and the whole preparation is kept only when the loop is vectorized.
* **L-fh** Spill slots of `y` and 4-lane `m` values are 32 bytes at 16-byte alignment, accessed by
  `vmovupd`; no frame is realigned (§2.12.7).
* **L-fi** Vector comparisons use ordered predicates for `lt le eq`, operand swaps for `gt ge` (SSE2
  has no ordered `gt`/`ge`), the unordered not-equal for `ne`; `xmin`/`xmax` follow §3.6.4's rule
  by the four-step sequence of §2.12.7; masks are loaded as 0/1 then negated and stored by a right
  shift of 63 and narrowing, so a stored `bool` is 0 or 1 (§2.12.7).
* **L-fj** `math_check`'s random differential test uses a fixed-seed xorshift generator, 2²⁴ inputs
  per function and lane pattern, mixing all bit patterns with each function's boundary ranges
  (§2.12.8).
* **L-fk** The heap check's count mode is the value `count` of `SEA_HEAP_CHECK` (§4.5): its line
  `heap: <a> allocations, <l> live objects` replaces the `1` mode's line; every other value still
  writes nothing (§2.12.10, Decision 105).
* **L-fl** A `vector` shape line is satisfied by an innermost loop identified as the scalar shape
  lines identify theirs (L-ar), from the line range by its own site or else the nearest site before
  its `loop` record (a vector body has none), inlined code keeping its callee's lines, and holding
  the line's listed lane ops (Decision 119); on `x86_64-linux` both the 4-lane and the 2-lane loop
  must be present (§2.12.10).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7b (found in its integration; the readings it fixed):

* **L-fm** `seafuse` numbers the `.l` locals it creates in `sea.hirf` canonically, in the file order
  of their declaring records, as `sealoop` does; T2's goldens fix it (§2.12.3).
* **L-fn** Decision 109's "file order" is the order of the declaring records of the `.l` locals
  (`tmp`, `bind`, `tbind`, `hloop`, `rcnt`), not the order of first reference; `tptr` types are
  likewise renumbered by `sealoop` in order of first reference, `seafuse` appending its own from
  `sea.hir`'s last type id (§2.12.3, §3.5.9 "Locals").
* **L-fo** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29) Decision 110's copying is built in 7b, not 7c, because
  7b's `seafuse` already writes L19's `HL` records into `inl` and `elem` bodies; and, amending
  Decision 110's text (§2.12.3, §9), a copied callee `.l` local becomes a new caller `.l` local (one
  per inlined call, renumbered in declaring-record order with the caller's own; `loc` position P
  under L18, the callee local's own position under L20), not a `.i` local, which keeps `sea.hirl`
  neutral.
* **L-fp** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29) An exception to Decision 109's byte identity: a
  `return` of an elemental application (a `tret` of an `emap`) inside an `inl` or `elem` function:
  `sea.hirl` and the sites of `sea.lir1` differ (`seafuse` writes L19's `tret` form, a block ending
  in `ret P k`, at the `emap`'s position, which L20 copies as `iret`), while `sea.lir`, the program
  output and the run-time diagnostics are identical (run-time errors report the line only).
* **L-fq** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29) Capacity diagnostics ("program too large: …") keep
  their message, but their position may move, `seafuse` counting nodes as a separate pass without
  L20's inline cost; L-el, §2.12.3 "Capacity" and Decision 109's "every diagnostic" exclude capacity
  positions.
* **L-fr** `seafuse` writes a `tasg` target of L19 as `asg P set target (lv Rj)`, and `sealoop`'s
  L6 and L17 store it; an `lv` of a `sea.hirf` `.l` home takes R25's V5 = 0 path in L17 (neutral).
* **L-fs** `ind2sub` with an array `r` in `sea.hirf` is `BAD_RECORD` in `sealoop` (`seafuse`
  rewrites it), as `inst` and `emap` are.
* **L-ft** `seaval` checks `lir3` as `lir2` (set `L`, no `LF`, no `x`/`y`/`m`, the `lir1`-only label
  rules off) and `hirf` as `hirl` without `inst emap cdat iblk iret`; `seafuse` checks that a
  `tbind`'s `n` and a `tasg`'s target count equal `k` (`BAD_RECORD`).
* **L-fu** `tests/protocol.sh` was edited by WP-PIPE: its fake chain needs the two new programs
  (§8, row 7b).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7c (found in its integration and its two reviews; the readings it fixed,
recorded 2026-10-30; L-fv–L-fy record decisions of the user):

* **L-fv** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29: D1) A group's leaf and check phases, its stored locals'
  `bind X = anew` and its reductions' accumulators stand directly in the enclosing block, ahead of
  the group's `block P n` (a `block` is a scope; a local bound in it would be released at its end
  while a later statement reads it); the finals are bound after that block (§2.12.4 F2).
* **L-fw** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29: D2; numbering a lead decision) F3's sum8 type F8 is
  appended to `sea.hirf`'s type table (§2.12.3 (3)), numbered with the `tptr` records in order of
  first reference, so a masked sum's mask `tptr` precedes it; `sealoop`'s reader accepts F8 among
  the appended records, does not take it for a duplicate `tptr` of `f64` or treat it as a `tptr`,
  and its writer renumbers it with them (fixed in 7c; §2.12.3, §3.5.9 "Types").
* **L-fx** (agreed by the user, 2026-10-29: D3) The broadcast copy reads a folded leaf through its
  own map at row I·[rows ≠ 1] and column J·[cols ≠ 1] (its SI and t, no SJ); a folded `.col` or
  `.row` reads at `lin(I·s, J·t, r)` with the strides of a whole array (§2.12.4 F1 (4)).
* **L-fy** (decided by the user, 2026-10-30) Concatenation parts fold in every row of a stack and in
  rows mixing scalars, vectors and matrices, with the foldability rule and the vector-result
  folding of `v[:]` and `A.flat` of §2.12.4 F4; this supersedes WP-FUSE3's reading that only one
  row of matrix parts folds.
* **L-fz** Positions and the order of the leaf and check phase are §2.12.4 "Readings fixed by 7c"
  (1) and (2) (T2a's R-a, R-b, R-c, R-T2b-4; all of a node's operand extents loaded before its
  checks, WP-FUSE3's reading 4); F8 reuses `sea.hir`'s `tfvec` of `f64` with n 8 when it has one.
* **L-ga** F1 (4)'s test Pl, NN and strides are placed as §2.12.4 F1 (4) says (R-d); with a single
  dynamic array leaf in a matrix space the always-true Pl and the broadcast copy are kept as written
  (R-T2b-5); a fixed-size in-place value's extents are its first array leaf's, a fixed vector's its
  static n (R-n), and a fixed-size root's static extents are `ci` `tmp`s at P (§2.12.4 "Readings
  fixed by 7c" (3)).
* **L-gb** A bare leaf is no element-wise tree, and `ind2sub` with a scalar `r` no fusible node
  (R-T2b-1, R-T2b-3), so the L13 dumps and `ew_ind2sub` are unchanged (§2.12.4 "Readings fixed by
  7c" (3)).
* **L-gc** Stores in place: a selection store only when its value reads no `lv` of the target's
  root (F1 (5) (ii) read strictly), never of kind V, and alone, never a group member; a whole-array
  target that its value reads other than as whole-array leaves at the element starts no group and
  is fused into RES (review 1, finding 1); the forms of R-f, R-g and of the dynamic matrix's
  broadcast copy, and `$` in a target index, are §2.12.4 "Readings fixed by 7c" (4) (F1 (3), (5),
  F2 (1)).
* **L-gd** Groups have one rank (R-T2b-2; a `.flat` reduction's space is a vector of R·C, finding
  6); a masked reduction does not start a group; the space test, data order, matrix groups and
  the split copy (with a masked reduction's split nest over its mask's base positions with counter
  J, finding 2) are §2.12.4 "Readings fixed by 7c" (5) (R-e, R-o).
* **L-ge** A `tbind` of a k ≥ 2 elemental application in a group is §2.12.4 "Readings fixed by 7c"
  (6) (R-m; WP-FUSE3's readings 1–3 and 6): direct `tbind` value only, leaf arguments, kept
  components only, at most 499 components per group; a `tbind` component's element store follows
  its `tbind` in that `tbind`'s block (review 1, finding 7: `sealower` accepts an `est` of a `tbind`'s
  `.l` local only in the block it begins).
* **L-gf** Reductions are §2.12.4 "Readings fixed by 7c" (7): masked forms (R-h; masked `sum` by
  R-l, the selected count as lane, not sum8's direct `hloop`), `.flat` with a single leaf (R-k),
  in groups (R-q, matching rank, the final at its statement's position after the block), same-mask
  data loaded once (R-r), `variance`/`std` of `i64` with F8 (review 1, finding 5); `variance` and
  `std` fused only over quiet trees, a failing root a barrier (review 2, finding 1; §2.12.4 F3).
* **L-gg** F5 with k = 1 writes its per-element `call` in the element expression (R-i; §2.12.4
  "Readings fixed by 7c" (8)).
* **L-gh** The slot cap (1 180 of a unit's 1 187 slots) is an implementation capacity: a unit over
  it is left unfused, like L-el; a node, symbol or type limit passed inside a fusion runs that
  fusion to its end on throwaway output and re-runs the walk once with every walk flag reset and a
  threshold that leaves that fusion and every later one unfused (coarser than "only the fusions
  that would exceed", allowed by §2.12.3); a second overflow, or one outside a fusion, is reported
  as before (§2.12.3 "Capacity"; review 1, findings 8 and 9; review 2, findings 2–5).
* **L-gi** Tests: `elem6_inst` is a subject test of L19, rewritten with `printf` separators so that
  no group forms (R-T2b-6; its `.out` gains `4 6 0 3`); §6.2's description of `fuse7_inl` follows
  L-fo (a callee `.l` local becomes a caller `.l` local, not a `.i` local); the expected outputs of
  `fuse_cat_*` and `r_fuse_cat_*` come from Python mirrors of LANGUAGE.md §6.9, those of the
  regression tests from LANGUAGE.md (§10.4, §10.5) and §2.12.3, each also identical to the pre-7c
  compiler's output (the reference of §2.12.2), capacity positions excepted (L-fq).
* **L-gj** `sealoop`'s reader requires an `rcnt`'s `l` of type 3 and `e` of type 2, as §3.5.9
  "Locals" says (`passes/sealoop/lp0main.bas` compared `5 − J`, now `6 − J`): a 7b defect never
  exercised, because 7b's `seafuse` wrote no `rcnt`; and an inlined callee's `.i` local that no
  record declares (a group local whose `bind` F2 dropped, R34) is numbered after the declared ones.

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7e (WP-LIB's readings, found in its build and recorded 2026-10-31; each
is written into its normative section; Decision 115 records the user's amendment of T13, Decision 116
the validation of `sea.lir` that L-gk describes):

* **L-gk** (decided by the user, 2026-10-31: Decision 116) `lirrw`'s `sea.lir` input kind, the full
  validator of the vector classes, is used by the tool `tools/lirchk.bas`, which `tests/run.sh` and
  `tests/stage.sh` run on every `sea.lir` they produce; `seavec` reads `sea.lir3` with the LIR input
  kind, as `sealopt` does, and does not read its output back, `lirrw`'s writer not validating the
  vector records `seavec` puts into its tables (§2.12.6).
* **L-gl** L-ez's "spilled" is §4.9.2's "Calls" save around each call the vector interval crosses
  (a save slot, listed by `ra_sv`), not a spill of the whole interval; on both targets and on the
  free path of a `release` (§2.12.7, §4.9.2).
* **L-gm** A vector interval that crosses a call takes the `f` row "crossing no call", not "crossing
  a call", so arm64 does not prefer `d8`–`d15`, which would only add prologue saves; it is saved
  around each call even in a callee-saved register, and a callee-saved register given to a vector
  value is still reported by `ra_used` (§2.12.7, §4.9.2).
* **L-gn** A mask register's lane count is fixed by its first write in record order; a read of a
  mask with no lane count yet is `BAD_RECORD` (§3.6.4 property 2); `mand mor mnot` and a `mov` of
  masks take the lane count of their (first) source; `ralloc`'s class is 6 for a 2-lane and 7 for a
  4-lane mask (§2.12.6, §2.12.7).
* **L-go** `lirrw` checks only `vfeat` against the target (§3.6.4: `x86_64-linux` only) and accepts
  `y`, `ldm4` and `stm4` in an `arm64-macos` file; `seagen_a64` rejects them as `BAD_RECORD`
  (§2.12.7; §2.12.6).
* **L-gp** A `lirrw` rejection (`BAD_RECORD`) prints no detail, so each `lirrw` rejection case of
  `tests/lib_check.sh` is a one-record mutation of an accepted file, which isolates its cause
  (§2.12.6).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7e (T2's and WP-VEC's readings, found in their builds and recorded
2026-10-31 with Decision 117; each decides byte-level output or legality and is written into
§2.12.6 or §2.12.10):

* **L-gq** T11's copy k, counted from 1, has J = S + (k − 1)·T (the agreed text's S + k·T counted
  from 0); only this keeps the loop's values (T2).
* **L-gr** T12's own use list (loads and stores with `idx` `-` or a constant register, and slot
  copies) replaces the Terms' private base, whose uses are only without an `idx`; otherwise T11's
  output, whose accesses have constant `idx` registers, could never feed T12 (T2).
* **L-gs** T11 does not apply when its loop's `ind` is read after the loop: the copies never write
  it, and L-ay would give it S + C·T (WP-VEC).
* **L-gt** T11 and T12 take their candidates (loops; slots) from the function as it stands before
  the transformation, in record order, as T13 does; T11's copies are not visited again (WP-VEC).
* **L-gu** A register is read after a loop L when a record after L's last record reads it, or a
  record before L inside a loop that encloses L does (reached around that loop's back edge); T11's
  `mov`s, T12 and T13's condition 3 use this reading (WP-VEC).
* **L-gv** P2 leaves an access unchanged when its index chain names one invariant register as two
  terms or has more than 6 invariant terms (a capacity of `seavec`'s term list; WP-VEC).
* **L-gw** The read and write counts T11–T13 use ("only definition", "nothing reads", "only write
  in L") are counted over the whole function (WP-VEC).
* **L-gx** A hand-written `.lir3` test states its subject in `tests/CORPUS.md`, since LIR has no
  comment record (T2; §2.12.10).
* **L-gy** `lirrw`'s string interning (`GOSUB 75000`: the string in `Z$`, its `S$` row in `Q2`, a
  new row when absent) is part of `lirrw`'s interface for the programs that load it; `seavec`
  uses it for the vector entries' names and the word `avx2`, and `passes/lib/API.md` documents it
  (its owner's change) (§2.12.6).
* **L-gz** (the lead, 2026-10-31, after T2's round 2, in line with Decision 117) In T12's
  first-access walk an `if`/`ifz` whose condition register has a single definition that folds (an
  `icmp` of two constants, as rule 17's `icmp gt E N Z`, or an `rcount` flag of constant `lo`, `hi`,
  `st` with `st` ≠ 0, as rule 4's) is decided: the part that runs is on every path, the other part
  (a constant-false guard's first part, a constant-true guard's `else` part) on none and dead for
  the walk; each decided block holding an access to, or a slot copy of, a replaced slot is resolved
  (its block records and dead part deleted) so that §3.6.4's property 2 holds for the new registers
  (§2.12.6 T12).
* **L-ha** (the lead, 2026-10-31, after T2's round 2) A location that no slot of its slot-copy chain
  accesses by `ldi ldf sti stf` has no class: it takes no part in the walk, gets no register and no
  `mov`, and its slots are still replaced (§2.12.6 T12).
* **L-hb** (the lead, 2026-10-31, after WP-VEC and T2 read T12's walk differently on `sr7_w3`) In
  T12's first-access walk the state after a `do`'s `enddo` is the join of the states at the `exit`s
  naming that `do`, not F6's "entry state after a loop's closing record": a path that reaches
  `enddo` loops back, so only the `exit`s leave, and a `do` with no `exit` leaves nothing reachable
  after it. An implementation may bound the nesting it tracks and fall back to the `do`'s entry
  state beyond it, which is conservative (a walk state only gains written locations) (§2.12.6 T12).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7e (the readings of pass 4, the harness, the cross run and `seavec`'s
review fixes, found in the packages' builds and recorded 2026-10-31 at the integration; each is
written into §2.12.6, §2.12.7 or §6.6.1 or is a reading of a test, and decides byte-level output or
legality, never a language feature; Decisions 115–117 were decided by the user):

* **L-hc** (WP-GEN-A64) On arm64 `v31` is the vector scratch register: `stm2`'s temporary,
  `xmin`/`xmax`'s temporary, the scratch of a memory-to-memory vector move and the cycle scratch of
  a parallel move (§4.9.2); `v30` serves `xmin`/`xmax` only when the destination is the operand
  `b`, and spilled operands are loaded into `v29`, `v30`, `v31` by their position. `xlane`'s `k` is
  0 or 1 (every vector has 2 lanes): another value is `BAD_RECORD`. A `y` register, a `y` instruction,
  `ldm4`, `stm4` and `vfeat` are `BAD_RECORD` in `seagen_a64`, `y` by class at the decoding and the
  others for lack of a template (L-go; §2.12.7).
* **L-hd** (WP-GEN-X64) The SSE2 forms of `xcmp`, `xsel` and `xmin`/`xmax` use a spilled operand
  directly as a 16-byte memory operand, so the vector spill slots are 16-byte aligned (L-fh): the
  spill area starts at a 16-aligned offset whenever `ra_sa` reports a vector slot and `%rsp` is
  16-byte aligned at the body; an offset of 2^31 or more is formed in `%r11` just before the
  instruction. Moves and saves stay unaligned (`movupd`, `vmovupd`) (§2.12.7, §4.9.2).
* **L-he** (WP-GEN-X64) `vzeroupper` (L-fd) is emitted only where no `y` or 4-lane `m` value is
  live: a `_y` entry returns with its upper halves live, and a `vzeroupper` there would destroy a
  live `ymm` value. "Every exit from a 4-lane loop's code" is therefore placed conservatively, with
  the extents of the `y`/`m4` values widened to their outermost enclosing loop; it is also executed
  after the saves of a `call`, `rcall` and `release`, and not before a `_y` entry. The rule decides
  performance only, never a result (§2.12.7).
* **L-hf** (WP-GEN-A64, WP-GEN-X64) `xfloor xceil xtrunc xround` and their `y` forms are
  `BAD_RECORD` in both code generators (Decision 100: no pass writes them, so pass 4 has no
  template); a vector or mask `func` parameter, `call` argument or result and `chk` argument is
  `BAD_RECORD` in both, as `lirrw` rejects it (§2.12.7, §3.6.4); an `rcall` of the entries 39–50
  does take vector arguments and results (in the first vector registers).
* **L-hg** (WP-GEN-A64, WP-GEN-X64) The `gen7_*` expected outputs print a NaN lane as the canonical
  quiet NaN (a NaN lane's bits are not observable, LANGUAGE.md §6.1), so one `NAME.out` serves both
  targets: the six arm64 `gen7_*.lir` are the x86_64 2-lane coverage through `cross_pack.sh`'s
  retargeting, and the 4-lane forms are `gen7_y*.lirx64` and `gen7_vfeat.lirx64`, which execute AVX2
  instructions unconditionally (only `gen7_vfeat` dispatches on `vfeat`), so they need an AVX2 host
  under both variants (L-hl; §6.2).
* **L-hh** (WP-HARNESS; Decision 116, L-gk) `tools/lirchk` reads one `sea.lir` through `lirrw` at
  `V8 = 3` and writes nothing, but `lirrw` copies the header and `DATA` records to its file 2 as it
  reads, so `lirchk` binds file 2 to `/dev/null`. It is silent with status 0 for a valid file, else
  `lirrw`'s own failure (`BAD_RECORD`, status 11, a capacity limit status 10). A missing `lirchk`
  binary is a setup error (status 2) of `run.sh`, `stage.sh` and `cross_pack.sh`, never a skip
  (§2.12.6).
* **L-hi** (WP-HARNESS) `tests/run.sh` validates the `sea.lir` of the one compilation it does for
  each test, with `--keep-temps` (its line `sea: temporary files kept in DIR` is removed from the
  standard error it compares); an earlier dump kind leaves no `sea.lir`, so nothing is checked
  there. `tests/stage.sh` validates every `seavec` output and every hand-written pass-4 input, and
  handles the x86_64 files of L-fc: a `NAME.lirx64` with a `NAME.lir3` is `seavec` on the `.lir3`
  retargeted to `x86_64-linux`, compared with the golden; a hand-written `.lir3` with a `.out` is
  also generated through `seagen_x64` (which must write a non-empty `sea.s`; its run is the cross
  run's); a `NAME.lirx64` without `.lir3` and `.sea` is an x86_64-only pass-4 test, generated by
  `stage.sh` and run by the cross run only; one with a `.sea` and no `.lir3` is a setup failure
  (§6.2, §6.6.1).
* **L-hj** (the lead, 2026-10-31; WP-CROSS) `cross_pack.sh` validates the x86_64 `sea.lir` of every
  case with `lirchk` (the driver's, `seavec`'s output, a hand-written pass-4 input): a rejection is
  a pack failure of the case (`NAME.packfail`). It skips a `passes/NAME.lir` beside a `NAME.lir3`
  (a `seavec` golden, as in `stage.sh`), packs a `passes/NAME.lirx64` that has a `NAME.out` and no
  `NAME.sea` (L-fc), and for one with a `NAME.lir3` runs the live `seavec` output through
  `seagen_x64`, not the committed golden (§6.6.1).
* **L-hk** (the lead, 2026-10-31; found by WP-GEN-X64, fixed in `tests/shape.sh`) The two targets'
  `sea.lir` are numbered differently once T13 is on (the x86_64 file has the `vfeat` and its two
  parts), so `shape.sh` takes the candidate loops of the x86_64 lines from a second compilation,
  `--target x86_64-linux --emit lir`, not from the arm64 file; the shape bounds are unchanged
  (§5.2, §6.2).
* **L-hl** (WP-CROSS) `cross_run.sh`'s AVX2 check (`grep -qw avx2 /proc/cpuinfo`, else exit 2) applies
  also when `SEA_KERNELS` is given, because the 4-lane tests run AVX2 instructions whatever the
  variant (L-hg); a given `SEA_KERNELS` replaces the pair by that one variant, unlabelled. The
  program, error, passes, accept and ports cases are built once and run per variant; build
  failures, `rt/` cases and `math/math_check` run once; the summary has one `variant <v>: passed: P
  failed: F` line per variant, an `once (build, rt, math)` line and the totals (§6.6.1).
* **L-hm** (the lead, 2026-10-31; review fix of WP-VEC) `seavec`'s scratch regions of the array `S`
  are disjoint while in use, each with a bound, and a transformation that would pass one is not
  applied (Decision 72): the counters (at most 9 999), the merges of if-conversion (at most 9 999,
  past which if-conversion refuses), the sum8 groups (at most 4 999), the other lists and T12's
  class, register and walk-frame rows as the header comment of `passes/seavec/ve0main.bas` lists
  (the table is there, not here, and is normative with this decision).
* **L-hn** (the lead, 2026-10-31; review fix of WP-VEC) A register is *local* to a loop L (§2.12.6
  "Registers", L-bl) when L writes it, nothing outside L references it and it is not a parameter:
  "written in L and read only in L" as the text says, and never a parameter, whatever the loop does
  with it. A parameter is therefore the same register in every copy of L (the review's
  miscompile: `fillsel3`, `param2`; tests `vec_reg_param_tail`, `sr7_reg_bigslots`).
* **L-ho** (the lead, 2026-10-31; review fix of WP-VEC) In T12's first-access walk, a path after an
  `if` whose two parts both end dead is dead (it holds no state), not the entry state restored as
  live (§2.12.6 T12; with L-gz and L-hb).
* **L-hp** (T1) The `vec_*` programs bind a slice (`let dn = d[0..n]`) before calling an elemental
  function on it, because a range argument folds into a moving pointer and is no unit access at
  `J`; `vec_ifexpr_pow` clamps with `min(d, 1e300)` and has no boundary lane at 2.79 or 51, since
  `tests/math/pow.vec` has no base 254 (the `&&` boundaries are in `vec_ifexpr_w1`); the `exp`
  rare-path argument is 600.2654583649127, a row of `exp.vec`. Their `.out` come from the committed
  bit patterns of `tests/math/*.vec` and Python mirrors of LANGUAGE.md §10.4–§10.5 (§6.2).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7f (the readings of the work packages, found in their builds and
recorded 2026-11-01 at the close-out; each is written into the section it names or is a reading of
a port or a test, and decides byte-level output or a check, never a language feature; Decisions
118–119 were decided by the user):

* **L-hq** (WP-HEAP; L-fk) The count mode's A is not counted at creation: `_sea_free` (`sea_free`)
  increments a 64-bit `_sea_freed` (`sea_freed`) in `rt_mem.s` beside its decrement of the live
  counter, and A = live + freed. This is exact because every constructor counts its object in the
  live counter, nothing but `_sea_free` uncounts one, and `_sea_free` takes only objects (a block
  that is not an object is released by the block path, which counts nothing); 9 `rt_heap_count_*`
  cases per target (§4.5, §4.7.1).
* **L-hr** (WP-PORT) W4's red/black colouring `mod(I + J, 2)` uses MATLAB's 1-based I and J:
  `let (I, J) = meshgrid((1..=nx), (1..=ny))`, the ranges parenthesised because a range used as a
  value needs parentheses (LANGUAGE.md Appendix A) (§2.12.10).
* **L-hs** (WP-PORT) MATLAB's centre lines `(nx + 1) / 2` (1-based) are `idiv(nx + 1, 2) - 1`, and
  likewise for `ny` (§2.12.10).
* **L-ht** (WP-TOKENS) The "last change" token of both SOR report lines (token 8) has no JSON key;
  it maps to `num 1e-8 0`, the solver's tolerance, which both runs end at or below (§6.4).
* **L-hu** (WP-TOKENS) The report's `omega` and `h` tokens have no `RULES` entry and are left
  unmapped: the default rule (one unit of the last printed digit) applies, `compare.py`'s 1e-9
  relative default being finer than one printed unit (§6.4).
* **L-hv** (WP-PORT) MATLAB's result record `ref` is named `out` in the port, `ref` being a Sea
  keyword; its JSON keys are those of the MATLAB reference (§2.12.10).
* **L-hw** (WP-LOOPFIX) `sealoop` (`lp2out.bas`) and `seafuse` (`fu2out.bas`) read the markers `^e`
  (a `tptr` reference) and `@p` (a new local) only in a `ty` or `lid` field, located by a table of
  field codes per opcode taken from the record formats of `include/passes.txt` (the sets `H HF HL`);
  a `^` or `@` byte in any other field, such as an escaped `s` payload, is text. The defect, present
  since 7c, crashed `sealoop` (`ILLEGAL 'VAL' ARGUMENT`) on `printf("W/m^2")` in a program with
  arrays, rewrote string constants such as `"^2"` (printed `0`) and could misnumber `tptr` types;
  tests `str_caret_bytes`, `str_caret_tptr` (§3.5.9 "Types", §3.1).
* **L-hx** (WP-FUSIONT) A `tests/fusion/` program reads K by comparing `args()`'s argument with
  `str(n)` for every n in 0..1000 (there is no string-to-integer conversion in v1, LANGUAGE.md
  §10.13), always to the end of the scan, so the scan makes the same 1 000 allocations for every K
  and cancels in the difference (§2.12.10).
* **L-hy** (WP-FUSIONT) K and the derived count are read from the program's header lines `// fusion
  K: N` and `// Allocations per iteration: N.` by `tests/fusion.sh`, and by `cross_pack.sh`, which
  writes them into the case's sidecar `NAME.fusion` (`k=`, `per_iteration=`) for `cross_run.sh`
  (§6.6.1). Measured at 7f's close, identical on arm64 and on `x86_64-linux` under both variants:
  `w1_bisect` 1 018 allocations at K = 2 and 1 018 at K = 3 (0 per iteration), `w4_rb` 1 042 and
  1 048 (6).
* **L-hz** (WP-SHAPE; Decision 119) The `-S` part of a `vector` line requires a lane-form
  instruction for every lane op the qualifying loop's LIR body holds, not only for the listed ones;
  a `-S` measurement that finds no instruction in the loop's range is a failure, never a pass
  (§2.12.10).
* **L-ia** (WP-SHAPE) A loop range of `shape.sh` that holds another loop's top label is not
  innermost code and measures as `none`. The guard was dead (it looked for the label after label
  lines had been skipped); `vmeasure` now tests for it before the skip. The scalar
  `measure()` keeps the same dead guard, left as it is: a known defect of the harness (§6.2).
* **L-ib** (Decision 118; T2) In T9 a `loop` that contains a `do` is not innermost (a `do` is a loop
  in §5.8's Terms), so it is not unswitched either. `vec7_p1_guard` was rewritten as a one-level
  guarded return that P1 rule 2 dissolves, every golden derived by hand (`tests/CORPUS.md`, §6.2).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 7g (the readings of the port and its token map, found in its build and
recorded 2026-11-01 at the close-out; each is a reading of a port or a token map and decides
byte-level output or a check, never a language feature; Decision 120 was decided by the user):

* **L-ic** (WP-PORT) `interp1` finds its interval by a linear scan: the largest k <= n - 2 with
  x[k] <= xq. It returns `(1-s)*y[k] + s*y[k+1]`, and NaN outside [x0, x_{n-1}] or for a NaN query.
  The NaN path is reachable: `steady_ratio` asks for the torque below 1500 rpm. At a knot both
  intervals give the table value exactly (§6.3).
* **L-id** (WP-PORT) The rank-3 arrays (`tDist`, `vTrap`, `nSteps`) become a struct array `Sweep {
  t, v, steps }` of nCrr elements, written with §5.5's field-of-element stores; the exports are
  `sweep[0].t` and so on.
* **L-ie** (WP-PORT) Growing arrays: all 16 `fe*` arrays are preallocated to `nCandMax` = 326,700,
  with the count `nFeas`, and cut to `[0..nFeas]`. `diff(...) <= 0` becomes loops. `1.5:0.25:3.5`
  and `2.0:0.25:4.5` become `linspace(1.5, 3.5, 9)` and `linspace(2.0, 4.5, 11)`, which give exactly
  the same values.
* **L-if** (WP-PORT) The fields the script adds later, `eng.tqGov` (computed after the validation)
  and `gd.sLimit`, are given in the struct literals.
* **L-ig** (WP-PORT) A single-output call of `engine_torque` is written `let (Te, _) = ...` just
  before its use; the operation order is unchanged.
* **L-ih** (WP-PORT) 0-based indices (`iBest`, `cfgPick`, `ord`, `b`, the backlash bands via
  `find_last`) are exported and printed `+ 1`. Tooth counts, nMin and the modules stay `f64` and
  print with `%d` as integral `f64`. The tables are annotated `f64[]`.
* **L-ii** (WP-TOKENS) Token-map readings: tokens with no JSON key but derived exactly (the run
  count, rank, stage number, the best ratio, backlash `min..max`) use `exact`; the err[%] token is
  `num 3.0864e-13 0`, `top_err`'s 1e-12 relative bound against max |top_err| 3.0864e-3, converted to
  percent, as L-eg says; keys whose tolerance is below one printed unit use `json <key>` as they
  stand, as W4's `T_max` does (§6.4). No gap beyond §6.3's list was met.

**Lead decisions of phase 8** (written 2026-11-01 with the text of §2.13, revised after one
independent review, and agreed by the user together with Decisions 121–129 on 2026-11-01); each is a
reading where LANGUAGE.md or the earlier rules leave a choice, written into §2.13:

* **L-ij** The shapes in `shape mismatch` are the operands' in source order (`@`: left, right;
  `solve`: n × n of A or F, then B; `eig_sym(K, M)`: K, M), written as §4.8's `h` slots; `matrix is
  not square` names the operand's shape; a static mismatch of `@` (both operands fixed-size) is 217
  at the operator.
* **L-ik** Each entry checks in its row's order; `solve`'s errors depend on A or F only, never on
  B's column count: `SINGULAR` is reported for an n × 0 B too, and the empty result comes after the
  checks.
* **L-il** `solve(F, B)` reports `matrix is singular` as `solve(A, B)` does (LANGUAGE.md §9.2's row
  read for both forms; §10.8's table states it only for the second).
* **L-im** `chol` reads the upper triangle only and tests no symmetry (MATLAB's `chol`); its pivot
  test is "not greater than 0", so a NaN pivot is `matrix is not positive definite`: the one place
  where a NaN stops instead of propagating, because the test is the operation's definition.
* **L-in** Partial pivoting takes the first row of strictly largest magnitude (LAPACK's `idamax`): a
  NaN never replaces a pivot candidate (Decision 129 (a)); an exactly zero pivot leaves its column
  unscaled and the factorization continues (LAPACK `dgetf2`), so `lu` never fails for a singular
  matrix; true division, not LAPACK's reciprocal scaling.
* **L-io** `rcond`, in this order (Decision 129 (a)): order 0 → +∞ (MATLAB's `rcond([])`); ‖A‖₁ NaN
  → NaN; a recorded zero pivot → 0; ‖A‖₁ 0 or +∞ → 0; then, by Decision 130 (a), a solve of the
  estimator whose Σ|x| is +∞ or NaN → 0 at once, and an estimate that is +∞, NaN or 0 → 0; unscaled
  triangular solves (no `dlatrs`).
* **L-ip** `eig_sym`: a matrix with a ±∞ or NaN element (after the symmetry test) gives n NaN; an
  eigenvalue not converged within `SEA_EIG_MAXIT` iterations, and every later one, is NaN; the
  result is sorted by §10.6's `f64` order; order 0 → the empty vector.
* **L-iq** Arguments and results: `i64` arguments converted, fixed-size arguments made dynamic
  (`dyn`) as Decision 39 did for `sort`; every result of the five functions dynamic; `@` of two
  fixed-size operands fixed-size up to 256 result elements and dynamic above (Decision 125 (a)),
  with a dynamic operand dynamic. W3's `eig_sym(Klin, Mlin)` of two `f64[2,2]` literals is therefore
  accepted.
* **L-ir** An array type whose element type is or contains a handle type (a struct field at any
  depth) is 258 `arrays cannot hold %s` naming the handle type, at the type node, or at the array
  literal or the `filled` call that would create it (LANGUAGE.md §4.1: such an array would store the
  handle).
* **L-is** A handle is one runtime block (§2.13.6's private layout); `sea_lu` and `sea_chol` count
  it in `_sea_live` like every object constructor (`rt_mem.s`'s header), so it is in the live count
  and in `SEA_HEAP_CHECK=count`'s total (§4.1, §4.5); `sea_free` frees and uncounts it; it refers to
  no other object.
* **L-it** Everything in the factorizations, solves, `rcond` and `eig_sym` that is not a Baysick
  kernel call performs the same IEEE operations in the same order on both targets and every variant
  (panels may be vectorized across rows or columns, never reordered per element); class-R results
  then differ only through `_bsk_kern_gemm`/`gemm_sub`. A property of the build, not of LANGUAGE.md;
  tests use exact data.
* **L-iu** Sea's kernels choose their variant by reading `_sea_variant` (§4.4's "variant table of
  the same shape as Baysick's" is read as that dispatch: three forms, two of them x86_64's);
  `_sea_variant` moves from `rt_main.s` to `rt_kern.s`, so a C test links the entries without the
  runtime's `main`.
* **L-iv** Every check of the five functions and of a dynamic `@` is made by the runtime entry, with
  the call's site; the compiled code makes none (L21's fixed-size products have none to make).
* **L-iw** L21 binds the operands' homes before its loops, starts each chain with the first product,
  and writes +0 for k = 0; vector @ matrix reuses L13's sum8 form; T11/T12 do the rest.
* **L-ix** `bin matmul` and the five `lib`s are `seafuse` barriers: leaves of the trees above them,
  their operand positions F1 positions, their statements group ends.
* **L-iy** `eig_sym(K, M)` tests, after its errors' shape and symmetry checks, K and M for a ±∞ or
  NaN element (n NaN, before the Cholesky of M, so an infinite diagonal never passes it), then
  factors M (`NOT_POSDEF`), then tests the reduced C (n NaN, before `tred1`, so `tql1` never sees an
  infinite value). No real choice: it is L-ip's rule applied to every matrix the eigenvalue step
  receives, and an error would make a NaN stop here while it propagates in `eig_sym(A)`.
* **L-iz** `VECMAT`'s tail lanes are filled with −0.0 (exact), never with a product of memory
  outside the operands; GEMV's and VECMAT's blocking is free (class E fixes each element's sequence,
  not the loops).
* **L-ja** The link-map test of §4.3 is `tests/la/la_link.sh` (§2.13.8): the link map (`ld -map`) or
  trace (`-Wl,--trace`) of a program calling `MATMUL` names only `rt_kinit.o` and `rt_k*.o` among
  `libbaysickrt.a`'s members (§4.3's sentence describes a test that does not exist today; `nm`
  cannot see members).
* **L-jb** `SOLVE`'s failed Cholesky attempt falls back to LU on a fresh copy of A, never to LDLᵀ
  (LANGUAGE.md's choice; MATLAB would use LDLᵀ for a symmetric indefinite A, with the same solution
  up to rounding).
* **L-jc** The private routines `sea_la_potrf(a, n, ld, w)` (0, or 1 + the failing pivot's index)
  and `sea_la_issym(a, n, ld)` (1 or 0) live in `rt_lu.s` (WP-LU's), are called by `rt_eig.s`, carry
  no `rt.inc` record (they are not entries and the passes never name them) and follow the platform
  ABI; WP-EIG codes against §2.13.6's interface in parallel and is merged after WP-LU.
* **L-jd** `tests/la/gen_consts.sh` (WP-LACHECK) writes `sea_consts.h` into the build directory from
  the contract files, as Baysick's `tests/kern/kern_run.sh` derives `runtime_consts.h`: every
  `.equiv SEA_*` of `rt.inc` and `limits.inc` as `#define`, and every record of `errors.inc`'s
  `SEA_ERROR_LIST` as `#define SEA_E_<NAME> <code>`; `la_check.c` uses only those names for
  `SEA_LA_NB`, `SEA_VAR_*`, the error codes and the site layout (`SEA_SITE_FILE`, `SEA_SITE_LINE`,
  `SEA_SITE_SIZE`). A `make` rule and `Makefile.linux` run it; `cross_pack.sh` packs its output.
* **L-je** RCOND follows `dgecon` exactly in what it estimates: ‖U⁻¹L⁻¹‖₁ with no interchanges, and
  `dlacn2`'s sign rule (v ≥ 0 → +1, else −1; −0 → +1, NaN → −1, as Reference-LAPACK's
  `SRC/dlacn2.f` writes it, confirmed in 8c); the identity's `rcond` is not 1 at every order
  (§2.13.6), so expected values come from `tests/vectors/la8_cases.py`.
* **L-jf** `CHOL` (and `sea_la_potrf`) sets R's strict lower triangle to +0 before the first panel,
  as the trailing updates read and write it inside diagonal blocks, and again after the last one, so
  a `Chol` holds exactly R.

Lead decisions of sub-phase 8b (the readings of its work packages, found in their builds and
recorded 2026-11-01 at its integration; each states the code as built and changes no agreed rule):

* **L-jg** (WP-LOOP) L21's `sea.hirl` form (`lpbmat.bas` 55000–55316; §2.13.4 is schematic, the
  records and a worked example are §3.5.9's L21). r, k, c are the extents (r = 1 for a vector a, c =
  1 for a vector b). `xblk P T n` holds `tmp I = a` and `tmp J = b` (each right after its operand's
  subtree), the home `tmp R` (`anew P T 0 0`; a result over `SEA_LIM_FIXED_ELEMS` elements is
  dynamic: a matrix `tmp g = ci r`, `tmp h = ci c`, `anew P T 0 2 (lv g) (lv h)`, a vector of n
  elements, which only k = 0 makes, `tmp g = ci n`, `anew P T 0 1 (lv g)`, not cleared since every
  element is stored; the vector form added by the review's fix, `lpbmat.bas` 55143–55144,
  55177–55181), and then, unless r = 0 or c = 0 (no loop, data or constant is written), the data
  `adat` of R, I and J in that order (`tmp D`, `E`, `F`) and the constants, bound once as `tmp`s in
  this order: B = `cb P 2 1` (true), C = `ci 0`, K = `ci 1`, T = `ci r−1` (a matrix a), V = `ci c−1`
  (a matrix b), X = `ci k−2` (k ≥ 2, also for vector @ matrix, where no record reads it); the value
  is `lv R`. Every loop is §3.5.9's rloop(B, start, last, K; ind), `if (lv B) { hloop … }`, whose
  last is its iteration count − 1, so the chain loop over z = 1 … k−1 has last X = k−2 and k = 1
  writes none. Indices are column-major `wbin` trees with a `ci` stride: a[i,z] = i + z·r, b[z,v] =
  z + v·k, R[i,v] = i + v·r. The running sum S is a `bind` of a scalar `.l` local (R8) whose value
  is the first product, then `asg set` S + product; with k = 0 there is no S and every element
  stored is `cf +0`. Matrix @ matrix has v outer, i inner. Vector @ matrix writes, in each column v,
  `tmp N = ci k` and §3.5.9's sum8 (`lp7red.bas` 35600) unchanged, its `ifx (bin gt (lv N) (lv Z))`
  included, without its `tmp D = data(V)` (E and F are loaded before the loops); the `ifx` is the
  `est`'s value child.
* **L-jh** (WP-CHECK) `ckmm` (`sc9arr.bas` 19341–19385, called from `sc5expr.bas` 10620 for every
  numeric operand pair the 240 and 230 checks leave): an `i64` operand gets an array `cvt` to the
  `f64` array of its shape (fixed-size if it was), an `i64` array literal too, as `+` gives it; when
  exactly one operand is fixed-size, that one gets a `dyn` to the dynamic `f64` type of its rank,
  after its `cvt`. Both are written as for a function argument, at the operand's own position right
  after its subtree: with the fixed operand on the right the `dyn` stands between the right operand
  and the `bin matmul` record, at the right operand's position (`M @ xf`: `lv M`, `lv xf`, `dyn`,
  `bin`); on the left it takes the left operand's position, which is the operator's (§3.3). Two
  fixed-size inner extents that differ are 217 at the operator, the node then of type 0.
* **L-ji** (WP-FUSE) `seafuse` needed no change: `fu4fan.bas` 30260 and 30773 already treat
  `matmul` (with `cat`) as non-fusible, which is L-ix's barrier, and its reader already accepted a
  `bin matmul` with array operands; it grew only by the three `consts` lines.
* **L-jj** (WP-TOOLS) `tools/seaval.bas` checks record formats, field types and the tree (§3.9),
  no operand types: R10, R16 and R35 are semantic rules of §3.5.9, not record formats, so it needs
  no change in 8b (§2.13.4's sentence that it "learns R35" is amended); `sealoop` and `sealower`
  validate R35.
* **L-jk** (WP-RT-A64, WP-RT-X64) The entries 51–53 as built (`rt_gemm.s`; `_sea_variant` in
  `rt_kern.s`): the products are `A[i,j]*x[j]` (GEMV) and `x[kk]*A[kk,j]` (VECMAT) in that operand
  order, and every sum is accumulator + product; a NaN result has the same bits under SSE2 and AVX2
  on one target but may differ between the targets (LANGUAGE.md §6.5: a NaN's sign and payload are
  not observable); GEMV blocks rows 8 → 2 → 1 on NEON and SSE2 and 16 → 4 → 2 → 1 on AVX2, VECMAT
  does one column per pass (L-iz: free); the arm64 entries never read `_sea_variant` (one NEON
  form); the entries check only the inner extents (`SHAPE_MISMATCH`, before any allocation, empty
  operands included); MATMUL's empty shortcut is `sea_arr_new_u` (no element) for r = 0 or c = 0
  and `sea_arr_new` (+0) for k = 0, no kernel called.
* **L-jl** (WP-LACHECK, T1, T2) Test readings: `la_check` compares every non-NaN result bit for bit
  and accepts any NaN for a NaN result (L-jk); a MATMUL element whose exact value is 0 with k > 0
  need only compare `== 0` (GEMM leaves the sign of an exact zero sum open), while k = 0 must give
  +0 bits (no kernel runs); the `la_mm_*` programs print class-R results as `x + 0.0`, so −0 prints
  as 0; `r_la_vm_shape` is T1's although §2.13.10's pattern `r_la_m*` does not match it;
  `la8_mm_rcall` has no `.hirf` because its `sea.hirf` equals its `sea.hir` (`stage.sh` then
  compares `seafuse`'s output with the `.hir` and feeds `sealoop` the `.hir`, L-ek).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 8c (the readings of its work packages, found in their builds and
recorded 2026-11-01 at its integration; each states the code as built and changes no agreed rule;
Decision 130, the user's, is in the decisions list):

* **L-jm** (WP-CHECK) 255 (a `ref` argument) for the five calls names the parameter by its position
  as LANGUAGE.md §10.8 writes it: `lu` and `chol` A; `solve` A, B (a `ref` argument has no value
  type that could choose the F form, so the first is named A); `rcond` F; `eig_sym` A, or K, M with
  two arguments; past the last parameter the function's name, as `ck_lib` does for the other
  library functions.
* **L-jn** (WP-NAME, WP-CHECK) 258 for a struct holding several handles names the first handle met
  in a depth-first walk of the fields in declaration order (a nested struct walked fully before the
  next field; a struct already met skipped); `seaname`'s `tyhd` and `seacheck`'s `hct` use the same
  walk.
* **L-jo** (WP-LOWER) The handle types 6–9 have LIR register class p, as `str` has (what §2.13.4's
  "a handle local counts as any reference local" needs).
* **L-jp** (WP-FUSE, WP-EXPAND) Neither `seafuse` nor `seaexpand` changed: the five calls are leaves
  and barriers by F1 (2) (L-ix), and G12 already accepts their trees.
* **L-jq** (WP-CHECK, the `dyn` position) For the five calls a fixed-size argument's `dyn` stands at
  the call's position (as Decision 39 for `sort`, L-iq), while an `i64` argument's `cvt` stands at
  the argument's; unlike `@`, where L-jh puts the `dyn` at the operand.
* **L-jr** (WP-LU-A64, WP-LU-X64, the handles) A `Chol` handle stores ‖A‖₁ = +0 (offset 24) and −1
  in the zero-pivot field (offset 32); bytes 40–63 are 0 in both kinds; the ‖A‖₁ sums start from +0;
  `rcond` returns the stored NaN norm itself in the NaN case. `tests/la/la_check.c` reads the handle
  at these runtime-private offsets and must change with the layout.
* **L-js** (WP-LU-*, the private routines as built) `sea_la_potrf(a, n, ld, w)` returns 0 or 1 + the
  index of the first pivot not > 0 (NaN included), works in place on the upper triangle only, leaves
  the strict lower triangle +0 on success, and touches w (n · `SEA_LA_NB` doubles) only when n >
  `SEA_LA_NB` (0 may be passed otherwise); `sea_la_issym(a, n, ld)` returns 1 or 0 and is a leaf.
  Visibility: `.private_extern` on arm64, `.globl` with `.hidden` on x86_64 (as
  `_sea_alloc`/`sea_alloc`).
* **L-jt** (WP-LU-*, WP-EIG-*, scratch and failure cleanup) W is allocated only when n >
  `SEA_LA_NB`; `SOLVE`'s one scratch block is the factor (8n² bytes), then W (only when n > NB),
  then the n u32 pivots; before `_sea_err(SINGULAR)` in `SOLVE` and `_sea_err(NOT_POSDEF)` in
  `EIG_SYM_GEN` both runtimes free the scratch block and then the already-allocated result (as a
  failing `sea_chol` frees its handle); unobservable today, since `_sea_err` exits, but the two
  targets agree.
* **L-ju** (WP-EIG-*, readings of the transcription) `tql1`'s search for a negligible e[m] ends at m =
  n − 1 (e[n−1] = 0 by `tql1`'s own comment; it matters only when tst1 is NaN, as when `tred1`'s
  scale overflows); `tql1`'s own ordering step is kept (p ≥ d[i−1] stops it, equal values keep their
  order) and §10.6's stable sort runs after it (it moves only NaNs); on a `SEA_EIG_MAXIT` failure at
  l, d[0..l−1] keep their values and d[l..n−1] are NaN, then sorted NaN-last; for n ≥ 2 an
  eigenvalue −0 comes out +0 (p = d[l] + f with f from +0), while for n = 1 A[0,0] is returned
  unchanged; `EIG_SYM_GEN` tests every one of C's n² elements for a non-finite value; Z overwrites a
  copy of K and C overwrites Z in place; finite input near overflow is transcribed as written
  (`eig_sym([1e308 1e308; 1e308 1e308])` gives 0x7FE1CCF385EBC8A0 twice, pinned by the rt tests).
* **L-jv** (WP-LACHECK, T1, the runtime tests; extends L-jl) On exact data, factors and solutions are
  compared by value (`==`) wherever a Baysick kernel may run (exact data fixes the values but not
  the sign of an exact zero); a `Chol`'s strict lower triangle, the interchanges and the
  hand-derived n ≤ NB cases are compared bit for bit.

Lead decisions of sub-phase 8d (the readings of its work packages, found in their builds and
recorded 2026-11-02 at its integration; each states the code as built and changes no agreed rule,
except that L-jw amends the wording of §2.13.9 item 2, "filtered standard output", now corrected
there):

* **L-jw** (WP-CROSS) `cross_run.sh` keeps a deferred run's standard output as written, its
  `Compute time` line included: `compare_report.py` needs that line at its place and skips it
  itself; `cross_accept.sh` removes it (the host's `filter=compute-time`) only for the byte
  comparison with the packed `NAME.out`.
* **L-jx** (WP-CROSS) In `cross_accept.sh`'s except check a JSON key is byte-equal when the key
  lists other than the excepted keys are equal and in the same order and each value is structurally
  equal with every number compared as its printed text; a token-map entry names K when its rule is
  `json K`; a line is excepted when such an entry's regex matches the Mac's packed `NAME.out` line.
* **L-jy** (WP-CROSS, small choices) The variant label in kept file names and `DEFER` lines is the
  `VARIANTS` word (`default`, `sse2`); `cross.sh` calls `cross_accept.sh` (and so needs `uv`) only
  when D > 0 or N > 0; a deferred run writing an unexpected extra file is a host failure, as for
  every port; a kept file that no `DEFER` line names is a setup error.
* **L-jz** (W3, the `f_nat` line) W3's `Linear natural frequencies` line prints `f_nat`, which has
  no `RULES` entry, so its tokens take the default rule and no token-map entry names `f_nat`;
  `cross_accept.sh` therefore compares that line byte for byte across targets. Accepted: both
  printed values are more than 1e-5 relative from a rounding boundary of their `%.3f` (1.1975144
  against 1.1975; 11.8866 against 11.8865), while class R differs by about 1e-15.
* **L-ka** (W3, the `Best` line) Token 5 prints `cSweep(iBest)`, not `i_best` itself; §2.13.9's
  "`json i_best`" is read as applying `i_best`'s exact rule to that token, as W7 does with `json G`
  at `i_best`.
* **L-kb** (W2, `solve_free`) `solve_free` keeps one signature (`F: f64[,]`); single right-hand
  sides are passed as `F.col` and read back as `[:, 0]`, so every solve has MATLAB's call shape.
* **L-kc** (W2, a range argument) A range passed as a value argument is parenthesized
  (`setdiff((0..nDof), fixedDof)`), by LANGUAGE.md §6.1 item 11.
* **L-kd** (W2 and W3, the token maps) Header-line tokens (geometry counts, steel mass, the sweep
  and influence lines, worst utilisation, applied total) take the default rule, as §2.13.9 says;
  key rules relative to the largest magnitude are converted to absolute `num` rules in the report's
  units (L-eg): `N0` in kN `num 2.109286e-5 0`, the midspan deflection in mm `num 1.921908e-6 0`,
  the reactions in kN `num 8.476971e-6 0`; the minimum FOS `json fos0`; the group count `exact`;
  Amin and Amax `json A_cat`; converged `exact`; `e_crit0` and `r_worst` by their `json` rules. W3
  converts in the same way its compression and extension travels to mm
  (`num 7.658217699648738e-7 0`, `num 4.690892221356693e-7 0`) and its lift percentage to
  `num 0.028567347521782603 0` (200/7001).

**Lead decisions of phase 9** (written 2026-11-02 with the text of §2.14, revised after one
independent review, and agreed by the user together with Decisions 131–142 on 2026-11-02); each is a
reading where LANGUAGE.md or the earlier rules leave a choice, written into §2.14:

* **L-ke** (the object model) A figure's whole state is in the `Figure` object's store; an `Axes`
  value is a counted reference to its figure plus an axes record index. Nothing refers to an `Axes`
  object, so no reference cycle exists, dropping an `Axes` value never loses what was drawn, and the
  figure is freed with the last `Figure` or `Axes` value (LANGUAGE.md §12.1's reference semantics).
* **L-kf** (data copies) A series copies its vectors and matrix into one uncounted block at the call
  (LANGUAGE.md §12.1: "with copies of their data"), never retaining the argument array; strings
  (`name`, labels, titles, category labels) are retained, since they are immutable.
* **L-kg** (signatures and checks) §12's parameters with a default are options, given by name only;
  `i64` and fixed-size arguments convert as for the phase-8 calls; each entry validates in parameter
  order at the call's site and nothing is validated later; properties keep their last value;
  `save_svg` may be repeated and draws the state at that moment.
* **L-kh** (colours) A series takes `color`, else its style letter, else the next cycle colour, and
  only that last case advances the cycle (index mod 7); `xline` follows the same rule (§12.3's bullet
  is general); a bar series has one colour; hex digits of either case are accepted and written in
  lower case.
* **L-ki** (style strings) Scanned left to right with `--` and `-.` tried before `-`; at most one line
  part, one marker, one colour letter; a marker without a line part draws markers only; neither
  draws a solid line; a marker in `xline`'s style is `invalid line style`.
* **L-kj** (extents) Non-finite values are skipped value by value; `xline` is not data for the
  limits (MATLAB's constant lines are not either); bars include the baseline 0; contours give their
  grid coordinates; an axis with no data has the limits 0 … 1; a non-finite `xline` position draws
  an empty path.
* **L-kk** (ticks) §12.5's "repeated multiplication and division by 10" is read as 10ᵏ by k
  multiplications for k ≥ 0 and 1 / 10⁻ᵏ for k < 0. For |k| ≤ 22 each decade is the correctly
  rounded value (10²² and every smaller power are exact in `f64`, so k ≥ 0 is exact and k < 0 one
  correctly rounded division); beyond 22 the multiplications round, so d(k) need not be the nearest
  `f64` to 10ᵏ, but it is deterministic (the same operations in the same order on both targets) and
  the steps and texts depend only on it. k is bounded to −300 … 300; the step search of §2.14.6,
  each count tested "≤ 7" (false when infinite or NaN) before any integer conversion; an axis with
  no step, or with a non-finite default limit, keeps lo … hi and has no ticks; a zero range is
  widened only to finite limits (v ± |v|/10, else v ± 1, else 0 … 1); explicit and tight limits keep
  their values and take the inside ticks; equal and non-finite ticks are not drawn; a tick −0 is 0;
  repeated texts follow Decision 142 (a).
* **L-kl** (coordinates) The mapping formulas of §2.14.6 in that operation order; coordinates clamped
  to −`SEA_LIM_PLOT_PX` … 2 · `SEA_LIM_PLOT_PX` before any use (NaN and −∞ to the lower bound, +∞
  to the upper), every length and offset written computed from the clamped values, so no number
  prints hundreds of digits and none is NaN; data outside the plot area is hidden by the panel's
  clip path; image colours and contour levels need a finite zmax − zmin and finite levels (else
  entry 0, no level), and a bar needs finite ends.
* **L-km** (twins) A pair shares x, title, x label, grid, legend, x limits, x category labels and
  `axis_equal` (stored in the base record; a call on the twin writes there); `ylabel`, `ylim`,
  `y_ticks` and `y_reverse` act on the axes' own y-axis; the pair's x extent takes both axes'
  series.
* **L-kn** (legend) A property of the pair: drawn when a location is set and a line or bar series of
  the pair has a non-empty label (contours, images and `xline`s have no label); entries in call
  order; `best` is `northeast`; the box geometry of §2.14.6 (8 px padding rows of 16 px, samples 20
  px wide).
* **L-ko** (right margin and colorbar) 68 px with a twin or a colorbar, 120 px with both (the
  colorbar right of the twin's labels); the colorbar is that of the pair's last image with
  `colorbar: true`, its ticks an explicit-limit axis over the image's finite range.
* **L-kp** (text) XML escaping of `& < > "` (§12.8) and bytes 0x00–0x1F other than tab, LF and CR
  written as spaces, which XML 1.0 does not allow; widths 0.6 × size per byte; other bytes copied
  (a string that is not UTF-8 makes an SVG a strict parser rejects; the tests use UTF-8 text).
* **L-kq** (bars) Δ is the smallest positive difference of the sorted finite x values (1 with fewer
  than two distinct values); a bar with a non-finite x or height is not drawn, a zero height is.
* **L-kr** (images) The extent and orientation rules of §2.14.6 (cell centres at the first and last
  coordinates, half a cell beyond; PNG rows top-down so that y[0] is at the bottom of a normal
  axis); ±∞ cells take the map's ends, NaN cells white, a constant image entry 0; an image with no
  cell or a non-finite extent draws nothing.
* **L-ks** (contours) Levels ascending, then cells column-major; "above" is ≥; edges interpolated
  from their first corner (shared edges give equal points); the saddle rule by the centre's state
  against corner a's; a non-finite corner or coordinate skips the cell; labels at the first segment's
  midpoint, `%g`.
* **L-kt** (PNG) RGB, depth 8, one IDAT, stored blocks of at most 65 535 bytes, filter 0 on every
  row, CRC-32 computed bitwise (no table, no state), Adler-32 with deferred reduction, base64
  without line breaks; an IDAT over 2³¹ − 1 bytes is `out of memory`.
* **L-ku** (entries) One entry per call with every parameter (defaults inserted by pass 2a), never
  an option record; `PLOT`'s site and `CONTOUR`'s last two integer-class arguments travel in stack
  slots on x86_64 (§4.8's "further parameters", implemented by pass 4 for calls and now used by
  `rcall`), tested by `plot9_rcall` and every plot program.
* **L-kv** (capacities) The `entries` capacity of `sealower`, `seagen_a64` and `seagen_x64` becomes
  128 (L-cs's two lines per pass); the `lirrw` passes keep 399. (`sealower`'s line budget for phase
  9 is Decision 141.)
* **L-kw** (constants) The layout numbers of LANGUAGE.md §12.5–§12.7 are local equates of the
  runtime files (`RTP_*`), not contract values; the figure layouts (`RTP_AX_SIZE`, `RTP_SR_SIZE`, the
  offsets of §2.14.6) are runtime-private, the same in both runtimes, and read by `tests/rt` (as
  L-jr's handle offsets).
* **L-kx** (the phase rule) 9b empties the phase-rule table: 259 becomes unreachable (its code
  kept), `seaname`'s branch for the types 6 and 7 goes, `seacheck`'s fallback at `sc6call.bas` 12635
  stays as the guard for a name missing from its table (unreachable when every predeclared name has
  a row); `err_ns_lib_figure`, `err_ns_handle` and `res_err_handle` are retired.
* **L-ky** (port readings) MATLAB's several x/y pairs in one `plot` are several calls; a matrix `y`
  (W7) is one call per row; legend texts given in `legend(…)` become the series' `label:`s; `bar(v)`
  without x takes MATLAB's positions 1 … n (W2), or 0 … n − 1 with category labels (W4, as
  `x_ticks` places them); `sprintf` titles are `format`; `yyaxis left/right` is the axes and its
  `twin_y`; `hold` and `axis xy` need no statement.
* **L-kz** (acceptance) `tests/accept.sh` runs each port once with `--export-reference --figures`;
  the run directory holds `NAME.json` and `output/NAME.svg` only; step 4 is `plot_struct.py` on
  `ports/NAME.struct`.
* **L-la** (cross files) The `NAME.expect/` mechanism of program and port cases takes
  subdirectories (`output/NAME.svg`); a `plots/` case packs every file its `.struct` names; every
  port packs `NAME.expect/output/NAME.svg`, the deferred ones included, and a deferred run keeps
  `NAME.VARIANT.svg` (`defer_variant`); a kept SVG is compared byte for byte unless the port's `// cross:`
  line has `svg=approx` (W2, Decision 138).
* **L-lb** (freeing) `Figure` and `Axes` objects are counted in `_sea_live` by their constructors
  (`FIGURE`, `PANEL`, `TWIN_Y`) and uncounted by `sea_free`; the `Axes` branch releases its figure
  through `_sea_release`; the `Figure` branch releases every string it retained and frees every
  uncounted block it owns; the `FREE` row of §4.8 says so.
* **L-lc** (the file) The document is built completely in memory, then written by one open, a write
  loop and a close; the buffer is freed before an error is reported (as L-jt), so a failed build
  creates no file and a failed write may leave a partial one.
* **L-ld** (private helpers, not entries, no `rt.inc` record) `_sea_fmt_num(dst, letter, prec, x)`
  in `rt_fmt.s` (one finite `f64` under `f` or `g` with the given precision, through
  `Lrt_fmt_float`); `_sea_file_put(path, bytes, len, site, cap)` in `rt_file.s` (the open/write/close
  of L-lc with `rt_file.s`'s errno handling; with cap ≠ 0 it frees the block (bytes, cap) before an
  error is reported and after the write; amended in 9b from four arguments, whose buffer leaked on a
  file error); `_sea_crc32`, `_sea_adler32`, `_sea_b64` and the PNG
  builder in `rt_png.s`; visibility `.private_extern` on arm64 and `.globl` with `.hidden` on x86_64
  (as L-js).
* **L-le** (drawing order) The data group draws the pair's series in call order, a twin's series
  interleaved with the base's by call order; images and contours are not moved below lines (W4 draws
  the image, then the contour, as MATLAB does).
* **L-lf** (order of the 9b build) All 21 ids enter `rt.inc` with WP-CONTRACT, before 9c's code, as
  8b did for 51–61; until 9c a program calling `bar`, `barh`, `contour` or `image` compiles and
  fails only at link, and no 9b test calls them.

Lead decisions of sub-phase 9b (the readings of its work packages and of its review, found in their
builds and recorded 2026-11-03 at its integration; each states the code as built, and those that
change bytes are also written into §2.14.6, which stays the single source):

* **L-lg** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; the limits rules) The limits rules of §2.14.6 apply in their
  numbered order. Explicit limits (rule 1) and rule 6's recomputation give numeric ticks even on an
  axis with category labels; category ticks arise only under rule 2. The lead's ruling; the x86_64
  runtime was aligned to it in the review.
* **L-lh** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; ties and repeated texts) An extent end is updated only on a
  strict `<` (lo) or `>` (hi), so of equal values the first wins. The suppression of an equal tick
  compares with the last tick appended. Decision 142's loop tries q = 7 … 17 in turn and stops at
  the first q that makes all adjacent texts differ, else q = 17.
* **L-li** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; `_sea_fmt_num`) `_sea_fmt_num` is a pure conversion; the callers
  add +0.0 where §2.14.6 asks for it. Its destination buffer holds every finite `f64` (336 bytes on
  arm64, 352 on x86_64; target-local). The heading's x `{W/2}` is f64(W) / 2 written `%.2f`.
* **L-lj** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; field contents) The figure allocates both tables (capacity 8)
  when it is created. The axes record's string fields keep a retained `""` (the writer tests the
  length); a series' label stores 0 for `""`. These are target-local field contents with no effect
  on the bytes written; `tests/rt` reads the offsets per target.
* **L-lk** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; WP-CHECK, the passes agent's L-lg) The 21 plotting classes 32–52
  are looked up by `sc9plot`'s `pcls`, called from `ck_lib`'s fallback (`sc6call.bas` 12635) and
  from `ck_narg`. One table serves the call and its named options; `NOT_SUPPORTED` stays as an
  unreachable guard (L-kx).
* **L-ll** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; settling untyped constants) An untyped integer constant passed
  positionally beyond the positional parameters is typed `i64`, and the 243 message lists it as
  `i64`. An untyped value of a named option takes the option's type (`f64` for an `f` option, else
  `i64`). A `ref` argument past the last positional parameter is counted and reported as 243.
* **L-lm** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; `cty`, a pre-existing defect fixed in 9b) The type of a bound
  value as written is its type after its `cvt` and then its `dyn` or `fix`. This fixes a latent
  `sealoop` `BAD_RECORD` for reordered calls and struct literals that pass an `i64` array to an
  `f64` array parameter or field. Tests: the programs `call6_named_cvt_fixed`,
  `call6_named_cvt_dyn`, `struct_order_cvt_fixed`, `struct_order_cvt_dyn` and
  `plots/plot_cvt_order`.
* **L-ln** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; WP-LOWER) The 21 rows find their entry by the `lib`'s name in
  capitals, through a separate table of 12-byte slots, `K5$` (W2 33–53). Validation uses the
  entry's Args classes. Array operands are allowed for `plot bar barh contour image x_ticks
  y_ticks` (`sl4fix.bas` 40162).
* **L-lo** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; WP-LOOP) R36 checks only the children of an array type (a dynamic
  `f64` vector or matrix, or a dynamic `str` vector) and copies the node; the scalar and handle
  classes are checked in `sealower`.
* **L-lp** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; contract) The plotting limits sit in their own section at the end
  of `limits.inc`, so the `DATA` positions that `tests/check_data.sh` checks stay unchanged.
  `tests/include_asserts.inc`'s assertion that `USER` is the last run-time code becomes
  `SEA_E_USER == 21`.
* **L-lq** (9b, agreed 2026-11-03; tests)
  * `tests/plots.sh` accepts `--save-out DIR` and `--only NAME` for cross packing.
  * A `.struct` bare key with no value is malformed (exit 2), and `subpaths` counts the `M`
    commands of a path's `d`.
  * `KEY~` works on every key: keys with selector fields (`count`, `subpaths`, `color`) keep their
    selectors literal and match the regex against the last field; `file~` and `panel~` select the
    single match and fail on none or several; `canvas~` matches `W H` and `panels~` the decimal
    count.
  * The T2 dumps are reproduced by `tests/vectors/plot9_dumps.py`; the hand check against §2.14.4,
    rule 39 and Decision 39 is the authority.
  * The rt tests' hand-derived SVG bytes (`rt_plot_svg*`, `rt_plot_svg_cat`) test the runtime
    against §2.14.6, not the language; this is consistent with Decision 140 (a).

Lead decisions of sub-phase 9c (the readings of its work packages and of its review, found in their
builds and recorded 2026-11-03 at its integration; each states the code as built, and those that
change bytes are also written into §2.14.6, which stays the single source):

* **L-lr** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; the known answers' files) In `rt_plot_kat.out` the `crc32` and
  `adler32` lines alternate per input in §2.14.8's order; the empty base64 input is the line
  `b64 0 ` (TEXT empty, one trailing blank); the 21 846 × 1 PNG's 65 538 pixel bytes (r, g, b per
  pixel, left to right) are the seeded sequence's first 65 538 bytes; the PNG lines come in the
  order 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 21 846 × 1, 1 × 256, `pngb64` after the first two; hex upper case, 8 digits.
* **L-ls** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; barh extents) A `barh` series gives 0 to x unconditionally (also
  when it is empty or has no finite h), then each finite hᵢ; its y-axis gets i − width/2 and
  i + width/2 for every i = 0 … n − 1, width/2 computed once. A labelled `barh` series is a legend
  entry drawn with the bar sample, as a `bar` series is, even when it draws no bar; a series that
  draws no bar still writes its empty `<g class="bars">` group.
* **L-lt** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; image extent) An image draws nothing and gives no extent unless
  n, m ≥ 1 and all four ends are finite; then x gets a, b and its own y-axis a_y, b_y. Rule 3
  (tight limits) applies when the pair holds any image series, drawn or not.
* **L-lu** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; colorbar) The colorbar is that of the pair's last image with
  `colorbar: true`, whether or not that image is drawn; xc = ((px + pw) + 12) (+ 52 with a twin),
  the additions in that order; its ticks use rule 4's widening only, then the explicit-limit ticks
  and the normal tick texts; the `colorbar-ticks` path is written even with no tick (empty `d`).
* **L-lv** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; contours) The outer `contour` group is always written, a level's
  group only when the level has a segment; the labels follow the outer `</g>`, one per drawn level
  ascending, `%g` of L_k with no `+0.0`; both coordinates of an edge point use p1 + t · (p2 − p1),
  the constant one included, so a non-finite t clamps both; a corner equal to a level counts as
  above it (≥).
* **L-lw** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; level colour) floor(256k/(n + 1)) is computed exactly in integer
  arithmetic on both targets; n + 1 is converted as a signed integer, so `levels` is in practice
  bounded far below 2⁵³ by the level loop (both targets alike; no test).
* **L-lx** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; private helpers, L-ld) Besides `_sea_crc32`, `_sea_adler32`,
  `_sea_b64` (x86_64 `sea_crc32`, `sea_adler32`, `sea_b64`, `.hidden`), each runtime has a PNG
  builder (arm64 `_sea_png(raw, rawlen, w, h, site)`, x86_64 `sea_png(raw, w, h, site)`), the
  colour map table built at first use, `rt_plot2.s` hooks for extents, the colorbar and the series
  writers, and private aliases (`.private_extern` / `.hidden`) of `rt_plot.s`'s writer routines; all
  target-local, none a contract.
* **L-ly** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; scratch memory) All PNG and colorbar scratch comes from
  `_sea_alloc` uncounted and is freed with `_sea_free_block` (the review moved x86_64's colorbar raw
  data from a static buffer); every check of entries 68–71 runs before any allocation, so no error
  path leaks.
* **L-lz** (9c, agreed 2026-11-03; `.struct` keys of 9c) The review found no check of contour
  segments, labels or image pixels against spec-derived values (a mistake common to both runtimes
  would pass the cross run); the keys `clabel`, `segment` and `pixels` are added to §2.14.8's
  table, their values derived by `plot9_cases.py` from §2.14.6 alone.
* **L-ma** (9d, agreed 2026-11-03; port readings) W1's a4 middle row, MATLAB's `round(end/2)`, is the
  0-based row `idiv(rows(dGrid) + 1, 2) - 1`, 44 of 90 (22.5 kW; the legends 45.0, 22.5 and 0.5 kW).
  W2's member loop variable is `el`, since `e` is a top-level variable. W3's `kRef` is 7 (MATLAB's
  8). W7's a3 title uses `Gsweep[iBest[0, 0]]` (`iBest` holds 0-based indices).
* **L-mb** (9d, agreed 2026-11-03; skeleton lexing) An attribute value for Decision 138 is the quoted
  value of an attribute in an element start tag. The XML declaration, comments, CDATA and end tags are
  copied unchanged, so they are compared byte for byte. Only an attribute named exactly `href` is
  exempt. A pair of numbers is compared in hundredths only when both have exactly two fraction
  digits; otherwise the texts must be equal, so 0.30 against 0.3 fails.
* **L-mc** (9d, agreed 2026-11-03; the run directory) The rule that the run directory holds only
  `NAME.json` and `output/NAME.svg` besides the executable is checked over every file and directory
  by relative path, the directory `output` itself allowed, so an empty extra directory fails too.
* **L-md** (9d, agreed 2026-11-03; shape lines) The ports' longer headers move the source lines the
  `vector` shape lines name: W1 259–265, W4 296 (`rb_half_sweep` 289–298). The `.shape` files and
  §2.12's current text follow; the 7f records keep the lines of their time.

**Lead decisions of phase L** (written 2026-11-02/03 with the text of §2.15, revised after one
independent review, and agreed by the user together with Decisions 143–150 on 2026-11-03); each is
a reading where LANGUAGE.md or the earlier rules leave a choice, written into §2.15:

* **L-me** (effects) `read_lines` has effects in LANGUAGE.md §8.1's sense (it reads a file, whose
  contents can depend on what the program wrote with `write_json` before): it joins `cpre`'s list
  (228 in an elemental function), is never removed as dead (so a missing file is reported even when
  the result is unused) and keeps its place among the other effects. `split`, `substr`, the parse
  functions and the bitwise functions have no effects (§8.1), but an unused call is never removed
  either: in `sea.lir` it is an `rcall` (an effect instruction) or a `chk` (a failing one), which
  §5.8's T10 does not delete, so its run-time error is reported whether or not the result is used
  (`r_lib_parse_unused`, `r_lib_shift_unused`).
* **L-mf** (lines) LANGUAGE.md §3.1's rule read for data: a line ends at LF; one CR before that LF,
  or one CR at the very end of the file, is removed; the bytes after the last LF form a line when
