  there are any; an empty file has no line; every other byte is kept, with no decoding, no BOM
  removal and no check of UTF-8.
* **L-mg** (reading) `open(path, O_RDONLY)`, `read` into one growing uncounted buffer (65 536
  bytes, doubled) in requests of at most 2³⁰ bytes (Darwin's `read` may refuse a larger count)
  until `read` returns 0, `EINTR` retried (the runtime-local `RT_FILE_EINTR` = 4 on both hosts),
  `close` with its result ignored; a NUL byte in the path is `cannot open` with `EINVAL`, as
  `make_dir`'s is `cannot create directory` with `EINVAL`; an `open` failure
  `cannot open`, a `read` failure `cannot read` (a directory: `EISDIR`); the whole file is read
  before any string is made; the scratch blocks are freed before every check the entry makes
  itself. A path is a host path; `-` is a file named `-` (standard input is not read).
* **L-mh** (split) Non-overlapping occurrences scanned left to right; occurrences + 1 fields;
  empty fields kept, nothing trimmed, `split("", sep)` is `[""]`; an empty separator is an error,
  never "split into bytes"; every element a new string, none sharing the argument.
* **L-mi** (parse_i64) The base is any `i64` expression, checked at run time (2 … 36), before the
  text; the text is an optional `+`/`-` and digits of the base in either case, nothing else; the
  value exact in −2⁶³ … 2⁶³ − 1 (the magnitude accumulated negatively so −2⁶³ parses); one error
  for a syntax and a range failure; the text quoted whole and as is in the message.
* **L-mj** (parse_f64) The grammar of §2.15.2, wider than Sea's literals (`.5`, `5.` and a leading
  sign accepted, no `_`), the eight words Sea writes accepted, no hex floats, no blanks, no
  `infinity`; the value correctly rounded (round to nearest even), overflow ±∞, underflow the
  nearest subnormal or ±0, the sign of zero kept. The runtime validates the grammar itself, then
  calls the host `strtod` in the C locale on a NUL-terminated copy, as it calls `snprintf` for
  output (LANGUAGE.md §11.1, §4.5). Both hosts' `strtod` are believed correctly rounded (Apple's
  Libc uses David Gay's `gdtoa`, glibc its multi-precision `strtod`); **unverified** on these
  exact versions until `lib_parse_f64_kat` and the rt known answers pass on both targets against
  Python's correctly rounded `float()` and the compiler's own literal conversion. If either host
  differs, Lc stops and the lead brings a Decision (Sea's own conversion in assembly, as phase 3
  did for the elementary functions) before going on.
* **L-mk** (substr) `substr(s, lo, hi)` is `s[lo..hi]` in meaning and checks (§5.1, §5.4): an
  empty range never fails, else the first position, else the last, is reported with dimension 0
  and extent `len(s)`; the result is always a new string (never the argument retained, even for
  the whole string).
* **L-ml** (bitwise) Two's-complement bits; `shl` discards the bits shifted out and never reports
  `integer overflow`; `shr` logical, `sar` arithmetic; the count 0 … 63 checked after both
  arguments are evaluated (`invalid shift count`); elemental on `i64` arrays with §6.3's
  broadcasting, a check failing at the first element in linear order; `bitnot` lowers to `ixor`
  with −1 (LIR `bnot` is logical); not constant expressions (§7.2), not folded by pass 2.
* **L-mm** (`%x`) `i64` arguments only (an untyped literal is `i64`; any other type, `bool`
  included, is 210 `format "%x" expects i64, found T` with the conversion as written); the bits
  printed unsigned; C99's width, precision and `- 0 #` flags laid out in C's order (prefix, zeros,
  digits: `%#010x` of 255 is `0x000000ff`); `+` and space accepted and ignored (Decision 150 (d));
  the runtime's own digit loop in base 16, no `snprintf`.
* **L-mn** (signatures) The text calls take scalars (`str`, `i64`); `base:` is an option, named
  only, with the default 10; results: `str[]` for `read_lines` and `split`, `str` for `substr`,
  `i64`, `f64`; the written form names every parameter (`lib parse_i64 2` with `ci 10` inserted),
  as 9b's plotting calls do (L-kg).
* **L-mo** (front-end placement) The seven bitwise functions join `ck_lib`'s class 2 (as `idiv`),
  `bitnot` by an arity test at the class's branch (no new class, so neither the `lred` path nor
  the reference-argument path is reached); the text calls are classes 53–57 of `sc9plot.bas`'s
  table-driven part, reusing its options, defaults and written form, their result types set after
  26510 (`str[]` through `tarr`, `i64`, `f64`, `str`); `sealoop`'s R37; `sealower`'s rule 40 in
  `sl1scal.bas` beside `idiv`, and rule 39's rows through `K5$`, the arity strings and the
  plotting calls' generic entry path (34063–34069, 34006, the alphabets gaining digits), as
  §2.15.4 writes them.
* **L-mp** (fixtures for rt tests) `tests/rt/run_rt.sh`, `run_rt_linux.sh` and `tests/cross_run.sh`
  (its own x86_64 rt loop, lines 564–594) copy `NAME.files/` into the fresh working directory
  before the run, as `tests/run.sh` does; `cross_pack.sh` packs it for rt tests. No other runner
  changes: programs and error tests already have fixtures.
* **L-mq** (entries) Five entries 83–87, all `S`, arguments borrowed, results owned, the elements
  of a `str[]` result new strings counted in `_sea_live`; `SEA_ENT_COUNT` 87 within the capacity
  128 (L-kv), so no capacity line changes.
* **L-mr** (no vector forms) The bitwise functions have no SIMD form: T13 vectorizes `f64` lanes
  only, so an `i64` loop stays scalar (fused, unrolled by T11 where it applies); phase 10 may
  measure it.
* **L-ms** (errors) Six new codes 30–35 (Decision 148 (a)) with the texts of §2.15.2;
  `CANNOT_OPEN`, `INDEX_OOB`, `ARRAY_SIZE` and `OUT_OF_MEMORY` reused with their texts; the check
  order of each call is its parameter order.
* **L-mt** (scalars only) The text calls are not elemental: `str` is not an elemental parameter
  type (LANGUAGE.md §8.5), and a loop over `str[]` is what W8's decode writes; an element-wise
  `parse_f64` over a `str[]` is later library work if a workload needs it.
* **L-mu** (limits) No new contract limit: lines and fields are `str`s (`SEA_LIM_STR_BYTES`) and
  their number an extent (`SEA_LIM_EXTENT`, reported by `ARR_NEW` as `invalid array size`); the
  first buffer, the `read` request cap and `parse_f64`'s stack buffer are runtime-local equates
  (`RTT_CHUNK`, `RTT_RDMAX`, `RTT_FBUF`),
  which no output depends on (L-kw's reading).
* **L-mv** (name collisions) The twelve new predeclared names collide only with functions named
  `split`, all renamed `parts` in Lb (5 bytes, so no dump column moves): WP-CONTRACT renames
  §3.4.1's worked example and the two `tests/lib_check.sh` patterns that mutate it (2740, 2742)
  in one change, since `lib_check.sh` reads the document; T1 renames `tests/passes/rs.sea` and its
  goldens `rs.ast`, `rs.res`, `rs.hir1`, the programs `tests/programs/arr_fixed_vals.sea` and
  `arr_locals_params.sea`, and their generators `tests/vectors/arr4e_cases.py` and
  `arr4d_cases.py`. The programs' outputs do not contain the name and stay unchanged; the dumps
  and the example change only in the name. No port or prelude function uses any of the names.
* **L-mw** (no phase-rule rows) Every name enters with its front end in Lb; the text calls fail
  only at link until Lc's runtime defines their symbols (L-lf's reading), so no `not supported
  yet` row is added and 259 stays unreachable.
* **L-mx** (private helpers) `_sea_str_make(bytes, len, site)` is `rt_str.s`'s existing private
  helper exported under that name (arm64 `Lrt_str_from` → `_sea_str_make`, `.private_extern`;
  x86_64 `.Lrt_str_of` → `sea_str_make`, `.hidden`; renamed, not duplicated, its callers in
  `rt_str.s` updated); it, the parse and split scanners in `rt_text.s`, and `READ_LINES`'s use of
  `rt_file.s`'s private routines are target-local, none a contract; `rt_args.s` may later use
  `_sea_str_make` (no behaviour change, not required by this phase).
* **L-my** (fusion of the shifts; found in Lb, agreed 2026-11-04) `shl`, `shr`, `sar` are failing
  element computations (§2.12.2) and join `seafuse`'s list of calls with a run-time check, as
  `idiv`; by F1 (2) they fuse only as a tree's root. So `bitand(shr(v, 8), 0x3FFFF)` over an
  `i64[]` is two loops (the `shr` materialized into a temporary, then the fused `bitand` nest),
  while `shr(bitand(v, 0xFF0), 4)` and any tree of the quiet `bitand bitor bitxor bitnot` is one
  nest. §2.15.4's `seafuse` sentence calling the first example "one nest" is corrected
  accordingly; the values are the same either way.
* **L-mz** (the order of `READ_LINES`'s checks; found in Lc, agreed 2026-11-04) `READ_LINES`
  frees its buffer B before every check of its own. For a line count above `SEA_LIM_EXTENT` the
  arm64 runtime frees B and lets `ARR_NEW` report `ARRAY_SIZE`; the x86_64 runtime reports
  `ARRAY_SIZE` (count) itself after freeing B: the same message, slots and exit status either way.
  Likewise a line above `SEA_LIM_STR_BYTES` is checked before `_sea_str_make` is called
  (§2.15.6, steps 5 and 6).
* **L-na** (the capacity bound) §2.15.6's "a capacity above 2⁶² is `OUT_OF_MEMORY`" reads: the
  buffer doubles while the new capacity is at most 2⁶²; a doubling that would give more is
  `OUT_OF_MEMORY`.
* **L-nb** (the rt known-answer file) `tests/rt/<target>/rt_lib_kat.out`, written identically for
  both targets by `tests/vectors/libL_cases.py` and the expected stdout of `rt_lib_kat.s`, which
  embeds the same inputs, calls the entries directly and prints in this format. One case per line,
  LF-ended, fields separated by one space, every text in double quotes; texts hold only printable
  ASCII 0x20–0x7E without `"` and `\` (no escaping). `parse_i64 B "T" V` (base, text, the result in
  decimal); `parse_f64 "T" H` (the result's 64 bits as 16 lowercase hex digits, a NaN as
  `7ff8000000000000`); `split "S" "P" C "F1" … "FC"` (string, non-empty separator, field count,
  the fields); `substr "S" L H "R"` (string, lo, hi in decimal, the result). The sections follow in
  that order; only cases that do not fail appear (an error ends the process). The file holds 391
  cases (114, 206, 37 and 34).
* **L-nc** (the stack bound) The frame bound of §2.15.5 is measured directly, with a guard fill
  below the incoming sp and `SEA_STACK_MARGIN` as the limit (`rt_lib_abi`), for every entry with
  its callees, and recorded in §4.8. The 512-byte own-frame rule is checked by reading the code,
  except for `PARSE_I64`, which calls nothing on success and is held to it directly on arm64.
* **L-nd** (the search in `SPLIT`) `SPLIT` may find its matches with any search that gives the
  same leftmost non-overlapping matches as §2.15.6's scan: the x86_64 runtime uses `memchr` and
  `memcmp`; the arm64 runtime a byte loop, with a counting loop for a one-byte separator.
* **L-ne** (two readings of §2.15.8) `lib_parse_f64_kat`'s "300 random doubles written with
  `%.17g` and as their shortest round-trip text" reads as 150 doubles, each written both ways (300
  texts), with about 116 special texts: 416 in all. `lib_read_lines_big`'s fixture is `big.txt`.

**Lead decisions of W8** (written 2026-11-04 with the text of §2.16, sub-phase W8a, revised after one
independent review, and agreed by the user with the text and Decisions 158–160 on 2026-11-04); each
is a reading taken because one answer is
clearly right, written into §2.16:

* **L-nf** (integers only) The sketch, its header and the simulator use no floating-point type and
  only integer arithmetic with truncating division (`tdiv`), every value far inside `int64_t`
  (the largest product, v·v in µm/s, is about 10¹⁵): the log then depends on no compiler, flag or
  library, and the sketch computes on the ESP32 exactly what it computes on the Mac. `make w8-log`
  checks the absence of `float` and `double` with `grep -w`, the absence of decimal floating
  literals (after comments and string and character literals are stripped, nothing matches
  `[0-9]\.[0-9]|[0-9][eE][+-]?[0-9]`, hexadecimal literals excluded), builds both simulators with
  `-Wfloat-conversion -Wdouble-promotion -Werror`, and runs an `-O0` build with the
  undefined-behaviour and address sanitizers beside the `-O2` build.
* **L-ng** (the bus) The simulated bus charges every frame its exact length with stuff bits and
  CRC-15 (§2.16.3) and arbitrates by identifier, so frame times, bus load and arbitration delays are
  real; the analysis computes the same lengths from the logged bytes (A3), which exercises the
  bitwise functions on every frame and checks the simulator through `bus_overlaps`. Timestamps are
  end-of-frame times, as a receiver sees them.
* **L-nh** (the TWAI API) The sketch uses the polled `driver/twai.h` (install, start, transmit and
  receive with zero wait), which the core 3.3.7 ships for the plain ESP32 beside the newer callback
  driver; the mock declares exactly the types, macros and four functions of §2.16.5 with the core's
  signatures and field order, so a use of anything else fails to compile on the host. The core's
  types header notes that the legacy types remain until IDF 6.0; a future core without them would
  need a new sketch API, a change agreed then.
* **L-ni** (the mode strap) GPIO 25 with the internal pull-up: open (a bare board) is the bench mode,
  grounded (the car) the car mode; the mock reads it `LOW` unless `--bench`. A bare board can
  therefore never send torque commands with `Enable` = 1 (it stays `INIT` without feedback).
* **L-nj** (the event loop) The simulator calls `loop()` every 50 µs of simulated time and processes
  events at equal times in a fixed order (model tick, model frames, bus, sketch); a received frame is
  handled at most 50 µs after its end, and the control step starts exactly at its 10 ms boundary.
* **L-nk** (timestamps) The car log's time base is T0 = 1 793 750 400 s (2026-11-04 00:00:00 UTC), so
  its lines look like a real `candump -L` log; the analysis splits a timestamp at `.` and parses two
  integers, so every time is an exact integer microsecond (about 1.8·10¹⁵, below 2⁵³, so MATLAB's
  doubles hold it exactly), and `parse_f64` is not used.
* **L-nl** (exact analysis) Every key is an integer computed exactly or a fixed short sequence of
  IEEE operations (divisions, multiplications by constants, `sqrt`) on exact integers in the order
  A1–A11 state, every sum below 2⁵³ (the largest, se, sxx
  and sxy of A9, stay below 10¹⁴): MATLAB and Sea agree bit for bit, the outputs are class E, and the
  rules are `exact` or 1e-15 relative.
* **L-nm** (the port's data layout) Parallel arrays and an n × 8 `i64` byte matrix instead of an
  array of structs with an array field (85 621 heap arrays); preallocation and slices instead of
  append; `tdiv` written with `idiv`; `i64` sums.
* **L-nn** (the timed region) Reading and decoding the log is the workload's main work, so the
  compute time of both the script and the port runs from before reading the file to after the
  analysis, the report and the figure outside it, as in W1–W7.
* **L-no** (other logs) `--log PATH` lets the port analyse a bench or hardware log; lines not starting
  with `(` (banner, boot messages) are skipped and counted, and the empty-set conventions of A2, A8
  and A9 keep a log without feedback frames from failing. A capture from a real board must start at
  the banner line (the ROM boot output before it trimmed by the user, §2.16.7), so that A1 stays
  strict: a malformed frame line is still an error. Acceptance uses neither.
* **L-np** (one message table in code) `w8_can_msgs.h` beside the sketch holds the identifiers,
  layouts and pack/unpack helpers, used by the sketch and by the model; a layout defect would then be
  shared by both, but the MATLAB script and the port decode the log independently from §2.16.3, so it
  cannot pass unnoticed.
* **L-nq** (numbers computed for this text) The log size, the fault counts of the generator, the
  bench line count, the checksums, CRCs and stuff counts of the worked examples, and T0 were computed
  with throwaway scripts (`uv run --no-project python`) from the definitions written here; W8b's
  outputs must agree with them, and a disagreement is a defect of W8b or of this text, decided before
  the log is committed.
* **L-nr** (the law in the log) The VCU sends every input and output of its law in the frames of one
  step, matched by the shared counter (A6), so the analysis recomputes the law by hand from the log;
  the four `law_*_mismatch` keys and `cycle_mismatch` are part of acceptance and are 0.
* **L-ns** (no reference line) Sea has `xline` but no `yline` (LANGUAGE.md §12.3); the figure needs
  neither (the fit in panel 1 is a two-point line), so no library change is asked for.
* **L-nt** (response delay) The delay is the dead time ℓ (0–50 ms in 1 ms steps) that minimizes the
  summed absolute difference between the measured torque and the command held from ℓ earlier: an
  integer search with an exact first minimum, robust to the rate limiter and to derating, which
  defeat a step-response definition.
* **L-nu** (faults and their definitions) Drops, late frames and corrupt checksums at 0.2 %, 0.2 %
  and 0.1 % of the feedback frames, a 120 ms blackout of MCU R and a 300 ms open pedal track give
  every analysis a few dozen real events, two of them causing VCU faults; a drop is seen as a
  counter step above 1 modulo 16 (the blackout's 12 frames stay below 16), a late frame as a counter
  step of 1 after more than 12 ms (a late frame is at least 13 ms after its predecessor, bus jitter
  under 1 ms), and every interval above 12 ms is a gap event plotted in panel 2.
* **L-nv** (files) The sketch folder holds only the sketch and its header, because `arduino-cli`
  compiles every source file of a sketch folder; the folder name equals the sketch name, as the
  flash script requires.
* **L-nw** (portability) The rules of §2.16.4 (fixed-width types, no `long`, `uint32_t` clock
  arithmetic, declarations before use, no designated initializer of `twai_message_t`) are what makes
  "unmodified on both" hold between the ESP32's 32-bit and the Mac's 64-bit `long` and without
  Arduino's prototype generation on the host. For the same reason no `clamp(T, T, T)`-style
  template (`std::clamp`, `std::min`, `std::max`) is called with mixed `int32_t` and `int`
  arguments or literals: `int32_t` is `int` on one target and `long` on the other, so such a call
  deduces on one and fails on the other; the sketch uses the non-template `w8_clamp32` and
  `w8_clamp64` of `w8_can_msgs.h`, and formats use `PRIu32`/`PRIX32`, never `%lu`.
* **L-nx** (outside `make test`) `make w8-log`, `make w8-log-update` and `make w8-sketch` are
  developer targets, run in W8b and whenever the sketch or the simulator changes; `make test` and
  `make cross` read only the committed files.
* **L-ny** (the model's scope) The model is the least that gives the analysis real dynamics: first
  order motor torque with power and speed limits, longitudinal motion with rolling and aerodynamic
  drag and no reversing, and a first-order yaw rate with understeer and the torque-difference yaw
  moment; no tyre slip, battery, temperature or lateral velocity state. Its parameters are invented.
* **L-nz** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (a failed start) A failed TWAI install or start prints only
  `# twai start failed`, with no banner, and `loop()` returns at once; "Then it prints the banner"
  is the success path.
* **L-oa** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (the car-mode replies) In car mode the sketch ignores extended-identifier
  frames; it prints an `0x381`/`0x382` reply only for a data frame with DLC 6, once per motor; it
  builds the 32-bit serial from two `w8_get_u16le` reads, because the header has no 32-bit getter.
* **L-ob** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (no constants in the header) `w8_can_msgs.h` holds no firmware or
  serial constants, because §2.16.3's API list is exhaustive; the model defines L 0x0213 /
  0x4C0A1001 and R 0x0212 / 0x4C0A1002 from §2.16.3's table.
* **L-oc** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (`delay`) `delay()`/`delayMicroseconds()` first run step (5) at the
  current time, then steps (1)–(3) and (5) of every event up to the target, without `loop()`. Loop
  times passed meanwhile are skipped, and the next `loop()` is at the first loop time after the
  target. The sketch never calls `delay`.
* **L-od** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (blackout draws) A blackout frame whose fault draw u is 2 or 3 also
  makes the second `S_BUS` draw ("the draws are made and discarded"). None of the 12 blackout frames
  draws 2 or 3 (their u are 316, 757, 343, 691, 415, 309, 217, 842, 267, 166, 821, 493), so the log
  does not depend on this.
* **L-oe** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (TWAI errors) A second `twai_driver_install` or `twai_start` returns
  `ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE`; a null config pointer returns `ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG`; frames that end
  before `twai_start` are not queued for the VCU; `twai_receive` returns only `ESP_OK` or
  `ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT`.
* **L-of** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (the mock's header) The mock's `TWAI_GENERAL_CONFIG_DEFAULT` writes
  `TWAI_ALERT_NONE` (0) and `ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1` (1<<1) inline, without declaring those names;
  `gpio_num_t` has the fixed underlying type `int`, so `TWAI_IO_UNUSED` (−1) is valid;
  `twai_clock_source_t` has only `TWAI_CLK_SRC_DEFAULT` = 4.
* **L-og** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (queues and stderr) A full model transmit queue stops `w8sim` with
  exit 2 (it cannot happen); frames lost at the VCU's receive queue are reported on stderr, and
  `make w8-log` and `make w8-log-update` fail on any stderr output; `--seconds` accepts 1 … 999 999.
* **L-oh** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (`w8-log-update`) `make w8-log-update` requires the float checks to
  pass and the `-O2` and sanitizer builds to give identical outputs, then replaces the three
  committed files together (copies first, then moves), so a failure never leaves them mixed.
* **L-oi** (W8b, 2026-11-04) (`TWAI_MODE_NORMAL`) `TWAI_MODE_NORMAL` without an acknowledging node
  is not modelled (no retransmission); the mock records the mode and does not act on it, since the
  bench uses `TWAI_MODE_NO_ACK`.
* **L-oj** (W8c, 2026-11-04) (A6 prevL/prevR) The previous commands of a cycle are the `TorqueCmd`
  of the `0x101` (`0x102`) frame immediately before the cycle's matched frame in log order, among
  all frames of that identifier, whether or not that frame was matched; 0 for the first.
* **L-ok** (W8c, 2026-11-04) (state) The State in A6 steps 6 and 8 and "in `RUN`" in A9 is the
  cycle's `0x120` 2-bit `State` field.
* **L-ol** (W8c, 2026-11-04) (counting) `law_rdes_mismatch` counts a cycle once when `YawRateDes`
  or `YawLimit` disagrees; `law_cmd_mismatch` counts it once when either command disagrees.
* **L-om** (W8c, 2026-11-04) (A8 validity) Every A8 feedback quantity (`torque_act_max`,
  `speed_max_rpm`, `current_max_A`, `derate_frames`, `cmd_timeout_frames`) uses checksum-valid
  frames only; "valid" means a valid checksum, with no separate DLC-8 condition. `torque_cmd_max`
  uses every command frame.
* **L-on** (W8c, 2026-11-04) (edge cases) A log with no frame lines is an error; W = 0 gives
  `bus_load_win` = [], `bus_load_max` 0 and `bus_load_max_win` 0; span = 0 gives `bus_load` NaN; a
  checksummed data frame with 0 data bytes counts as failing its checksum; a frame too short for a
  signal that the analysis reads from it stops the program with an error naming the line; `iface`
  is "" with no frames; `v_max` is 0 with no `0x120` frame; A10 counts a remote frame as answered
  by the first data frame of that identifier before the next remote frame of that identifier. None
  of these arises in the committed log.
* **L-oo** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (fixture lines) A fixture line is exactly `// fixture: PATH` in the
  port's leading comment block (its first lines starting with `//`). PATH is components of
  `[A-Za-z0-9._+-]` separated by single `/`, with no `.` or `..` component and no leading `/`. Any
  header line matching `//`, blanks, `fixture`, blanks, `:` that does not fit is malformed (a setup
  error). `accept.sh` checks every selected port's fixtures before building any port.
* **L-op** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (scratch ports) `tests/accept.sh` and `tests/cross_pack.sh` take a
  `PORTS` variable (default `sea/ports`) so a scratch ports directory can be tested; fixture paths
  stay relative to the `sea` directory.
* **L-oq** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (deferred ports) `cross_run.sh`'s deferred-variant check (the
  `// cross: compare=accept` ports W2 and W3) accepts no file besides `NAME.json` and
  `output/NAME.svg`, so a deferred port cannot have fixtures today. W8 is not deferred (class E,
  §2.16.11). A deferred port that needs fixtures must first extend that check to accept unchanged
  `NAME.files/` entries.
* **L-or** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (malformed lines) The port's A1 checks line by line where the script
  checks each condition over all lines in turn, so with several malformed lines the two may name
  different (each malformed) lines. Both stop with an error naming a malformed line, as §2.16.8
  requires; the committed logs have none.
* **L-os** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (character checks) Sea has no byte access, so the port checks each
  character with `substr` and string comparisons before `parse_i64` reads it (the script's digit
  tables). This keeps the script's messages naming the line. Leading zeros of the seconds are
  dropped first, so a long run of zeros cannot overflow `i64`.
* **L-ot** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (hex tokens) `compare_report.py` cannot name a map entry for a
  non-numeric reference token, so the serial `%08X` (`4C0A1001`) and the identifier `0A0` are
  compared as text, which is exact. Every numeric hex identifier is `exact`.
* **L-ou** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (firmware token) `%d.%02d` prints the firmware as one decimal token
  (`2.19`), since §6.4 splits only at `..`. One `exact` rule covers both parts, because `%02d` fixes
  the minor part's width.
* **L-ov** (W8d, 2026-11-04) (no A9 cycles) With no A9 cycles (a bench log) the port plots panel 1's
  "fit" series from two empty vectors, as MATLAB's `plot([], [])` does. This keeps the legend's
  structure and never reaches `min` of an empty vector, which is a run-time error in Sea.

**Lead decisions of phase 10** (written 2026-11-04 with the text of §2.17, sub-phase 10a, revised
after one independent review, and agreed by the user with the text and Decisions 168–172 on
2026-11-04); each is a reading taken because one answer is clearly right, written into §2.17:

* **L-ow** (no warm-up run, one measurement) Nothing runs a port between its build and run 1, so run
  1 is the first run, as MATLAB's first repetition is; best of 5 includes it (§5.7). The pass is
  decided within one final measurement; runs of different attempts are never combined.
* **L-ox** (the printed compute time) The ports print the compute time with three decimals because
  the MATLAB reports do and the reports are compared (§6.4); the check therefore compares the largest
  value the printed number can stand for, printed + 0.0005, strictly below MATLAB's best at full
  precision. This can only make the check stricter, never pass a slower run.
* **L-oy** (every timed run is correct) Run 1 of each workload is judged as acceptance judges it, and
  runs 2–15 must give the same bytes (the `Compute time` line aside), the same status and an empty
  standard error, and leave only `NAME.json` and the fixtures. Judging happens after the timed runs,
  so the `uv` processes never run between two timed runs.
* **L-oz** (scheduling) No QoS class, affinity or nice value is set for any measured process on
  either system, so every implementation runs under the same default scheduling as MATLAB did; this
  departs from Baysick BENCH.md §3.1 (which sets a QoS class and pins on Linux) for the sake of that
  equality. The drivers refuse to run niced. Because a shell started by an agent may inherit a
  lowered scheduling class that no tool can portably query, `spawn_time` records each workload
  run's user + system CPU time (`wait4`), and `report.py` flags runs whose CPU time is below 0.8 of
  their wall time as runs that waited for a CPU; a flag is reported, not a failure.
* **L-pa** (power) The baseline machine `Mac14,9` is a portable; in final mode the drivers refuse to
  measure on battery or in Low Power Mode, which lower the clock, and record the power source.
* **L-pb** (what the check accepts) Only final-mode results of a clean tree, whose summary agrees
  with its runs file: the check can then be re-run by anyone on the committed files, and the
  measured binaries are those of the recorded commit.
* **L-pc** (the machine) §1.2's comparison is valid only on the baseline's machine, so a model or CPU
  name different from the MATLAB files' is a failure of the check, not a warning.
* **L-pd** (NumPy) Timed in-process (`main()` with `perf_counter`, five runs in one interpreter, the
  module imported untimed), the committed `.py.json` protected by redirecting `common.REF_DIR`, and
  run 1 judged by `compare.py`'s own NumPy-mode function; Mac only, because the column exists to sit
  beside MATLAB's and the host has no MATLAB baseline. Five runs, as the MATLAB files hold, not 15:
  the column is not judged, and the slowest scripts make 15 runs costly. The redirection of file
  descriptor 1 and the flush before it are outside the timed region, the flush after `main()`
  inside it; `numpy.sh` writes the record, with the facts only Python knows (versions, BLAS,
  threads, the load after the last timed run) from `numpy_time.py`'s `info.txt`.
* **L-pe** (exact kernel data) Integer and dyadic data make every correct implementation's result
  identical, so validation is an equality against `expect.c`'s `int64_t` values, as Baysick's tests
  use exact products; the cost of these operations does not depend on the values.
* **L-pf** (one protocol for all implementations) Each implementation is an executable with the same
  arguments and output, timed by itself around the calls, one process per repetition, with the same
  calibration and batching, so Sea and the vendor are measured identically; a Sea program cannot
  time a repetition loop of the runner's choosing any other way.
* **L-pg** (no hoisting) A loop-invariant `a @ b` could in principle be moved out of the timed loop,
  and the fused `axpby` allocates nothing per call, so an allocation count proves nothing for it.
  Instead every implementation changes one input by the call number's parity before each call, so
  no call is loop-invariant and the checked result is the last call's (exactly checkable for both
  parities), and a batched call may not be more than twice as fast as a single one (Decision 171
  (a)). The Sea programs' text is fixed in §2.17.6 so the guard's premises cannot drift.
* **L-ph** (vendor calls) `cblas_dgemm` with β = 0 into a preallocated matrix; `dgesv_` with its
  copies inside the timed call, because `solve` must also not change its arguments; `vDSP_vsmsmaD`
  as Accelerate's one-pass out-of-place a·x + b·y, and on Linux `cblas_dcopy` + `cblas_daxpby` as a
  labelled two-pass proxy, since OpenBLAS has no out-of-place form (Baysick BENCH.md §2 labels its
  `add` proxy the same way).
* **L-pi** (no peak loops) The Sea-level benchmarks measure the language over the kernels; GEMM's
  quality against the instruction-set peak is Baysick's measurement (Baysick BENCH.md §3.4), and
  Decision 162 chose a small set over a full suite.
* **L-pj** (micro-benchmarks re-measured) The compiler changed after 5d (phases 6–9, L, W8), so the
  micro-benchmarks are re-measured at the measured commit, with the current compiler and C only; the
  5d files stay as the record of phase 5.
* **L-pk** (kept attempts) A failed measurement is committed and then moved to
  `bench/results/p10-attempt-K/`, so the record shows every attempt and `BENCH.md` §10 lists them.
* **L-pl** (order) On the Mac everything is built first, then the workloads (the pass rule) are
  measured, then the kernels, the micro-benchmarks and NumPy (the longest), each after its own start
  condition (Decision 170 (a)), so no build and no previous tool's heat precedes a measurement
  without a cool-down; the Linux run follows the Mac measurement so its `ssh` traffic never overlaps
  a Mac measurement.
* **L-pm** (Linux) The ports are compiled on the Mac and linked on the host as the cross tests do;
  workloads and Sea kernels run under both x86_64 variants; run 1 of each is judged on the Mac with
  the same `compare.py` and `compare_report.py` commands (the host need not have `uv`); no compile
  time is reported for Linux.
* **L-pn** (generated tables) Every number in `BENCH.md` §2 and §4–§8 comes from `report.py`, and
  the lead checks that by re-running it; no measured number is typed by hand.
* **L-po** (load) Under Decision 170 (a) a driver measures only after the cool-down and once the
  1-minute load average is at most 2.0, and stops with exit 2 when that does not happen within 15
  minutes; the final measurement's agent then reports instead of retrying, so the user can make the
  machine idle. The wait and the loads before and after every driver are recorded, and `check.py`
  warns (never fails) when the workloads' load exceeded 2.0.
* **L-pp** (no re-measurement after 10d) The version is a string in the POSIX-sh driver only; the
  compiled programs do not contain it, so 10d changes no measured binary.
* **L-pq** (Python tools) `check.py` and `report.py` read JSON and TSV; Python's standard library does
  that reliably where sh and awk would not, and `uv` is already required by acceptance. They never
  import NumPy.
* **L-pr** (§5.7's kernel list) §5.7 lists Sea's own kernels (GEMV, LU, Cholesky, triangular solve,
  sort, the vector elementary functions) as measured "this way"; under Decision 162 (a) phase 10
  measures the three Sea-level benchmarks of §2.17.6 instead, which run GEMM, LU with its triangular
  solves, and a fused vector loop through the language, in §2.17.9's TSV format rather than
  Baysick's and against the vendor library only, with no instruction-set peak (L-pi). With the
  agreement §5.7 says so (§2.17.14).
* **L-ps** (one session) `make bench` creates a session id that every record carries; a final-mode
  driver never replaces a result file and `session.sh` needs an empty directory, and `check.py`
  requires one session and one `sea_commit` across every record present, so the committed results
  are one measurement and cannot mix runs of different sessions or commits.
* **L-pt** (C call barrier) Each timed C call goes through a `noinline` function ending in `asm
  volatile("" ::: "memory")`, so `-O2` can neither inline it into the timing loop nor hoist or merge
  identical calls; with the per-call input change of L-pg this makes the C and the Sea loops do the
  same work.
* **L-pu** (build, then measure) Separate `build` and `measure` commands, with `measure` refusing stale
  or missing builds, keep every compiler and linker out of the measured interval and give the start
  condition a machine that is no longer building; the cross remote script follows the same order on
  the host.
* **L-pv** (the printed wall) Walls are written with nine decimals, so the check compares the best
  wall + 5·10⁻¹⁰ strictly, as L-ox does for the compute time; the summary's medians of 10 carry one
  decimal more and are recomputed exactly in decimal.
* **L-pw** (cross outputs) On Linux, W2 and W3 (class R) are judged by `compare.py`'s rules only, as
  `make cross` defers and judges them; W1, W4, W5, W7 and W8 must also give the Mac's bytes (the
  `Compute time` line aside), which `make cross` already guarantees, so a host run that differs is
  wrong even if it passes the rules.
* **L-px** (NumPy pinned) The NumPy column names its version, so the version is pinned
  (`numpy==2.5.4`, the release `uv` resolves today) rather than whatever `uv` picks on the day of the
  measurement; the run-1 check confirms it reproduces the cross-check's outputs.
* **L-py** (clean trees) Cleanliness excludes `bench/results`, which the measurement itself writes,
  and is checked from the driver's own root; Baysick's tree is recorded and required clean too
  (outside its `sea` submodule path), because its runtime is linked into every measured binary.
* **L-pz** (overrides) `PORTS` and `KERNELS` let 10b inject failing programs without touching the
  tree, as `tests/accept.sh`'s `PORTS` does; final mode accepts only their defaults, so a final
  result always measures the committed programs.
* **L-qa** (fixed program texts) The three Sea programs are written verbatim in §2.17.6, so their
  input change, check computation and output format are part of the agreed text; a text the
  compiler rejects is corrected in the document with the lead, never silently in `bench/`.

Added in 10b (2026-11-04): the readings the 10b tools took where the agreed text left a detail
open, written into §2.17 where it says "as built in 10b"; the lead confirms them with the 10b
verification before committing:

* **L-qb** (the machine line's baseline) `check.py` prints the distinct models and CPUs of the
  MATLAB files joined by `/`, so a mismatch inside the baseline itself is visible on the line
  instead of being hidden behind one file's values (§2.17.8).
* **L-qc** (reading a load average) The 1-minute load is the first number of the recorded field,
  so the record's exact spacing and separators never make the check fail (§2.17.8).
* **L-qd** (report headings) `report.py` prints BENCH.md's section numbers and titles with `###`
  subsections, so 10c pastes the output unchanged (§2.17.9).
* **L-qe** (micro precision) The micro tables print times to 3 decimals and rates as `%.2f`, the
  formats of every other generated table (§2.17.9).
* **L-qf** (a bare README table) `report.py --readme` prints no heading, so the README keeps its
  own heading levels (§2.17.9).
* **L-qg** (micro variants) The micro record's `variants` is `none`: the micro-benchmarks call no
  kernel, and every record keeps the same fields (§2.17.7).
* **L-qh** (micro loads) The micro record writes the loads as the other records do, three numbers
  separated by single spaces (§2.17.7).
* **L-qi** (micro `--out`) A relative `--out` is taken from the Sea repository, as `BENCH_OUT` is,
  so `make` and a direct call write to the same directory (§2.17.7).
* **L-qj** (micro rules in final mode) Final mode forces §5.9's 1.0 s and 5 repetitions whatever
  the environment holds, so an exported quick setting can never shorten a final measurement
  (§2.17.7).
* **L-qk** (the micro cross stamp) `micro.sh --current --cross` builds and measures in one call, so
  it compares the stamp taken before the remote run with the one taken after it instead of a
  `stamp.txt` from an earlier `build` (§2.17.3, C1).
* **L-ql** (marker placement) The attempt marker is made after the checks that need no
  measurement and just before the first step that measures or could leave a partial result: for
  workloads `--cross` after the bundle is packed, for micro `--cross` before the compile (§2.17.3,
  C2).
* **L-qm** (nice in quick mode) Nice 0 is required in final mode only; the nice value is recorded
  in both modes, so a quick trial may run niced without blocking development (§2.17.3).
* **L-qn** (check order) The output-file, session and mode checks run before the preconditions,
  so a mistaken invocation is refused before anything is built or measured (§2.17.4).
* **L-qo** (build without a session) `workloads.sh build` needs no session: it depends only on the
  trees, which its stamp records (§2.17.4).
* **L-qp** (`ports.txt`) The build records its resolved ports directory, and `measure` refuses
  binaries built from another one, so an injected `PORTS` can never be measured as the committed
  ports (§2.17.4).
* **L-qq** (the mirror refusal) `workloads.sh` and `numpy.sh` also refuse a final-mode run into a
  quick session's directory, so a final measurement is never mixed with quick records; C3 itself
  requires only the quick-into-final refusal, and `kernels.sh` and `micro.sh` do not add the
  mirror (§2.17.3, C3).
* **L-qr** (the OpenBLAS header) `kernels.sh --cross` probes the include directory with
  `pkg-config` and then the Debian/Ubuntu paths, and accepts a directory only when the vendor
  harness's `config` line confirms `openblas_get_config`, so a wrong header is never linked
  silently (§2.17.6).
* **L-qs** (minimum of three) The reference time is the minimum of three validated runs, the
  least disturbed estimate of one call's cost (§2.17.6).
* **L-qt** (the reference batch) The kernel calibration times a batch of b ≥ 2 calls, growing ×4
  until it lasts 10 µs, instead of one call, because one call is below the macOS clock's tick and
  carries the first-call cost; the guard then allows a factor of 2 against that reference
  (§2.17.6).
* **L-qu** (starting the final run) The final run is started in the foreground or through
  `/bin/sh -c '… &'`, because zsh's `BG_NICE` gives a background job nice 5 and final mode
  refuses it (§2.17.3).
